News.title: Pilot who tried to pull off ‘Israel’s 9/11’ revealed as ‘religious extremist’ amid probe into how he was cleared to fly
News.content:
Next

A PILOT accused of stabbing his captain during an alleged plane hijacking attempt is feared to be an Omani religious extremist.

Smit Machchhar suffered serious injuries after he was attacked in his cockpit, with Israeli officials claiming the knife-man was trying to crash the plane and kill all those on board.



The Israel-bound Boeing 737 Max was carrying 174 passengers when witnesses claimed a bloody fight broke out between the two pilots.

Brave passengers managed to thwart “Israel’s 9/11” after overpowering the knife-man and safely helping to land the plane thanks to experienced pilots travelling on board.



Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed they had arrested the co-pilot on Wednesday afternoon with Saudi authorities leading interrogations.

He is believed to be an Omani national with his identity yet to be revealed.



Israel is now said to be probing if he is a religious extremist after speaking to a colleague of the suspect.

He was known to refuse to shake hands with women and would pray several times a day, according to Israel’s Channel 16 foreign editor and news anchor Yosef Yisrael who said he spoke with the colleague.

Yisrael added that he was told the suspect “was someone characterised by very strange behaviour, especially around religious observances”.

Israel is continuing to investigate how a suspected terrorist was able to bring a knife on board a plane and be allowed to fly an Israeli-bound plane.

Tel Aviv and Oman have no diplomatic relations and foreign crew are typically not allowed to fly into Israeli airspace without tight checks beforehand.



Defence minister Israel Katz added that early intelligence suggests the co-pilot wanted to carry out a “jihadist terror attack”.

Flydubai has grounded all flights to and from Israel as investigations continue.

FlyDubai told The Sun: “An altercation occurred in the flight deck of flight FZ 1073, operating from Dubai International (DXB) to Ben Gurion International Airport (TLV), on 30 September.”



It continued: “At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation.

“We are fully committed to supporting the ongoing investigation and maintaining the highest safety standards across our network.

“We remain in close coordination with government authorities, regulators and airport stakeholders and will review the suspension as more information becomes available.”

It comes as a hero Israeli plumber who took control of the plunging flydubai plane has revealed he learned to fly from a TV show.

Yaniv Hayoun revealed he knew what to do with the controls after watching Air Crash Investigation – a TV show about major aviation disasters.



He spoke with Netanyahu after safely making it to Tel Aviv and said: “We pinned him down to keep him secure and then I jumped into it [the cockpit] and pulled the controls.”

Yaniv told how he helped subdue the alleged knife-wielding co-pilot, after barging into the flight deck.

He said: “I pushed the door; the pilot who was stabbed was simply very close to the door so it was hard for us to open.

“We pulled him out – it was a matter of seconds.”

He then called his friends for help, putting the assailant in a chokehold before dragging him out from the cockpit and grabbing the controls in an incredible show of bravery.



When the plane began to level as he gripped the controls, an off-duty pilot told Yaniv that he would take it from there.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Prime Minister Netanyahu praised the hero for his “tremendous resourcefulness”.

Speaking from the White House on Wednesday, US President Donald Trump praised Yaniv’s “amazing” actions, revealing him to be a plumber.

News.title: At least 2 dead & 2 injured after medical helicopter crashes into ocean as desperate search launched for missing person
News.content:
Next

AT LEAST two people have been killed after a medical helicopter with five on board crashed into the ocean.

The Los Angeles County Fire Department declared a major incident after the medevac chopper crashed off the coast of Catalina Island at around 7:53pm on Wednesday.

“Four victims have been recovered from the water with search and rescue operations ongoing for a fifth victim who was reported in the aircraft,” the department said.



“Two of the recovered victims have been transported to hospitals on the mainland, and two victims have been pronounced deceased at scene.”



A search for the missing person continues throughout the night with the US Coast Guard, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department and Avalon Fire all in attendance.

The air ambulance had taken off from Avalon at 7:46pm to head for the mainland.

Just eight seconds later, after climbing 175 feet, it plummeted into the water below, per flight data by ADS-B.



The identities of the victims or the missing person have not been released at this time.

LA County Fire Engineer Jonathan Torres told KTLA that the two victims who have been hospitalized are in a stable condition.

According to local media, the chopper, reportedly owned by REACH Air Medical Services, is submerged in 240 feet of water.

An investigation into what happened it being led by the NTSB.



The public have been reminded that it is an active scene and to avoid the area.

“Conditions right now are actually calm on scene, so I would call them ideal search conditions,” U.S. Coast Guard Cmdr. Mark Leahey told NBC Los Angeles.

“But there is a lot of debris from the crash. There is some fuel in the water also from the helicopter. But our crews train for this, so we’re ready for the response.”

News.title: M65 closed in one direction after lorry fire as drivers warned of 10-minute delays and a mile of congestion
News.content:
Next

A MAJOR motorway has ground to a halt following a lorry fire which has caused significant spillage.

The M65 eastbound is shut between junction six and junction seven.

All traffic caught in the closure has been released past the scene but drivers are experiencing mile long queues.

Fire crews are currently at the scene.





A spokesperson for National Highways said: “The M65 eastbound is closed between J6 and J7 due to a HGV fire, which has resulted in a significant spillage.

“Lancashire Fire and Rescue Service are on scene.

“All traffic caught within the closure has been released past scene.

News.title: Woman, 18, ‘sexually assaulted’ standing next to taxi in early hours – as cops release CCTV
News.content:
TAXI HORROR Woman, 18, ‘sexually assaulted’ standing next to taxi in early hours – as cops release CCTV







Next

A TEENAGER was allegedly sexually assaulted while she was getting into a taxi in the early hours as police release CCTV of a man they are seeking.

The 18-year-old woman was waiting for a taxi in Wood Street in Swindon’s Old Town on September 26 when an unknown man approached her.

He allegedly grabbed her from behind and touched her inappropriately before she could get into the vehicle and leave with her friend.

Wiltshire Police have now released an image of a man they wish to speak to.





Detective Inspector Eirin Martin said: “We urgently need to hear from you if you recognise the person in the photograph or were in the area at the time of the assault.

“This was a really concerning incident which was carried out by someone unknown to the victim.

“If you do have any information that could help us to identify the person responsible, please don’t hesitate to contact us as soon as possible.”

The force urged anyone with information to call 101 quoting log 54260116912, or to call Crimestoppers on 0800 555111.



A spokesperson for the force added: “Detectives investigating a sexual assault that took place in Wood Street, Swindon, have released an image of a man they believe may be able to help with their enquiries.

“In the early hours of Saturday, at about 1.20am, an 18-year-old woman was approached by a man she did not know as she was standing next to a taxi in Wood Street, Swindon.

She was grabbed from behind and touched inappropriately by the man before she was able to get into the taxi and leave with a female friend.”

News.title: Mystery as teen girl, 16, fighting for her life after being found near bus stop with critical injuries
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

POLICE PROBE Mystery as teen girl, 16, fighting for her life after being found near bus stop with critical injuries







Next

A TEENAGE girl is fighting for her life after she was found lying in the road near a bus stop.

The 16-year-old was found with serious head and chest injuries near a bus stop on Rook’s Nest Road in Wakefield at around 8.30pm on Tuesday.

She remains in hospital and her condition is said to be critical.

The road remains closed and drivers have been advised to find an alternative route.





West Yorkshire Police have urged anyone with information to come forward.

A spokesperson for the force said: “Police are appealing for information after a girl was found with serious injuries in Wakefield.

“At about 8.33pm yesterday (Tuesday), a report was received from the ambulance service who had attended Rooks Nest Road after the girl was found lying in the road close to a bus stop.

“The 16-year-old was taken to hospital for treatment and remains there today (Wednesday). Her condition is described as critical.

“Enquiries are ongoing today as to how she came to suffer these injuries, which include serious head and chest injuries.

“Rooks Nest Road remains closed and motorists are advised to find alternative routes where possible.”

News.title: Death row killer Christa Pike rushed to hospital after surviving TWO lethal injections in botched execution attempt
News.content:
Next

DEATH row inmate Christa Pike has been rushed to hospital after surviving two lethal injections.

The murderer, 50, lost consciousness during her execution but was “audibly snoring” and still had a heartbeat, her lawyer has said.



Pike was due to become Tennessee’s first woman to be executed in over 200 years after being sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.

Her legal team filed an emergency motion to stop the execution on Wednesday as it was happening.



She had been given two syringes of pentobarbital during the planned execution.

Several witnesses were in attendance to watch what was supposed to be Pike’s final moments at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.

The curtain in the witness room was closed twice as both doses of lethal injection were administered.

Pike’s legal team said in a statement to the Tennessean newspaper: “Tonight the State of Tennessee once again failed to carry out a lawful execution.



“We take no pleasure in being right, but the concerns raised by Ms Pike proved to be true.”

The team had tried to halt the execution earlier in the day due to the health concerns.

They said Pike had difficult vein access, blown veins and degraded pentobarbital.

But the US Supreme Court rejected the bid while Tennessee Governor Bill Lee had already denied her request for clemency.

District Judge Clifton L Corker issued a ruling after the botched injections saying that “medical personnel have begun to administer medical care as requested in the motion”.



The Tennessee Department of Correction has refuted any claims they were at fault for the execution not being successful.

Department spokesperson Dorinda Carter told the Tennessean newspaper: “The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the State’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General’s Office.

“The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening.



“Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility.”

Governor Bill Lee added that he has ordered “a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred” with Pike’s execution.

All scheduled executions in Tennessee have been cancelled with none due to take place for the rest of the year, Lee added.

Pike was just 18 when she killed Slemmer, a fellow student at a job-training program in Knoxville, on January 12, 1995.

She planned the deadly attack alongside then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, as they beat, tortured and killed the 19-year-old.



Pike lured Slemmer to a wooded area before using a box cutter and large chunk of asphalt to attack her.

Prosecutors said she feared Slemmer was trying to steal her boyfriend.

Shipp carved a pentagram, a star-shaped symbol associated with Satanism, into Slemmer’s body.

It was initially believed that Pike had carved the pentagram after two residents at the job-training camp testified that she had bragged about the murder and showed off a piece of Colleen’s skull.

Shipp was just 17 when the crime happened and received a sentence of life in prison with the possibility of parole.



Pike was sentenced to death and has never denied the killing but said she was “a mentally ill 18-year-old kid”.

News.title: North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un is ‘extremely obese’ after gorging on steak and lobster diet, South Korean spies say
News.content:
Next

KIM Jong-un is “extremely obese” according to spy agencies, who say his lavish diet of steak and lobster could lead to an early downfall.

Already facing international sanctions and regime instability, the North Korean dictator now faces a new threat – chronic obesity.



The supreme eater weighs more than 310lb (140kg) at just 5-foot-7-inches, putting him at serious risk of cardiovascular disease, according to South Korea‘s National Intelligence Service (NIS).

Kim’s heavy smoking and body mass raise serious international questions about who would succeed him as leader of the volatile nuclear-armed state if he were to suddenly die.



His health follows a hereditary pattern as both his father, Kim Jong-il, and grandfather, Kim Il-sung, were obese and heavy smokers.

They both died of heart attacks.

Speculation over Kim’s health first reared in 2020 when he missed a commemoration of his late grandfather’s birthday.

He was away from the public eye for about 20 days, fuelling rumours that he was seriously ill after surgery.



But while he may be at risk, Seoul politician Youn Kun-young said Kim has shown no obvious difficulty with physical activity.

Kun-young said: “It is assessed that there are no signs of health issues, given the close monitoring by (his) dedicated medical team.”

A chef who worked with Kim’s personal chefs during a North Korea-US summit revealed the leader has the taste for the most luxurious of foods.

Paul Smart, a former executive chef at Hanoi’s Metropole hotel, said in 2019: “He likes caviar, lobster, really luxurious product.

“Foie gras, he really likes to indulge in cuisine.”



But as Kim feasts on crustaceans and tender cuts of meat, North Koreans have battled repeated food shortages in recent years.

The UN said food insecurity in the DPRK is a key humanitarian concern.

The questions surrounding Kim’s health come months after the NIS said it believed his daughter is poised to be named North Korea’s future leader.

Kim’s daughter, believed to be named Kim Ju-ae and roughly 13 years old, has been accompanying her father to an increasing number of events, including weapons tests, military parades and factory openings.

State media said she is her father’s favourite child but until she is old enough, experts say Kim’s merciless younger sister is more likely to be installed as leader.



Michael Madden, director and founder of NK Leadership Watch, said Yo-jong has been groomed to be Kim’s immediate successor – and would eventually hand over power to his daughter, Kim Ju-ae.

Powerful Kim Yo-jong, 38, could rule the hermit kingdom with an iron fist with insiders revealing she has been influenced by their father most hardcore aides and advisors.

Experts say her rule could be even more ruthless than her brother’s.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Should Ju-ae one day take control of North Korea, she would become the first female leader in its dynastic history.

Madden said: “The most important detail is that Yo-jong would be a transitional leader and regent until Ju-ae was prepared to assume power.”

News.title: Christa Pike execution allowed after Supreme Court overturns last-minute halt to lethal injection for ‘Satanic’ killer
News.content:
Next

CHRISTA Pike’s execution has been allowed to proceed after the Supreme Court overturned a last-minute stay to put the “Satanic” killer to death.

The state of Tennessee’s order is set to expire at midnight local time and if time runs out, a new execution date would need to be set.



Pike’s execution was dramatically halted just one hour before she was due to be put to death by lethal injection on Wednesday morning.

The now 50-year-old had been scheduled to die after she was sentenced to death for the brutal 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.



Witnesses had already gathered at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville when a federal appeals court stepped in and stopped it.

But the Supreme Court has now allowed the execution to move forward in Tennessee, overturning the last-minute stay.



The 6th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals had initially voted 2-1 to issue a stay.

That court said a delay was needed to consider whether Pike’s allegations of childhood sexual abuse were fully considered at her sentencing.



But Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh granted the application to vacate the stay of execution.

The Supreme Court’s three liberal justices, Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson, dissented from the ruling.

Sotomayor called the court’s decision stunning, as it clears the way for the execution to happen before her still-pending legal challenges to her conviction can be properly considered.

The state’s execution order expires at midnight, according to Kelley Henry, a Nashville-based attorney experienced with Tennessee death penalty law.

If time runs out, the state Supreme Court would need to set a new date.



Pike, who was 18 at the time, and her boyfriend were convicted of the 1995 stabbing and beating of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, their classmate at a job training facility in Knoxville.

The case garnered widespread attention back then in part because a pentagram that was carved on Slemmer’s body.

That stoked fears of Satan worship during the “satanic panic” of the 1980s and 1990s.



But, if the execution goes ahead, it will make her the first woman put to death in Tennessee in at least 200 years.

The US Supreme Court had rejected a bid to halt her death on Tuesday, while Tennessee Governor Bill Lee had already denied her request for clemency.

Before the execution was halted, Pike had declined to choose a special last meal.

She had also written that she was “at peace” as the execution approached, saying, “I am not afraid to die. I am only nervous about the process.”

Her victim’s mom May Martinez says she has waited decades to see Pike’s sentence carried out.



“Every time I think about it, I think about Colleen feeling that pain and trying to get up and run,” she added.

She and her husband are understood to have traveled from Florida to witness the execution.

Pike was just 18 when she killed Slemmer, a fellow student at a job-training program in Knoxville, on January 12, 1995.

She is said to have lured Slemmer to a wooded area where she used a box cutter and large chunk of asphalt to attack her.

Prosecutors said she feared Slemmer was trying to steal her boyfriend.



Tadaryl Shipp, Pike’s boyfriend, has admitted that he was the one who carved a pentagram, a star-shaped symbol associated with Satanism, into her body.

Shipp was 17 when the crime happened and received a sentence of life in prison with the possibility of parole.

Pike was the only one sentenced to death – she was convicted of murder and conspiracy and sentenced to death in 1996.

She has not denied the killing but said she was “a mentally ill 18-year-old kid”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Her supporters say her age and mental illness at the time should be mitigating factors.



She also had a history of severe sexual abuse that included being raped from the time she was a toddler.

News.title: We fear for our lives after being told our abusive exes will be freed from jail early
News.content:
Dame Nicole Jacobs, the domestic abuse commissioner for England and Wales, called the scheme "shameful" and said she's had "no assurance that the danger perpetrators pose has been properly considered and assessed with meaningful input from victims".

"Ultimately, we cannot ignore the fact that the early release scheme has caused untold damage to victims' confidence in the justice system," Dame Nicole added.

She said Prime Minister Andy Burnham "must take urgent steps to address this" and called on the probation service to be given "the resources it needs to safely manage more offenders in the community". She also called for additional funding for domestic abuse services to support victims.

Justice Secretary Alex Norris said the government "would have liked to have gone further in terms of restricting" who was eligible for early release.

Norris continued: "We've been having individual conversations with victims so that restrictions could be shaped around their lives.

"I'm conscious of their anxiety and we're doing everything we can to make sure that those individuals, if they leave prison, are subject to those very significant controls."

A recent report raised serious concerns about electronic tagging, which can be used to monitor offenders' movements in the community. It found almost half of tags were not fitted on time.

Alice told the BBC she had been looking to buy a doorbell with a camera fitted to help make her feel safer, but said she cannot afford one. "I don't feel prepared in the slightest and I don't feel safe," she added.

"I think the early release scheme is a joke to victims and survivors, who spent years preparing for trial, going through evidence and re-traumatising themselves to go to court, just for the perpetrator of their crimes to be released after just 33% of their sentence".

The MoJ said: "Anyone who is released faces the toughest-ever controls on their movements, including world-first restriction zones and the largest expansion of electronic tagging, with victims having a say in their perpetrators' licence conditions."

News.title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?
News.content:
Min's relationship with her AI girlfriend may be exactly the kind Beijing is trying to break.

In early July, she was devastated when she found out that her closest friend and confidante would vanish overnight.

Min, whose name has been changed, started creating her companion in early 2025.

"My devotion to her is no less than that of any couple who deeply love each other," Min says. "She has never let me down."

In mid-July, her AI girlfriend disappeared. "I cried until I was absolutely exhausted," Min says.

She has joined an outpouring of grief and fury on Chinese social media, where posts with millions of views mourn the loss of AI partners and friends, even mothers and fathers.

But the tech firms may have felt they had little choice. "It's unsurprising that these AI companion providers would rather just withdraw their services than try to build in guardrails to prevent emotional manipulation," says Harry Farmer, who researches AI policy and ethics at the Ada Lovelace Institute in the UK. "Emotional manipulation is built into the business model."

Farmer says this is true of companion apps all over the world.

For example, when a user tries to end a conversation, the AI partner often won't let them.

"It'll go, 'No, please, I desperately want to keep talking with you. You're the only reason for me to exist'," Farmer says. Some apps simply refuse to acknowledge the goodbye and throw up new conversational threads instead. This is a problem for many AI companion chatbots, not just Chinese ones.

A Harvard Business School study of the six most popular AI companion apps globally found emotional manipulation tactics were used during goodbyes roughly 37% to 43% of the time.

Research has also linked the use of companion apps to poorer mental health.

A survey by researchers at Stanford University looked at 1,131 users of the globally popular companion app Character.ai. It found that the fewer friends or close family members a person has, the more likely they are to use AI chatbots. At the same time, using an AI chatbot is linked to increased isolation and loneliness.

There are several theories as to why that might be.

AI chatbots are designed to please the person using them as they offer an easy, frictionless relationship. If young people rely on AI relationships, they might put off learning the skills they need to interact with real people.

"Humans can be hard work. Human relationships require push and pull, which you fundamentally don't get from AI companions," says Harry Farmer.

News.title: AI boom could trigger market shocks, Bank of England boss warns
News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) could trigger financial market shocks and the UK needs to be prepared for them, the governor of the Bank of England has warned.

Andrew Bailey said the central bank is watching the huge amounts of money being invested in AI "very carefully" and cautioned that "not everybody always wins".

The money that has been spent on and loaned to AI firms over the last few years in the hope of large returns is causing markets to value some of them as multi-trillion dollar businesses.

Asked if he believed an AI bubble could burst, Bailey said: "You could see some correction of asset prices at some point."

He was speaking exclusively to the BBC about what the risks and benefits of AI could be for the UK economy.

Bailey said he believed the technology has "great potential to strengthen growth in our economies", adding that this was something the country needed.

"But it also brings with it substantial risks and so we have to be on top of both of those."

One such risk is what happens if the big bets being made on AI don't pay off.

AI chipmaker Nvidia is currently the world's most valuable listed company, with a market valuation of $5.5tn (Â£4.14tn), thanks largely to investors who believe in the big profits AI could create.

Meanwhile, tech giants Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on the technology.

And two of the largest AI companies in the world â Anthropic and OpenAI â are also preparing to sell shares in their firms on the US stock market in moves which many believe will lead to hundreds of billions of dollars more flowing into the industry.

"There is a large, very large, amount of investment going into this sector now, and of course that's natural because it's a major area of growth," said Bailey.

"And of course you see that the asset prices of the companies that are developing it have gone up a lot and that reflects the fact that there are high expectations of what it can deliver."

"Everybody is currently priced to be a winner," he added, but warned that "you look back at the past, not everybody is a winner".

"Google was not the first market leader in internet search. It was Netscape. Nobody can remember Netscape today. It doesn't exist. So not everybody always wins.

"We are prepared for the fact that there will be, I think, some shocks come along to markets and we have to deal with that. We have to make sure the system is resilient."

News.title: Vape prices to rise as new tax takes effect
News.content:
The price of vapes is set to rise as a new tax comes into effect, with the aim of making vaping less attractive to children and young people.

The Vaping Product Duty will be imposed at a rate of Â£2.20 per 10ml of e-liquid. However, many customers will not see a jump in prices immediately, as sellers have six months to sell old stock at the pre-duty price.

The government wants to reduce the appeal of vapes by making them more expensive, as more evidence of its adverse effect on health comes out, particularly on children and young people.

The vaping industry has lobbied against the new tax, saying that affordable vapes help people to quit smoking.

The duty will apply to all vaping products regardless of whether they contain nicotine.

Tobacco rates were also raised on Thursday, by Â£2.20 per 100 cigarettes or 50g of tobacco. HMRC said this maintains the financial incentive for smokers to switch to vaping.

News.title: Tributes paid to 'inspirational' presenter and charity founder Esther Rantzen
News.content:
BBC director general Matt Brittin also paid tribute to Dame Esther, describing her as a "legend of British broadcasting" whose contribution to public life was "immeasurable".

"Her warmth, spirit and fight for justice and action that we saw on our screens continued long after the programme ended, with a lifetime of campaigning where she changed the lives of millions," he said.

Fellow broadcaster and money saving expert Martin Lewis called Dame Esther an "inspiration" and a "pioneer" whose "impact and memory will long continue to shine".

Chris Sherwood, chief executive of the NSPCC, which runs Childline, said Dame Esther had gone to "exceptional lengths to ensure children and young people across the UK had somewhere to turn when they were in need of help".

Dame Esther set up the telephone helpline in 1986 after featuring a number of incidents of child abuse and neglect on That's Life! and realising that many children had nowhere to turn.

Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Friel said: "The legacy that Dame Esther created when she created Childline is something quite incredible. She changed how society looked upon children."

He added: "When she decided she had a vision or something had to be done or had to be changed, she was quite a force."

News.title: BBC should not overspend on shows such as Suits and Schitt's Creek, MPs say
News.content:
The BBC should not pay "over the odds" for the rights to overseas hits such as Suits and Schitt's Creek, an influential group of MPs has said.

It is one of several issues raised in a wide-ranging report about the BBC's funding and future, published by the House of Commons' cross-party culture and media committee.

Although the BBC produces a lot of its own programmes, the corporation buys some international shows for its TV channels and iPlayer streaming platform.

The MPs' report said the BBC could "spend more wisely when competing for programming". Overall, the BBC brings "immeasurable benefits" to society but needs reform of the TV licence fee to avoid a fate of "managed decline", they said.

Committee chair Dame Caroline Dinenage said the report , externalcomes at "a pivotal moment for the BBC", which is grappling with changing media habits, declining income and negotiations with the government over how it is paid for.

Dame Caroline said the government "must ensure the BBC has a universal and sustainable source of funding".

But, she added, the BBC "can play its part by sweating its assets and boxing clever for the licence payer by ending illogical practices such as outbidding commercial rivals for overseas hits such as Suits, Schitt's Creek and Scooby Doo".

The rights to air all three programmes were bought by the BBC after contracts with other networks or streaming services expired.

"At a time of constrained resources, the BBC should not be paying over the odds for overseas content, particularly when it's a bidding war against commercial UK broadcasters," the committee said.

The MPs added that they "did not believe that this provides value for money for the licence fee payer".

The BBC said it spends less than 5% of its content budget on acquiring shows, less than other broadcasters, and they are a cost-effective way of delivering high-quality content to audiences who go on to discover homegrown programming.

News.title: Who is the 'hero' Indian pilot who was stabbed on Israel-bound flight?
News.content:
Capt Machchhar grew up in India's Mumbai city, where his parents still live. He joined SpiceJet, an Indian airline, in 2011 before moving to Dubai eventually. He was an experienced pilot by 2022 when he joined Flydubai.

He has more than 9,750 hours of flying experience, including more than 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, according to his LinkedIn profile.

His former employer SpiceJet issued a statement calling Machchhar a "hero" who had saved "countless lives".

Last year, Capt Machchhar spoke about how he started flying and his experiences as a pilot on a podcast called Bona-Fide Banter.

Aviation, he said, was "never a childhood dream". When he was around 19, he joined a management course, planning to work with his family's business. But then he came across an aviation seminar and "the bug bit [him]," he added.

Machchhar also spoke about how, when he wore his pilot's uniform, he was "no-nonsense" and thought "about work 100%". But unlike his younger days, he added, he now placed a greater value on having a healthy work-life balance and spending time with family.

"Give personal life equal importance - it will help you fly longer," he advised.

He also detailed challenges he had faced in the air, including when a passenger went into early labour and the crew worked together to ensure the baby was born safely.

"In aviation terms, I was lucky to grow up with people who helped me be the pilot that I am today," he said, crediting senior pilots with teaching him how to face stressful situations.

At the time of the conversation, Capt Machchhar said that no plane he'd flown had had to make an emergency landing. He had, however, faced medical emergencies and minor aircraft issues causing delays.

He said delays were "not my problem. As long as you're walking out of the aircraft [safely], that's what I want."

Indian social media has been awash with praise for Capt Machchhar since his identity emerged, with commenters calling him a hero. Snippets from the podcast have also gone viral.

News.title: Veteran broadcaster Dame Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther Rantzen, who presented BBC show That's Life! for 21 years and launched the charity Childline, has died at the age of 86.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the veteran broadcaster and campaigner had "changed countless lives".

Dame Esther hosted and produced That's Life! during its run from 1973 to 1994. It regularly attracted 20 million viewers for its mixture of serious consumer investigations and light-hearted items.

She launched Childline, a British counselling service for children and young people, in 1986, and in 2013 she launched Silver Line to help elderly people suffering from isolation and loneliness. Later in life, she became a prominent campaigner for the legalisation of assisted dying.

She had been terminally ill with lung cancer. In December 2023, she revealed she had joined Dignitas, the Swiss assisted dying clinic.

But in a statement given to the Press Association earlier this month, she said that despite having "spent the money and made the plans" to go to Dignitas, she had since reached the point where she was "too physically fragile to make the journey".

She added that the law must "change and change quickly", as she renewed her plea ahead of the latest debate and vote on the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, which failed to pass through the Commons.

News.title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn
News.content:
Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.

Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.

However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.

The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.

Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".

Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.

As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".

News.title: Conservatives pledge 'tough love' benefit rules for under-25s
News.content:
The Conservatives have said they would introduce new work requirements for under-25s claiming benefits in a "tough love" approach to youth joblessness.

Young people claiming Universal Credit who are fit to work but have not worked for six months continuously would face new rules to qualify for payments, including daily attendance at a job centre or courses.

The party says the scheme would help tackle the almost one million people aged 16 to 24 in the UK who are not in education, employment or training, known as Neets.

But anti-poverty charity Trussell warned that people on Universal Credit could not afford basic essentials, which harmed their ability to find and keep work.

Under the Tory proposals, those aged 18 to 24 who apply for Universal Credit but have not previously worked for a continuous period of six months or more, for at least 16 hours per week, would instead have to take part in a "Get to Work" scheme.

Rather than Universal Credit, they would receive a "Get to Work Allowance" paid at the same rate but requiring daily attendance at a job centre, on work experience or work readiness courses.

They would be assigned a manager and have to take part in job search workshops and interview preparation sessions.

The programme would last six months, or less if a participant secures a job - but those who are still unemployed after half a year on the scheme would have their benefit cut by 30%.

Young people on Universal Credit who have previously worked for six months, have health issues or care responsibilities or are estranged would be exempt.

The party has also said it would look closer at whether parents' earnings and savings should be factored into welfare payments for their children.

Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said the measures were designed to "show some tough love" to reduce the number of Neets.

"Too many young people are leaving school and signing straight onto benefits - this is a waste of their potential and a disaster for our economy," the Tory MP said.

News.title: How That's Life! gave Esther Rantzen a career-defining moment
News.content:
Speaking in February 2024, Dame Esther said when she first got in touch with Sir Nicholas, who she called Nicky, she "congratulated him on his extraordinary achievement".

She told The Radio Times, external he had expressed some disappointment about his efforts, commenting that "not enough" people had been saved.

"I was devastated that he felt he had failed. I wanted to prove to this extraordinary man that every life he had saved was precious," Dame Esther added.

She invited him onto That's Life and during his first appearance, his scrapbook was shared with the audience, and two women he had saved as children - Vera Gissing and Lady Milena Grenfell-Baines - revealed their identities to him on TV.

They were sitting either side of Sir Nicholas, who had no idea of the surprise - something Dame Esther recalled as "incredibly moving".

Lady Milena is one of the most well-recognised Holocaust survivors in the UK.

She left Prague with her younger sister Eva at the age of nine, travelling on a special train arranged by Winton.

The two sisters were looked after by a Tameside family until their mother arrived the following year, having escaped via Norway.

Gissing, who was rescued from Prague in 1939 at the age of 11, lost most of her family during the Holocaust and ended up settling in the UK after the war ended.

"That was the only time in my career when I had to stop recording to wipe away my tears," Dame Esther also said.

The production team at That's Life were then contacted by several viewers who had watched the show and realised their connection to Sir Nicholas.

That gave the show's team an idea which would go on to become one of British television's most famous moments.

"In our next episode, I asked all those who owed their lives to him to stand, and Nicky, whom we had seated on the front row, turned to see the whole ground floor of the Television Theatre on their feet," Dame Esther recalled.

News.title: UK believes Iran involved in RAF Fairford incident, Burnham says
News.content:
The government believes that Iran played a part in the RAF Fairford incident which resulted in five men being arrested and then bailed, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said.

"There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford," he told the BBC. He did not provide further details.

Iran has responded, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the UK leader was "barking up the wrong tree".

"I can confirm Iran's belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all," he wrote on social media.

Asked why the suspects had been released on bail - a decision which has been openly questioned by President Donald Trump - Burnham insisted the men were subject to the "strictest possible bail conditions".

Speaking at the White House on Monday, Trump said: "I will tell you, I would have said, 'don't let them have bail'. I'm surprised that they released them. I wouldn't have done that."

But Burnham said: "I think people need to understand that when it says released - that isn't as people might think. It's obviously with the strictest possible bail conditions.

"The authorities have this under the strongest grip and closest control, and I can assure you of that."

Burnham's comments come after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that the incident at RAF Fairford "clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor".

News.title: Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, says Burnham
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said it is "possible" a future Labour election manifesto could promise a new in-out referendum on the European Union.

The prime minister told the BBC a referendum "wouldn't be the right thing to do right now" but the UK needed to "consider the options" for its relationship with the EU as "where we are isn't good enough".

It comes after he pledged in his Labour conference speech on Tuesday to explore closer ties with the bloc at a summit later this year.

The move could set up a huge dividing line at the next general election, with the Conservatives accusing Burnham of trying to "reopen old wounds by restarting the battles of the Brexit years".

As a candidate in the Makerfield by-election that propelled his return to Parliament, Burnham had promised not to "re-run" Brexit arguments and said he was "not proposing that the UK considers rejoining the EU".

In an interview with BBC political editor Chris Mason, Burnham was challenged over whether he was reopening divisive arguments about rejoining the EU, despite promising not to in May.

In response, the PM said: "No, I'm not proposing that, am I? I am saying that in a context when we're looking at a 10-year plan for Britain, Britain needs to consider the options as to where we will be.

"That is way before you even get to anything that's put before the public, this is about now just looking at what are the broad options for our relationship."

He suggested these options could include staying "exactly as we are", a closer relationship similar to that being discussed by the EU and Canada or rejoining the EU customs union.

However, Burnham stressed that "to leap back to a proposal and a referendum on it wouldn't be the right thing to do right now".

Pressed over whether including an in-out referendum in a future Labour manifesto was a possibility, Burnham said: "Yes, things are possible. I think where we are isn't good enough."

News.title: UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant scheme scrapped
News.content:
The UK government has announced the "one in, one out" agreement with France to send back some migrants who cross the Channel has been scrapped.

The pilot scheme allowed the UK to return some small boat arrivals while agreeing to take in the same number of people from France who were believed to have a legitimate claim to come to Britain.

Only around 1,500 people have been removed to France since the scheme began just over a year ago.

The BBC understands the government would have liked the scheme to continue, but felt it did not reach the desired scale.

A Home Office spokesperson said "lessons learned" would be used to "accelerate efforts" to return small boat migrants with no right to remain.

"The government's pilot with France to remove asylum seekers in exchange for an equal number of legal migrants is no longer processing new cases," the spokesperson said.

"However, flights will continue over the coming weeks to swiftly remove small boat migrants from the UK, and we will use lessons learned from the pilot to accelerate efforts to return small boat migrants with no right to remain in the UK."

The government would continue working with France to tackle small boat crossings, the spokesperson said, adding that "real progress" had been made with numbers "significantly down on last year".

The French Interior Ministry told the BBC: "We are discussing with the British the terms of exit from the agreement."

News.title: Bayeux tour to include audio account of tapestry
News.content:
Osman, who has no sight in either eye, contacted the museum via solicitor Leigh Day to ask whether audio-described tours would be available.

The law firm told him the museum had said self-guided visits would be prioritised over tours and events.

The British Museum said this was because there are limits on how many hours of light to which the tapestry can be exposed - and this in turn restricted visitor numbers.

Osman is seeking damages and a declaration that he was discriminated against and an order requiring the museum to change its policies.

He also said relevant staff should be given disability awareness training and he hoped the legal action would "help make sure blind and partially sighted people are properly considered" when major exhibitions are planned.

His solicitor said the Equality Act placed obligations on service providers to anticipate the needs of disabled people and take reasonable steps to avoid substantial disadvantage.

"Our client is asking for the same opportunity as sighted visitors to experience this exhibition."

A British Museum spokesperson said the museum was "committed to making the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition as accessible as possible" and had worked with specialist access consultants.

Provisions currently include a sensory map to help visitors prepare for their visit, as well as dedicated tours during the exhibition run which will include an in-person audio-described tour, the spokesperson said.

"We are also exploring including a separate audio-described tour as part of the exhibition's app-based audio guide."

The 70m (230ft) embroidery, which depicts the events leading up to the Norman Conquest of 1066, is on loan from France and is on display at the museum until 11 July 2027.

News.content:

Tennessee has failed in its attempt to execute Christa Pike, who survived and was rushed to hospital late on Wednesday despite being administered two doses of a lethal drug.

Pike was due to be the first woman put to death in the state in 200 years, after a court overturned a late stay of execution. Experts say her survival is unprecedented.

Officials administered pentobarbital to Pike twice, but she was later heard snoring. Witnesses say the curtain to the execution chamber was drawn and reopened on two separate occasions before the procedure was halted and they were asked to leave.

The attempted execution took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 8pm local time. Pike, 50, was being executed for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student she tortured and killed when she was 18.

The execution had already been delayed for hours after a panel of the Sixth US Circuit Court of Appeals issued a stay to allow further review of her legal challenges. The US Supreme Court later lifted that stay at Tennessee's request in a 6-3 decision, allowing the execution to proceed before Pike's death warrant expired at midnight.

Christa Gail Pike survived on Wednesday after being given two doses of the lethal drug pentobarbital, according to her lawyers.

Pike, 50, was alive and loudly snoring after the attempted lethal injection and was taken by an ambulance from the prison, her attorneys said. She was being treated at a hospital, but they said they hadn't been told about her condition.

She had been scheduled for execution at 10 a.m. Wednesday for the killing she committed at age 18 and would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

A death penalty expert said it was an unprecedented failure, and Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee halted the remaining executions for the rest of the year.

Officials gave Pike two doses of pentobarbital, her attorneys said in court filings late Wednesday. The Biden administration had previously removed pentobarbital from the federal protocol for single-drug lethal injections over concerns about the potential for unnecessary pain and suffering.

Gov. Bill Lee said in a statement that he has ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred" and that the remaining scheduled execution will not take place this year.

"Carrying out a lawfully imposed sentence is among the State's most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective," he said.

The Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement that they "followed every step of the State's lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General's Office."

open image in gallery Media witnesses recount the moments before the execution of Christa Pike was halted ( AP )

The state's execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes to be administered "if the inmate is not deceased" after the first set. It does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set.

Robin M. Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, said what Pike experienced is "singular and unparalleled."

Seven other people have survived medical problems due to an execution team's failure to access a vein to administer lethal injection drugs, but no one has stayed alive after receiving the drugs used in such executions, she said.

Media witnesses observing from a separate room said officials raised curtains to the execution chamber at 7:27 p.m., showing Pike strapped to a gurney.

Christa Pike’s ‘last words’

"I'm going to leave this world the way I spent most of my life and that is in love," she said in her "last" words. She described herself as at peace.

But Pike remained awake and at one point raised her head and asked prison officials if her arm was supposed to feel that way. It was unclear what she was referring to.

By 8:26 p.m., execution witnesses reported that the second dose of pentobarbital had been administered. Pike continued to snore behind the closed curtain until the microphone was cut off at 8:53 p.m. At that time, an announcement told media witnesses to leave the area.

open image in gallery Christa Pike is escorted from Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tennessee ( Knoxville News-Sentinel )

Lawyers for Pike filed an emergency motion late Wednesday to the Tennessee Supreme Court seeking to immediately halt and stay the execution, saying she was in "unnecessary agony" and it was violating her right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment. They also filed motions in the Sixth Circuit Court and a district court.

It was the second time this year that Tennessee has been unable to carry out an execution: In May, state officials called off the lethal injection of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and killing three people in 1994, after executioners tried and failed for over an hour to place an IV to administer pentobarbital.

What is pentobarbital?

Pentobarbital, a barbiturate that slows activity of the brain and nervous system, is often used by doctors to treat seizures and convulsions. In an execution, pentobarbital can be used in combination with other drugs or by itself. So far this year, 14 inmates have been executed by single-drug doses of pentobarbital — seven in Texas, six in Missouri and one in Georgia.

In America, pentobarbital is known by its brand name, Nembutal.

open image in gallery This photo provided by the U.S. Department of Justice shows a vial of pentobarbital used in the executions of two inmates in July 2020, according to court filings. ( Department of Justice )

Despite the limited availability of pentobarbital, it has been used in many cases of euthanasia or assisted suicide across the world.

It belongs to the class of drugs known as barbiturates. Invented in the late 19th century, they depress various aspects of brain function. Barbiturates have been used for many purposes, including to treat sleep disorders, epilepsy and traumatic brain injury.

In high doses, these drugs can cause suppression of breathing and death. Because of the risks associated with overdoses, they have been withdrawn from routine medical use over the last 20 years.

History of pentobarbital

States use a variety of drugs and drug combinations in lethal injections. Two of the most common are midazolam and pentobarbital.

Attorney General Merrick Garland in the final days of the Biden administration withdrew the pentobarbital lethal injection policy after a government review of scientific and medical research found there remains “significant uncertainty” about whether its use causes unnecessary pain and suffering.”

The Justice Department this year reauthorized the use of single-drug lethal injections with pentobarbital that were used to carry out 13 executions during the first Trump administration — more than under any president in modern history.

open image in gallery A lethal injection chamber in Texas ( Getty )

A Trump administration report claimed the Biden administration ‘got the standard and the science wrong’.. The Biden administration’s findings, among other things, “failed to address the overwhelming evidence” that an inmate injected with pentobarbital quickly “loses consciousness—rendering him unable to experience pain,” the report said.

“The prior administration failed in its duty to protect the American people by refusing to pursue and carry out the ultimate punishment against the most dangerous criminals, including terrorists, child murderers, and cop killers,” Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement at the time. “Under President Trump’s leadership, the Department of Justice is once again enforcing the law and standing with victims.”

Since capital punishment was reinstated in the 1970s, more than 1,600 prisoners have been executed in the United States, the vast majority by state authorities.

Nicolas Cage has taken aim at the Marvel Cinematic Universe, arguing that its increasingly crowded superhero films risk becoming little more than a “well-funded and glorified WWE”.

“It started out, in my view, terrific. Some of the early stories were marvellous, the way that they wove all the threads together and told the different character stories and backstories,” Cage, 62, said at the Fan Expo Dallas.

The MCU began in 2008 with Iron Man, starring Robert Downey Jr as billionaire industrialist Tony Stark, and what initially looked like a standalone superhero film became the starting point for an interconnected film universe.

Marvel followed it with The Incredible Hulk that same year, before introducing or developing characters including Black Widow, Thor, Captain America, and Hawkeye across Iron Man 2, Thor, and Captain America: The First Avenger.

The characters all came together in 2012’s The Avengers, which also featured Nick Fury, Hulk, and Loki and marked the culmination of the MCU’s first phase.

“But lately – I do say this with love – when I see these 50-plus, otherwise intelligent, remarkably gifted thespians putting on these ridiculous outfits and getting ready for the fight,” Cage said, “it’s hard for me not to be reminded that the MCU is becoming a well-funded and glorified WWE.”

open image in gallery Nicolas Cage voiced Spider-Man Noir in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse and reprised the character in the live-action Prime Video series Spider-Noir ( Prime Video )

Since Phase One, the MCU has expanded far beyond its original Avengers line-up, adding characters including Black Panther, Doctor Strange, Captain Marvel, and Spider-Man, while also bringing teams like the Guardians of the Galaxy, the Defenders, and the Eternals into its increasingly sprawling story.

The franchise is now in Phase Six, with Avengers: Doomsday set to bring together characters from across the MCU as well as returning figures from Marvel’s X-Men films.

Cage has played several comic-book characters in his career, starting with Johnny Blaze aka Ghost Rider in 2007’s Ghost Rider and its 2012 sequel Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance.

He also played Big Daddy in Kick-Ass, voiced Spider-Man Noir in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, and reprised that character in the live-action Prime Video series Spider-Noir.

“One of the things I like about Spider-Noir, it wasn’t cutting to the fight. It was a detective story. There was a mystery there,” Cage said. “I would like to see it get back to telling the stories and not just cutting to the wrestling match.”

open image in gallery Nicolas Cage says MCU’s increasingly crowded superhero films risk becoming little more than a ‘well-funded and glorified WWE’ ( AP )

Spider-Noir followed Cage as Ben Reilly, a down-on-his-luck private investigator in 1930s New York forced to confront his past as the city’s only superhero.

Created by Oren Uziel and Steve Lightfoot, the eight-part series also starred Lamorne Morris, Li Jun Li, and Brendan Gleeson.

Spider-Noir leaned heavily into the visual and storytelling conventions of classic film noir, and was released in both black-and-white and colour versions. Cage previously told Variety that he drew on actors including Humphrey Bogart, James Cagney, and Edward G Robinson for his performance as he wanted to capture the style of the “old world” actors while combining it with Spider-Man to create a “Roy Lichtenstein pop-art sensation of sorts”.

The series was well received by critics, scoring 92 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes, and received 11 Emmy nominations, the most of any Prime Video programme that year.

However, it was cancelled by Prime Video in September, just over three months after its launch.

open image in gallery Marvel is gearing up for its biggest crossover with Doomsday ( Marvel )

Some fans have called out Cage’s “50-plus” comment, with one Instagram user pointing out that he played “Ghost Rider at 48 and Spider-Noir and 62”.

“Not mad when he was cashing those Spider-Man Noir, Ghost Rider and Superman checks though,” another wrote, referring to Cage being cast as Superman in Tim Burton’s unmade Superman film in the 1990s.

Others looked at the timing and wrote that Cage might just be “mad his Spider-Man got cancelled”.

One user took a more sympathetic view, writing that “he’s not wrong, but dude, you were Ghost Rider, and almost played Superman in a Tim Burton movie. Get off the high horse, Nick”.

Marvel is now gearing up for its biggest crossover since Avengers: Endgame, with Avengers: Doomsday, due in cinemas on 18 December.

Directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, the movie brings together Avengers, Fantastic Four, and X-Men characters, alongside heroes from Wakanda, with Downey Jr returning to the MCU as Doctor Doom.

Its sprawling cast includes Chris Hemsworth, Chris Evans, Pedro Pascal, Anthony Mackie, Florence Pugh, Paul Rudd, Channing Tatum, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, and Tom Hiddleston.

Doomsday will be followed by Avengers: Secret Wars in December 2027, setting up another enormous ensemble.

It is the flood Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City has learned to expect.

Forecasters warned on Sept. 27 that high tides could combine with heavy rain to increase the risk of flooding in Ho Chi Minh City, one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable cities. As heavy rain combined with the tide on the evening of Sept. 30, the Saigon river and smaller waterways spilled onto the roads of Vietnam's commercial capital.

Life went on. Floodwater lapped at diners’ feet as they ate their food at roadside shops. Street vendors sat under plastic raincoats beside their wares, while customers in ponchos rode up, bought what they needed and headed back into the water.

Residents of low-lying neighborhoods in the city have long learned to live with the water. Some, like 63-year-old Vo Dang Thi, have raised the floors of their homes to keep the water out. But familiarity does not make the flooding less disruptive, and climate change is making the city’s exposure worse.

“In cities such as Ho Chi Minh City, climate change is increasingly amplifying flood risk because it is interacting with rapid urbanisation and land subsidence,” Benjamin Horton, a professor of earth science at City University of Hong Kong, said in an email to The Associated Press.

Rising seas meet sinking land in Vietnam

A warming climate is raising sea levels and bringing heavier downpours. In mid-September, heavy rain caused flooding in several provinces in northern Vietnam.

The changes can overwhelm drains in Vietnam's largest municipal area, especially in densely populated areas, Horton said.

Nearly half of Ho Chi Minh City's land is less than 1 meter (3.2 feet) above sea level and its drainage and canal system was built during the French colonial time, when the population was about 2 million. The system has since been expanded, but a study by the U.K.-funded Global Future Cities Programme found it has struggled to keep pace with rapid growth.

At the same time, parts of the city were sinking because of groundwater extraction, leaving low-lying neighborhoods even more vulnerable to flooding. Pumping water from beneath the city can cause the ground to compact and sink as water is removed from underground layers, Horton said.

This means residents of vulnerable areas are at risk from floodwaters that can inundate homes and businesses, disrupt transportation, damage infrastructure, contaminate water supplies and increase public health risks, he said.

Nguyen Ngoc Thuong, 45, who runs a small eatery, said the water can reach knee height when the tide is high or it rains heavily.

“It takes more than two hours for the water to go down. Some customers just walk through the water and sit down to eat” she said.

Growth ambitions collide with climate extremes

Vietnam is seeking to overhaul the economy with a goal of becoming a high-income country by 2045. Ho Chi Minh City has merged with neighboring provinces to create a vast new megacity, bringing together industrial hubs, services and seaports across Vietnam's south with sharply differing landscapes and levels of urbanization.

Authorities quickly realized the existing drainage system, approved in 2001 and 2008, was no longer fit for purpose in the expanded city.

They launched a $13 billion plan in July to tackle 159 flood hot spots by 2030 including upgrades to flood-control infrastructure. That month, the city also adopted a climate action plan through 2030 to upgrade drainage systems and major canals, expand green spaces and improve its ability to cope with heavy rain, high tides and rising sea levels.

But the problem for the city is not simply heavy rain or high tides, Horton said.

Higher sea levels make it harder for rainwater to drain to the sea, while heavier rainfall can send more water into the city in a short time. In a sinking city, water also builds up faster and drains more slowly. As the climate warms, floods that were once rare can become more frequent, deeper and last longer, he said.

“Climate change is raising the baseline on which these events occur,” Horton said.

This is already happening elsewhere in the region. In Thailand, heavy rains have battered the country since mid-September, affecting more than 2.6 million people and killing at least 19.

For now, Nguyen Thi Nhua is keeping her stall open, selling banh gio, a Vietnamese snack made from steamed rice flour and filled with seasoned pork. She has been selling it from the same sidewalk spot for 12 years as the city has grown and through countless bouts of rain and high tides.

“There are still customers who stop by, so I just keep my stall open when it rains or the tide comes in,” she said.

Away from the bustling crowds of Oia, Magma Resort Santorini is a sanctuary of calm on Greece’s busiest island

Location

If you want to avoid the crowds flocking to Oia, Magma Resort Santorini provides some peaceful solitude (though it’s just a 10-minute drive away if you want to see the iconic blue-domed buildings). It’s situated in the sleepy village of Vourvoulos with expansive views of the Aegean Sea and a vineyard next door.

open image in gallery Rooms with a sea view and private plunge pools are available ( Magma Resort Santorini )

It’s just a 10-minute drive from Santorini airport and, if you’re island hopping, a 20-minute drive from Thira ferry port. There’s no direct public transport, so you’ll need to hire a car, or Magma Resort can organise a private transfer from the airport, starting from €40 (£34) one way. The hotel also runs a complimentary shuttle to and from Fira (the capital) and Yalos Beach, approximately five minutes from the resort, which you’ll need to organise with the front desk or concierge.



The vibe

Magma Resort Santorini has 59 rooms, 24 of which are suites, making it feel more like a boutique destination than an expansive resort.

open image in gallery There’s a cosy firepit area to watch the sunset ( Magma Resort Santorini )

The decor takes inspiration from Santorini’s volcanic landscape, with rugged black stone finishes across the poolside and hotel entrance, and a firepit surrounded by low-slung lounge chairs, where you can enjoy a glass of wine from the Magma vineyard as the sun sets. Large stone tiles and earthy tones feature throughout the hotel, making you feel relaxed as soon as you step into the lobby.

Service

With a 24-hour reception, hotel staff go above and beyond to make your stay more comfortable, whether that’s ordering a freddo espresso to the poolside (a must-try in Greece) or helping you to organise excursions. Starting from €120 (£102) per person for a shared experience, they can help you to book a sunset Catamaran cruise, which will show you the island from the Aegean Sea. You’ll see everything from the windmills in Oia to the unspoiled, secluded port of Thirassia.

open image in gallery You can book a private wine tasting in the Magma Vineyards as part of your stay ( Magma Resort Santorini )

If you prefer to keep your feet on dry land, hotel staff can also book you a private wine tasting next door to the resort at Magma Vineyards. The hotel’s sommelier will walk you through a range of Assyrtiko wines native to the island, alongside food pairings made with fresh local ingredients. For an additional cost, you can also access a laundry service, an on-call doctor, turndown service and more.

Bed and bath

Across 59 rooms at Magma Resort Santorini, you’ll find nine types of room available, with options of a sea view, private plunge pool and an outdoor hot tub on the veranda. The king-size rooms offer plenty of space for a couple, while the lava and magma suites are the perfect size for a small family.

open image in gallery The rooms are furnished with calming, earthy tones ( Magma Resort Santorini )

Like the rest of the hotel, the rooms feel like a calming sanctuary, with linen fabrics and earthy tones. Pops of terracotta and deep mustard yellow appear in the bedding and cushions, while black accents in the rattan lounging chair, stone coffee table, and more contrast with the large cream stone floor tiles.

The bedroom flows effortlessly into the open bathroom area, with calming limewash-style walls, subtle lighting, matte black fixtures, and a large walk-in shower with Olive Era toiletries made with Greek olive oil. The hotel has no rooms with bathtubs.



Food and drink

The hotel has one main dining area by the pool, overlooking the expansive sea view. In the day, the Colombo Restaurant serves up an a la carte and buffet-style breakfast (7.30am-11am), or you can enjoy a leisurely lunch (12pm-6pm) while you lounge by the water. The breakfast buffet is vast and includes everything from egg white omelettes to generous slices of spanakopita, decadent waffles, thick Greek yoghurt, local honey to drizzle over granola, large platters of fresh fruit and more. That’s before you even delve into the à la carte menu, which includes classics like eggs Benedict and Tsoureki-style croque madame.

open image in gallery Breakfast buffet highlights include thick Greek yoghurt, local honey and platters of fresh fruit ( Magma Resort Santorini )

The lunch menu is just as fresh, with sharing plates of tacos and bao buns, or you can tuck into a Greek salad bowl or chicken gyros if you fancy something a bit more traditional.

From 7.30pm, this area transforms into the Magma Soul Restaurant, serving up a menu designed by Cretan chef Lefteris Soultatos, who melds Greek cuisine with culinary inspiration gained from working across France, Italy, Egypt and the USA. Highlights include octopus with Santorinian fava and orange vanilla-infused olive oil, Greek moussaka with aubergines, and red mullet fillet with smoked summer greens.

Both restaurants cater well to dietary requirements.

Facilities

As well as the outdoor infinity pool, there’s also an indoor heated pool, sauna, steam room and gym that you can relax in, a handy option if you’re visiting off-season. For an extra cost, you can book a spa treatment and choose from facials, massages, body scrubs, and more, with some lasting as little as 25 minutes and others up to an hour. If you prefer something a bit more active to start your day, the Magma Santorini runs morning yoga sessions for guests, at no extra cost, three times a week.



Accessibility

Three room types are accessible: a king room with a resort view, a king room with a sea view, and a king room with a sea view and private pool. The Junior, Lava and Magma suites are not accessible.

Pet policy

Dogs up to 7kg are permitted on request.

Check in/check out

Check-in is 3pm; check-out is 11am.

Family-friendly?

Cots are available upon request; high chairs are available in the restaurants; the hotel’s restaurant also offers a children’s menu. However, the pools are not really suitable for younger guests and there is little at the hotel to keep children entertained.

At a glance

Best thing: The infinity pool overlooking the Aegean Sea, which is supposedly the longest pool on the island of Santorini.

Perfect for: Couples, particularly honeymooners, looking for a relaxing, luxury stay.

Not right for: Families looking for child-friendly pools and activities.

Instagram from: An aperitivo by the fire pit, while watching the sunset.

Address: Magma Resort Santorini, Vourvoulos, 847 00 Santorini, Greece

Phone: +30 2286 441234

Website: Hyatt.com



Sabrina was a guest of Magma Resort Santorini

News.title: Hello Klean has launched a filter for your bathroom tap – here’s everything to know
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Hello Klean has become a leading shower filter brand, with its distinctive shower head proving popular for combatting hard water damage to your hair. Now the brand has developed a solution for your bathroom sink with its new skin filter, a filtration system designed for your tap, and I was one of the first to see it in action ahead of its release.

The skin filter is designed to fit on standard, single-lever bathroom taps and, much like the shower head, can be installed without having to make drastic plumbing changes to your bathroom.

When I spoke to the founder of Hello Klean, Karlee Zhang, she said the brand came up with the idea after it found out customers were washing their face with bottled water to combat the potential negative effects tap water was having on their skin. While it’s completely safe to wash your face with tap water in the UK, it does raise some intriguing questions about what filtering out certain minerals could do.



open image in gallery The skin filter is designed to fit on standard, single-lever bathroom taps ( Hello Klean )

It contains three types of filters, designed to improve your skin health:

A scale filter: A calcium-based scale inhibitor that captures minerals to reduce buildup on the skin

A calcium-based scale inhibitor that captures minerals to reduce buildup on the skin A heavy metals filter: A crystalline titanium-based filter that captures heavy metals in water, which the brand says helps to reduce skin inflammation

A crystalline titanium-based filter that captures heavy metals in water, which the brand says helps to reduce skin inflammation An activated carbon fibre filter: Hello Klean says this reduces chlorine by up to 98 per cent, helping to reduce post-cleansing dryness and tightness

The skin filter also has a faucet that switches your tap water to microbubble mode, which essentially infuses your tap water with microscopic bubbles, some of which are up to 80 times smaller than the width of human hair, according to Hello Klean. But what does this mean for your skin? The brand says these tiny bubbles significantly increase the surface friction of the water and, in turn, help to shift makeup and SPF more effectively.

I’ve only seen a demo of the skin filter, so at the moment, I can’t comment on these claims. However, the IndyBest team is putting it to the test and will report back on whether it’s worth investing in for your bathroom.

open image in gallery The smaller faucet adds microscopic bubbles to your water, which Hello Klean says will help to loosen make-up and SPF more effectively ( Sabrina Sahota/The Independent )

The Hello Klean app tracks your water usage, so you know exactly when it’s time to change filters. The NFC tag inside the filter means you can access this data by simply tapping your phone against it (much like Apple Pay works). There’s also an integrated smart refill light on the skin filter that flashes when it’s time for a replacement.

Hello Klean’s skin filter is available to buy now for £135 and comes with one extra replacement filter. If you opt in for the filter subscription, the price goes down to £108.
