The identity and motive of the Omani copilot who stabbed his captain on a flight to Israel, causing the plane to plummet dangerously and forcing it to land in Saudi Arabia, remained unknown on Thursday as investigators raced to learn more.

Israeli passengers on the FlyDubai flight carrying 174 people from the United Arab Emirates to the Israeli city of Tel Aviv have described how the bloodied Indian captain managed to open the cockpit door to let them in before they grappled with the copilot and stabilized a descent so sharp that the plane’s rudder was torn away.

“We felt helpless, suspended in midair, and I didn’t know who to turn to. But it was all instinct to survive,” one of the responders, Asaf Rajuan, said in a new statement shared by Israel’s presidency.

Saudi and UAE authorities have said little publicly beyond confirming that investigations were underway. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the copilot was arrested.

Capt. Smit Machchhar, widely praised as another hero of the flight, was reportedly in stable condition, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said overnight. The condition of the arrested copilot was not clear.

In a CNN interview aired on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu said the attacker was an Omani national and was being interrogated in Saudi Arabia.

U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that he and Netanyahu discussed the incident “at length” over the phone and that it seemed as though the copilot “was perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job."

Netanyahu said he spoke with the UAE’s president, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who agreed that Israel would join the interrogation of the suspect.

Israel’s foreign ministry said the people on board were from Israel, India and the UAE. The U.S. State Department said four passengers had American citizenship.

FlyDubai has said its flights to and from Israel would be suspended while an investigation takes place.

Netanyahu had warned in recent days of unspecified, heightened security threats. The country is a week away from the anniversary of the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel, which has triggered the war in Gaza.

In the chaos taht unfolded about two and a half hours after leaving Dubai, the flight descended from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet (around 10,000 meters to 5,100 meters) in about a minute, before making an erratic circle close to the Jordanian border and landing in the Saudi city of Tabuk about an hour later, according to Flightradar24, which identified the aircraft as a Boeing 737 Max 8.

A person who heard the flight’s communications with air traffic control described the plane being turned away by Saudi Arabia and Jordan before eventually landing in Tabuk, while passengers screamed in the background. The pilot’s voice was trembling as he called “mayday” and said a hijacking was taking place.

The air control operators gave no reason for the refusals. The person who heard the communications spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.

___

Associated Press writer Josef Federman in Jerusalem contributed.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco is particularly popular in south Asia that is placed between the cheek and lower gum. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

News.title: Why the UK medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks
News.content:
The UK’s medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks, experts have warned, with the NHS dependent on a system where much of the world relies on a handful of countries for its drug supplies.

India and China are the backbone of the global medicines market, manufacturing around two-thirds of the world’s active pharmaceutical ingredients. This leaves countries exposed to factory shutdowns, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions, shipping disruption and sudden changes in the price or availability of raw materials, experts told The Telegraph.

“We rely now more than ever on other countries to make sure we can get access to the medicines that the vast majority of people take,” said Dr James Davies, director of research and insights at Community Pharmacy England.

Nearly all the active ingredients in the UK’s most widely used medicines are made overseas, around 80 per cent of them in China and India, leaving the NHS exposed to shocks thousands of miles beyond its control.

The resilience of Britain’s medicine supply has eroded gradually in recent years, as global instability has placed growing strain on the supply chains it depends on.

“We’ve seen more global turbulence in general,” said Dr Davies. “It’s not unique to the UK, but it’s affecting countries across Europe, across the Western world, with the Iran war, with difficulties flying things over Ukraine and Russia, and challenges with shipping in the Red Sea.”

In the UK, shortages have been reported across a wide range of products, including antibiotics, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder medicines, epilepsy treatments, hormone replacement therapy, and some diabetes medicines.

The drugs most at risk are the cheapest and most widely used – statins, blood pressure pills and antibiotics – taken by millions of people and manufactured in China and India at huge scale and minimal cost.

“Some antibiotics are almost exclusively made in China,” said Dr Davies. “For some of the blood pressure medicines, they’re more likely to be made in India. But across the board, those two are where most of the raw ingredients for those active pharmaceutical ingredients come from.”

News.title: Fraudster jailed for 41 years over Pakistani nurse scam in Saudi
News.content:
A fraudster who sent 92 Pakistani nurses to Saudi Arabia on fake documents in an elaborate scam to provide workers for short-staffed Gulf hospitals has been jailed for 41 years.

Ghulam Zulfiqar Ali used forged experience certificates, created fake verification QR codes and phoney employment platform IDs.

Ali was being paid by the Saudi authorities to find staff, but also charged genuine Pakistani nurses who wanted a job overseas, in a racket that has caused major embarrassment to the Pakistan’s authorities.

Gulf nations including Saudi Arabia are experiencing a severe shortage of nurses, compounded by rapid population growth, a rising burden of chronic diseases, and heavy dependence on nurses from abroad.

The World Health Organization (WHO) forecasts a global shortfall of 4.5 million nurses by 2030, and recruiting nurses for developed countries is a lucrative trade.

The 91 women were all genuine nurses, but did not meet the criteria for the “Nurse Highly Qualified” visa category under which they were sent.

When the Saudi authorities realised the fraud they deported all the nurses.

Syed Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari, director of Pakistan’s Federal Investigation Agency, told the Telegraph: “They lost both their money and their employment, and the incident caused serious embarrassment to Pakistan internationally.”

Investigators found that between October 2022 and September 2023, a Pakistani employment firm called M/S Sahou Manpower obtained permissions for the recruitment of 108 nurses for a Saudi-based manpower company, to work in hospitals under the visa category “Nurse Highly Qualified”.

The investigation found the Saudi employer bore all recruitment costs, including visa processing fees and air tickets.

It paid the Pakistani recruiting firm between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,100 (GBP 830) per candidate. However, Ali was also demanding between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,000 (GBP 750) from each nurse.

Investigators found the candidates were genuine nurses, but did not meet experience requirements and were given fake certificates.

Meanwhile Ali had not uploaded their details to Saudi systems designed to verify and check qualifications and give each applicant a QR code. Instead he provided them with faked QR codes and verification platform IDs.

Ali was convicted of cheating, two counts of forgery and emigration offences.

He was given 41 years imprisonment by the special court in Rawalpindi. He was also fined £1,904 and ordered to pay £25,031 compensation – £272 to each of the 92 nurses.

His accomplice, Ghulam Fareed, was given three years’ imprisonment and a £544 penalty.

Nasreen Begum, one of nurses, told the Telegraph: “We are thankful to FIA for compensation. Most of us have genuine qualifications as nurse-midwives, licenced practical nurses, clinical nursing assistants and a lady health visitor but our documents weren’t verified and that landed us in a difficult situation.”

Zeenat Khan, another victim of the fraud, said she had opted to take a job in Saudi Arabia because she was jobless despite having nursing qualifications.

She said: “I have three kids and wanted to give them a good education. Now, I hope to get back my money,” she said.

Swera Ali said she had been working in a private hospital in her native Lahore, Punjab province, but received only £50 a month and performed 16 hours duty.

She said: “My parents took a loan from relatives to facilitate me, but my hope of making money from an overseas job was short-lived when they deported us after less than a month.”

Mr Bukhari added: “The investigation established that their nursing diplomas were genuine. The fake QR codes and fake [employment platform] IDs were created by the accused, and the experience certificates were forged by the visa agent without the knowledge of the nurses.”

News.title: How vaccines and antibiotics can beat some cancers
News.content:
At least one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a new study published in The Lancet.

An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024 – out of a total of 20 million recorded worldwide – were caused by common infections, almost all of which could have been prevented with treatments such as antibiotics or vaccines.

Almost half of infection-linked cancers, around 760,000 cases, were caused by H. pylori, a bacterium that infects the stomach, researchers from the International Agency for Research on Cancer found.

The pathogen, which is typically ingested through contaminated food and water and is carried by around 60 per cent of the world’s population at any given time, can remain relatively undetected in the gut for between 20 and 40 years without causing any symptoms.

If left untreated, it can trigger chronic inflammation in the stomach and cellular mutations that, in some cases, lead to gastric cancer.

Cases of stomach cancer linked to H. pylori are particularly common in East Asia, where roughly 80 per cent of the population carries the bacterium. This is due in part to the prevalence of a more aggressive strain of the pathogen, known as CagA, which is endemic to the region.

East Asian diets – which typically include salty, pickled or smoked foods – can also damage the stomach’s protective lining and accelerate the inflammatory processes that can contribute to stomach cancer, researchers have found.

While H. pylori infection is treatable with a course of antibiotics, its symptoms often mimic those of other digestive problems and can be difficult to distinguish without testing.

This means the infection can remain undetected for years, allowing inflammation and damage to progress.

News.title: ‘Pooled’ TB testing could save money and improve diagnosis, study finds
News.content:
Mixing phlegm samples from multiple patients in “pooled tests” for tuberculosis could halve costs and help find millions of missing cases, according to a major new study.

While most advances in fighting TB come with a large price tag, the shift in strategy could dramatically boost access to diagnosis and save money, experts said.

TB is the deadliest single infection globally, killing around 1.3m people every year, despite being both preventable and curable.

The gold standard in diagnosis is rapid molecular testing, which detects genetic material from the bacteria causing TB in patient sputum samples within hours. But each sample needs a specialist diagnostic cartridge that costs around US$8, beyond the budget of many poorer countries even before recent aid cuts.

In a pooled test, samples from multiple individuals are tested in one cartridge. If the result is negative then all of them are reported to be negative, but if the result is positive each is re-tested individually.

Results published in The Lancet Global Health found the strategy, with up to four patients in each pool, used half as many cartridges as individual testing – 7,028 compared to 14,362. It detected 84.9 per cent of people with TB compared with 88 per cent for individual testing.

The study involved more than 14,000 people whose symptoms suggested TB in Bangladesh, Brazil, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria and Vietnam.

Sports.title: Inside Matthias Jaissle’s journey from childhood tumour and months in wheelchair to becoming Newcastle boss
Sports.content:
Next

THE TRAUMA of having a neck tumour removed and months of being confined to a wheelchair failed to stop Matthias Jaissle.

The pain of that childhood health scare and the injury that ended his playing career in its prime has instead only made Newcastle’s head coach the man he is today.



Little was known about the German, 38, when he replaced Eddie Howe in August.

His energetic touchline antics have already made him a hit with the Toon Army – and landed him in trouble with match officials.



Stars like Lewis Hall speak openly about how great he is to play for.

But Jaissle’s short, sharp, and sometimes abrupt, answers in press conferences have failed to provide much of an insight into his character.



Now, for the first time since his arrival, he has lifted the lid on how his steely mentality was forged as a kid in the village of Neckartailfingen in an intimate sit-down at the club’s Knox training HQ.

Jaissle said: “I had a tumour, when I was five, in the neck. I couldn’t move my neck side to side.

“I was only five but I learned a lot about life already. How important it is to be healthy and how grateful you can be to be healthy and to follow your dream. It was not clear I would be able to play football at that age.”

Fortunately the former centre-half made a full recovery to become pro and moved to Stuttgart’s academy aged 14, where he was coached by future England boss Thomas Tuchel.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Promotion glory to Bundesliga followed after a transfer to Hoffenheim as did international recognition with Germany’s Under-21 side until more agony was in store.

He said: “That [tumour] was one part. Unfortunately, I was really unlucky with injuries.

“When I was in the youth team I missed a year, not being able to play a match. I was 16 but that gave me the discipline in life to really fight.

“At that age, you are usually going out, partying, you could quit in that period but I carried on.



“When I made my debut in the first team, after seven or eight months of playing regularly for Hoffenheim I ruptured my ACL, my meniscus, the cartilage, everything. I was done. I knew then it could be difficult to carry on playing at the highest level.

“It was tough. I had just become a Germany U21 player and I was about to be called into the national team for the first time.

“That was the next step. We would have played in the Under-21s Euros that summer and I ruptured my ACL in that March.

“It was a tough moment. I was really down back then. I listened to the stories saying I could be back in four months and I fully believed. After four months I was still in a wheelchair.”

Eventually he retired aged 25. But Jaissle was not ready to give up on the beautiful game.



And an invite into the famed-Red Bull setup by his former Hoffenheim coach Ralf Rangnick ignited a new fire within him.

Jaissle said: “I was struggling for a couple of months, really down, tough to get motivated, tough to get your own rhythm again.

“It was clear I wanted to have something with football again, not necessarily being a coach. It could have been sports director, athlete manager, agent, whatever. I started studying different things.



“Then I got the chance through Ralf Rangnick — therefore sometimes I mention him as a mentor. I got the chance to do a trainee program in Leipzig.

“I wanted to transfer the things I learned in my study onto the pitch or in the offices. It was planned to make every six weeks another department.

MATTHIAS JAISSLE MANAGERIAL CV The German has already got an impressive array of silverware on his CV. RED BULL SALZBURG Austrian Bundesliga: 2022, 2023 Austrian Cup: 2022 AL-AHLI Saudi Super Cup: 2025 AFC Champions League Elite: 2025, 2026

“I started as an assistant coach for Sebastian Hoeness, the current coach of Stuttgart and after two weeks I felt, ‘Wow, I have joy back in life, not only studying and reading. I have a new purpose’.”

Two years as No2 to Alexander Zorniger in Denmark at Brondby followed. Jaissle then proved himself as boss in his own right at RB Salzburg’s feeder club FC Liefering.

In 2021 he earned a promotion to the top job with the Austrian giants and led them to two titles, an Austrian Cup and into the Champions League knockout stages.



More success came in Saudi Arabia at Al-Ahli, winning back-to-back Asian Champions League crowns and the Super Cup, before his shot at the big time arrived in the shape of Newcastle.

The challenge of taking over a side that had replaced a host of established international talents with promising youngsters was too hard to resist.

And even when it felt like the world was crashing down around him as Newcastle were thrashed 4-1 at Leeds this month, his belief and confidence never wavered.



Especially in his “vertical football” philosophy that has so far produced just one defeat in seven games in all competitions. And it all stems from overcoming that early health scare.

Jaissle, who revealed he has now found a house in the North East to move into with his partner Lisa Czetsch, said: “For sure that makes you the person you are, in whatever aspect it is.

“The belief that you can overcome every obstacle. Every setback also has a positive side as well.

“So if you overcome these challenges, then you usually become stronger, more resilient.”

He added: “The style will work anywhere. They questioned it in Saudi Arabia – can you play that style when it is 40 degrees outside?



“Can you play it when players are maybe not at the physical level that you have had before? We showed it is possible.

“Look at Barcelona now, and the way they are flying. I would not say that Hansi Flick is from the Red Bull dynasty, but there are a lot of elements in the way he works that I can see are from there.

“The players there might have been more used to playing in a tiki-taka style, but they have adapted and you can see it is working.



“I was listening to Rodri, and he was saying a lot about the physicality and the way they train now. It shows that it can be done in every league, in my eyes.

“That’s also the reason why I am here and why the club signed me. The club is striving for a clear identity and, fortunately, a playing style, independent of who the coach is in the past years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Therefore I think it is a great fit for me. What I mentioned, it is the same approach, that is the good part because the players were already here who fit into that style.

“In the summer we made a couple of adjustments although we signed younger players, but that is exciting.”

Sports.title: Maths may suggest Man City get a 456-point deduction to end up in non-league – but football doesn’t work like that
Sports.content:
Next

FOUR points deducted for Forest. Six for Everton. Another two for Everton. Six for Leicester.

So what happens when Manchester City are found to have breached the rules 114 times?



Four multiplied by 114 is a 456-point deduction.

Manchester City would be relegated so far down the football pyramid they would be in National League North.



Except it doesn’t work like that.

There is no Premier League list pinned to the wall saying: one ­financial breach, four points; two breaches, eight; 114 breaches, please report to the National League.

The four-point calculation is not a rule. It is what happens when you take recent points deductions and try applying an average to a case which is anything but average.

That is important because 114 ­findings does not mean 114 identical PSR breaches.

The charges cover different rules, different seasons and different types of conduct over nine seasons.

So 456 points is not the answer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But it is useful because it shows how ridiculous it would be to try to find the answer by multiplying ­previous sanctions.

And then you read the judgment and sat in every ­Premier League meeting where it has been discussed — as I have — this affair stops being a maths problem.

The Independent Commission found that a series of City’s sponsorship agreements were “shams”.

The club’s accounts between 2009-10 and 2017-18 had wrongly recorded more than £830million as income when it should have been treated as equity contributions. Expenses were also understated.

The accounts simply did not provide a true and fair picture of City’s financial position.



Then comes the sentence that blows away any suggestion this was simply a dispute about accounting terminology: “By its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL rules.”

There isn’t much ambiguity there.

It doesn’t say City misunderstood the rules or that they were complicated.

It doesn’t say somebody forgot to tick a box.

The commission also found that, when the accounts were restated, City failed to meet the relevant break-even requirement by a “very substantial amount” in every season covered by that charge.



City made “concerted efforts to stop and frustrate” the investigation and breached its duties of co-operation in most of the respects alleged.

So while a 456-point punishment may be absurd, it does not follow that the punishment should be modest.

That is the trickiest part of this entire business.

What is the Premier League actually intending to punish?

The number of rules broken? The number of seasons involved? The financial advantage? The sporting advantage? The deliberate nature of the conduct? The attempt to frustrate the investigation? Or all of it?



Look at Forest and Everton.

Forest received four points for a PSR breach.

Everton’s original ten-point deduction was reduced to six on appeal.

A separate Everton breach resulted in another two points.

Those cases establish that points deductions are not fixed. They also don’t establish that four points is the exchange rate for cheating.



Football does not work that neatly. And nor does compensation.

This is where the old Carlos Tevez case comes back into the conversation.

West Ham were fined £5.5m over the registration arrangements involving Tevez and Javier Mascherano. They were not docked points and avoided relegation, while Sheffield United went down in 2007.

After years of legal wrangling, West Ham paid Sheffield United around £20m in compensation.



Punishment and compensation are two different things.

That matters because if another club can demonstrate it suffered a direct financial loss as a result of City’s conduct, why should that question disappear?

We have seen the principle tested again with Burnley being awarded £26m in their compensation claim against Everton, who are appealing.

But there is a very large difference between saying ‘we were harmed’ and proving ‘this is the damage you caused us’.

Football is basically one enormous Sliding Doors movie.



If City had not done this, who ­finishes where?

Who gets into the Champions League? Who wins the title? Who stays up?

Who signs which player?

And does the manager who gets sacked in November still get sacked if the league table looks different?

You cannot simply redraw every Premier League table since 2009 and announce new winners.



Sporting history does not come with a reset button.

Then there are the players.

The commission found that in ­certain arrangements terms relating to remuneration and image-rights ­payments ought to have appeared in players’ contracts but did not.

That is a regulatory issue.

Players weren’t sitting with a calculator and a copy of the Premier League handbook.



They sign contracts, they don’t ­prepare the club’s accounts. There is the increasingly popular idea City should get some enormous points deduction and “work it off” over ­several seasons.

What is this — football community service? A points deduction is a sanction, not a mortgage.

You don’t hand Manchester City a 456-point overdraft and tell them to make monthly repayments.

The commission has to decide what sanction is appropriate for the actual findings and the rules governing those historic breaches.



What are Man City charged with? THE Premier League claim Man City hid £900m in 'sham' deals across a nine-year period. They were found guilty on 114 of the initial 115 charges – with the number now up to 130 charges – which fit into six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

That is a much harder task but it is also the only sensible one.

A punishment designed simply to make people gasp does not necessarily make sense.

If City get a points deduction, explain the number. If it’s a fine, explain why money is sufficient.

If there are sporting sanctions beyond points, explain what they are intended to achieve.

If other clubs have suffered demonstrable financial losses, deal with compensation separately.



The Premier League has spent years telling its clubs that financial rules matter.

Clubs have lost points, paid fines, been relegated, and have been forced to sell players.

Clubs have watched European football disappear from their budgets.

Now the biggest case of all has arrived. And the commission’s judgment does not describe a club which ­simply got its sums wrong. It describes overstated income of more than £830m, sponsorship arrangements called “shams” and accounts that did not give a true and fair view.

It says City clearly intended to ­circumvent the rules and the club made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the investigation.



Those are the facts the punishment has to answer. Not 456 points or whatever number looks most frightening on the front page.

There is a temptation in football to think justice means making somebody suffer as much as possible.

It doesn’t. Justice means making the punishment make sense.

If the sanction is too small, every club that has played by the rules will ask what the point was.

If it is simply enormous because enormous looks good, City will ask what the logic was.



And if there is no logic, the argument never ends and the appeals rumble on for years.

So, the Prem needs to do something much harder than produce a spectacular number. It needs to explain it.

Explain what advantage was gained.

Explain how the duration and seriousness of the conduct have been weighed and why the sanction is proportionate.

And explain why another club committing the same offence would be treated the same way.



That last bit is the one I would put in bold. Because every owner in the Premier League is watching. Every chief executive is watching. Every supporter is watching.

They want to know whether the rules mean what they say and whether they are same for everyone.

The answer cannot simply be the biggest punishment anyone can ­imagine. Nor can it be the smallest punishment the lawyers can defend.

It has to be one that can survive scrutiny from Manchester City, from the other 19 clubs, from the courts and, most importantly, from supporters who want to believe the competition is run on a level playing field.

This is not about finding a number that makes everybody happy. There probably isn’t one.



So what would I do?

I would go for a 50-point deduction, an £83m fine — roughly 10 per cent of the £830m by which sponsorship income was overstated — and a three-year restriction on registering new players.

Not because 50 is some magic number but because the punishment has to hurt on the pitch as well as in the accounts department.

Crucially, I would still leave City something to play for this season.

A 50-point deduction would put them in an extraordinary fight for survival. But it would not make relegation a mathematical certainty from the moment the punishment was announced.



That matters. Punishment should be severe, but football should still be allowed to happen.

Make Manchester City fight for every point, make them earn their way back from the hole they have dug and let the rest of the season determine whether they survive.

I would also expect City to face at least one season excluded from European competition, subject to Uefa’s own process and jurisdiction.

I would go after individuals, too.

The commission says a number of important witnesses called on behalf of the club gave false evidence, with some giving evidence they knew to be untrue and were therefore dishonest.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

That should potentially mean a ­suspension from holding senior football positions.

You cannot tell every club in the Premier League that financial integrity is fundamental and then punish only the corporate logo on the shirt.

FOOTBALL star Erling Haaland, the Premier League’s top scorer last season, has netted a £19.6million fortune.

The 26-year-old Man City ace has built his vast wealth while his club remains mired in a financial scandal.



Figures show his image rights firm, York Promotions, has cash deposits of £5million and assets and investments worth more than £12million.

Assets include a share in two planes worth £2.1million.



Haaland earns £500,000 a week on the pitch.

Top players earn extra cash from clubs from the sale of merchandise like shirts that bear their “name, nickname, slogan and signatures, image, likeness, voice, logos, get-ups, initials, team or squad number”.



The in-form striker has deals with big-name brands Nike, EA Sports, Midea, Breitling, Dolce & Gabbana, Red Bull, Beats by Dre, TAG Heuer, Prime Hydration, Hyperice, and the Norwegian Seafood Council.

Leeds-born Erling runs the company with his dad and manager Alfie, who also played for Man City.

Top tax accountant Julia Hoyle – an associate of Haaland’s late agent Mino Raiola – is also listed as a director.

The ace has been linked with a move to Barcelona or Real Madrid after it was found Man City arranged “sham” contracts with commercial partners.



The contracts were part of a “disguised funding scheme” to inflate club revenue by more than £900million.

The disgraced club now face possible relegation.

Sports.title: Crazy moment Lionesses hero Williamson picks ball up and gives away penalty as Arsenal crumble in Champions League
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL squandered a two-goal lead to drop crucial Champions League points against Paris FC following a Leah Williamson howler.

The 29-year-old gave away a penalty following a bizarre handball incident at the end of the match.

With the Gunners leading 2-1 in the 86th minute, goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez kicked the ball to Williamson, who set herself to take a goal kick.



The England captain put her hand on the ball, prompting referee Iuliana Demetrescu to swiftly give a penalty.



Despite protests from Williamson, the spot-kick stood and was converted by Maeline Mendy to level the score.

Arsenal had led the match 2-0 thanks to goals from Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway, but Clara Mateo capitalised on a high defensive line to get Paris back into it.

The Gunners came close to seeing the game out for the win, but the late error saw them drop points for the first time in this European campaign.



It was also the latest in a run of disappointing results and performances.

Reflecting on the bizarre moment, Russo said: “It was a mistake, obviously it wasn’t intended at all. We let them come back into the game in the second half probably way before that moment.”

Head coach Renee Slegers did not show up for the post-match press conference after the disappointing end.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Instead, her assistant, Aaron D’Antino, spoke to the media.

Reflecting on the result and performance, he said: “It’s incredibly disappointing, or frustrating I should say, because we felt like for large periods of the game we had good control.

“They are a counter-attacking team, that is their threat, so we were aware of that. And yes, the first moment we conceded the first goal, we can defend it better from the first phase.

“But there were periods of the second half that we were really happy with our attacking intent and that’s a key area that we’ve been working incredibly hard on and we thought we got some good rewards.

“And then the way that the game ends is incredibly disappointing. We didn’t think it was a penalty, we don’t think the goal kick had actually been taken from what we had seen.



“But it goes to VAR and apparently that’s a penalty.”

Slegers now finds herself under increasing pressure following a slow start to the season.

The Gunners currently sit seventh in the WSL table with just five points from their opening four games.

They have scored just two league goals during that time.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Punishment update, Andy Burnham statement, new evidence claim
Sports.content:
Manchester City are facing a severe punishment after being found guilty of breaching 114 financial rules

The latest news on Manchester City after the club were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules, as the deadline to appeal the decision moves ever closer

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's Manchester City charges live blog for Thursday, October 1.

The Premier League announced earlier this week that City had been found guilty of 114 charges brought against them for financial breaches.

City responded by maintaining their innocence and have until Friday to launch an appeal, with the club expected to do so before the deadline.

It now remains to be seen what punishment is given to City, with reports claiming that chiefs at other football clubs want a sanction to be imposed before the end of the season.

Etihad, the main shirt sponsor for City, meanwhile, have also issued a statement in response saying they are "deeply concerned" by the Premier League's announcement. There are also concerns that City's Abu Dhabi owners could be stripped from the club, something Prime Minister Andy Burnham doesn't want to happen.

Elsewhere, former City chief Chris Bird has claimed his old club might have new evidence to prove their innocence. However, football finance expert Stefan Borson has refuted the claim, insisting that under Premier League rules, City cannot submit new evidence without the independent panel's permission.

Stay tuned for the latest news and updates in our live blog below as the saga continues to unfold...

Sports.title: How 13 of the world's most powerful countries have reacted to Man City's bombshell verdict
Sports.content:
How 13 of the world's most powerful countries have reacted to Man City's bombshell verdict

The most powerful nations in the world have responded to Manchester City's charges

View 9 Images The Premier League states that Manchester City systematically broke rules for almost a decade (Image: Getty)

The Premier League has confirmed Manchester City have been found guilty of all financial rule breaches brought against them. And the shockwaves aren't just reverberating around English football, but across the entire sporting world.

‌



Following a landmark investigation launched almost eight years ago, an independent commission concluded that between 2009 and 2018, City orchestrated "sham" contracts to artificially inflate revenues and suppress costs by between £830million and £900million.

‌



In what the Premier League has labelled "the most significant disciplinary case in the league's history," the club was also found guilty of concealing financial streams, violating spending caps and systematically stonewalling the multi-year inquiry.

‌



City have vehemently rejected the verdict, branding the findings a "conspiracy theory" and pledging an immediate appeal, which must be lodged by October 2. Whilst formal sanctions remain undecided, a separate hearing will take place to hand down the penalty.

Man City rivals' private thoughts on vote to expel club from Premier League READ MORE :

With potential outcomes ranging from massive points deductions and unprecedented fines to the stripping of titles, the case stands to rewrite the history of English football. Media outlets across every continent have reacted accordingly.

View 9 Images Owner Sheikh Mansour, chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano's legacies are all in the firing line (Image: Getty)

‌



South China Morning Post - Hong Kong

"Man City might be the biggest cheats the sporting world has ever seen. What comes next?" questions the South China Morning Post, based in Hong Kong. "Ben Johnson's Olympic gold and Lance Armstrong's seven Tour de France titles were wiped out. Will City's Premier League crowns go the same way?

"Regardless of how it plays out, this episode has infiltrated every corner of the Premier League, driving a bus through the English top flight's pompous claim to be the world's best domestic competition.

"A penny for the thoughts of executives at Sky Sports, currently paying around £1.3billion a year to screen a league where nobody knows whether what they have watched over the past 17 years was for real, in legal terms, at least.

‌



View 9 Images It is unknown what will happen to Enzo Maresca's side (Image: Getty)

"With their wish to tighten the belts of fat cats who would have gladly poured their own cash into clubs, and, by extension, invested in the English game, the Premier League has tied itself in knots.

"Railroaded into straitened circumstances, clubs are increasingly selling major assets overseas, leading to a steady talent drain. Still, if Manchester City are found to have ridden roughshod over rules they agreed to be bound to, all bets are off regarding their punishment."

‌



Gazzetta dello Sport - Italy

Italy's La Gazzetta dello Sport points to some possible retribution for Inter Milan, who lost the 2023 Champions League final to City, but claims: "This is a huge victory for the English league.

"It means that the Premier League is capable of enforcing its rules and that clubs aren't free to break them. Despite seeing a huge asterisk over its last 15 years, the Premier League as an entity emerges strengthened.

View 9 Images Former manager Pep Guardiola's legacy has been questioned (Image: Getty)

‌



"The damage to their reputation has already been done. The 115 charges are no longer the elephant in the room, but there's no doubt that the club has broken the rules in its rise to the top of English football.

"Even if they aren't removed, those headlines will remain asterisks. Meanwhile, clouds gather over the present until the sanctions become definitive. City's future as a global player, if they're expelled from the Premier League, is at risk."

ESPN - USA

American company ESPN has raised one specific line from the Premier League's "core decision" document, perhaps hinting at how this case will be resolved. It writes: "There is one line in the core decision that offers a little bit of hope.

‌



"Maybe it's a bread crumb from the panel, suggesting what they hope the best possible outcome might be. Article 70 states that 'There was no evidence that [REDACTED] authorised the operation... and so went on without his knowledge.'

"Who are they talking about? Is it Khaldoon Al-Mubarak, the chairman? Could it be somebody high enough up the Abu Dhabi food chain that could legitimately say: 'Enough! We're obviously not getting away with this. There's no evidence that I was involved, so I'm putting a stop to this.'

View 9 Images City won seven major trophies during the period in which they have been found guilty of cheating (Image: Getty)

‌



"'I'm calling up the Premier League and the affected clubs and their owners, most of whom are fellow billionaires anyway, I'm dumping all the responsibility on my lawyers, accountants and club executives and I'm going to see if there's a plea bargain to be had.'

"It's a far-fetched thought and it's also hard to see what a plea bargain might look like - at least one that would satisfy other clubs and their fan bases. It would need to be painful for City not just financially, but in sporting terms too.

"Then again, if there's one thing the owners aren't lacking, it's money. But it might just offer a way out and spare the Premier League another protracted legal battle. If not, if City lose the appeal and the acrimony continues, the knowledge that nearly a decade of Premier League football was, in many ways, a sham, is going to be a body blow.

‌



"Not so much for fans of other clubs because most concluded a long time ago that City were guilty. But for City fans themselves, who were lied to all this time and who put their trust in a lie. Some won't care. Many will. But we'll all have to live with the fallout."

FOX Sports - Australia

FOX Sports in Australia points to a local case for answers: "Those who have been there in the stands for the entire ride are hurting. Fans on the blue side of Manchester who have taken immense pride in their club, who always played little brother to their rivals over at Old Trafford, are outraged.

"After seeing their club emerge from the third tier of English football in the late 1990s to become a Premier League powerhouse, their spirits are broken. They were duped. The titles may stand or like what happened to Melbourne Storm in the NRL when their salary cap scandal was exposed, those triumphs may simply be struck from the record with no champion awarded in those seasons."

‌



The National - United Arab Emirates

View 9 Images Some suggest City could be relegated (Image: Getty)

It is telling how The National broke the groundbreaking news regarding City. The Premier League's statement, included in many other articles from around the globe, is almost entirely omitted. The outlet's headline references City's impending appeal and almost immediately points to the club's own statement, in which they stated they were "disappointed and surprised" by the verdict.

City's statement is included in full and The National writes that the club's lack of co-operation is only "reported." In 2016, the newspaper was acquired by International Media Investments, a subsidiary of the Abu Dhabi Media Investment Corporation.

‌



This private investment firm is wholly owned and controlled by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who owns City via the Abu Dhabi United Group and is the vice president and deputy prime minister of the UAE. City came under his ownership in 2008, during which the nine years of financial breaches took place.

BILD - Germany

German outlet BILD dubbed the findings "City's full verdict of shame" and wrote: "The punishment is still pending and will be decided in a separate proceeding. According to the Premier League, fines, point deductions, and other sporting sanctions are among the possible penalties. Media reports also indicate that relegation is a possibility."

‌



Le Parisien - France

French publication Le Parisien suggests that things look bleak for City in its report, which reads: "Officially sanctioned, Manchester City can expect the worst."

A Bola - Portugal

A column in Portuguese paper A Bola claims fans might abandon the club: "I can't help but think of the fans who, after years of being Manchester's poor relation, were on top in every aspect: money, titles, players, and who may now start fleeing in droves."

Viaplay - Norway

The future of striker Erling Haaland will be a topic of debate should City receive severe punishment and Viaplay in Norway has likened the situation to Lance Armstrong's infamous doping case.

‌



View 9 Images Haaland's future could hang in the balance (Image: Getty)

The panellist wrote: "I have read the premise and justification for the Premier League finding Man City guilty. In my mind it is a 'Lance Armstrong moment.' The number of offences. The seriousness of several of them. How long has it been going on? Based on those premises, there is no doubt. It is financial doping and must be punished severely."

The Times of India - India

Haaland's future was the sole focus of The Times of India: "If Haaland himself decided that remaining outside the Premier League was not compatible with his ambitions, the situation could develop into the kind of blockbuster transfer that few clubs could ignore."

‌



Daily Maverick - South Africa

The Daily Maverick in South Africa uses Chelsea's recent disciplinary matter to put City's breaches into perspective: "A recent matter regarding Chelsea, in which they incurred a £10-million fine after breaking the Premier League agent regulations 74 times, offers a clear contrast. In that instance, Chelsea were praised for self-reporting the violations.

"The Blues were also determined not to have derived any meaningful sporting benefit. Conversely, neither mitigating circumstance seems relevant to City's situation, given the widespread allegations of fraudulent financial reporting and the concentration of charges concerning non-compliance with league rules."

View 9 Images One outlet recalled how Chelsea self-reported their wrongdoings (Image: Getty)

‌



La Tercera - Chile

La Tercera in Chile issued concern about City being stripped of titles, including the 2013/14 Premier League crown won under Chilean Manuel Pellegrini: "The league is now in a position to impose drastic sanctions on City, including stripping them of the titles they won, one of which was with Pellegrini as manager."

Mundo Deportivo - Spain

Finally, Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, like many other outlets around the world, states that whatever punishment is imposed on City, this is a stain that will never be washed off.

View 9 Images The general consensus is that City's reputation has been irreversibly tarnished (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

It penned: "Whatever the punishment, City's glory days will be overshadowed. The team that dominated the Premier League for a decade might even win its appeal, but for the public and the other clubs, the suspicions that it broke the rules of competition, using fake sponsorships to disguise Abu Dhabi's money, are already well-founded.

"Despite the mockery they have displayed for years and regardless of how long the legal battle drags on with the appeal, one thing is certain: English football will never be quite the same.

"The inevitable outcome, whatever the final sanction, will be the irreparable stain that falls upon Manchester City. A shadow of doubt will always hang over their successes, hovering around the dirty methods they used to win titles and trophies."

Sports.title: Wayne and Coleen Rooney’s son released by Premier League club as they open up on difficult call
Sports.content:
Wayne and Coleen Rooney’s son released by Premier League club as they open up on difficult call

Wayne and Coleen Rooney have discussed the moment that their son was released by the Premier League club

View 3 Images Wayne and Coleen on the Therapy Crouch podcast (Image: YouTube)

Wayne and Coleen Rooney youngest son Cass has been released from Everton's academy. The former Toffees and Manchester United star and TV personality have four sons: Kai, Klay, Kit and Cass.

‌



Their eldest, Kai, 16, is impressing for United's Under-18s after being awarded a scholarship this summer. His younger brother Klay, 13, is also on the books at Old Trafford.

‌



Eight-year-old Cass had been a regular at the The Blues' academy until recently. Appearing on the Therapy Crouch podcast alongside ex-Liverpool favourite Peter Crouch and his wife, model Abbey Clancy, Wayne and Coleen opened up about their son's devastation upon learning he had no immediate future at Everton.

‌



"The youngest one, he got let go," Coleen said. "That was the hardest thing. Because the older two had been there and stayed there at United, Cass was at Everton. It was only Under-7s and he is a massive Evertonian, so he's got a season ticket and he loves Everton. So, the fact that he was there was everything to him.

"We knew, because it was a big squad, and obviously, then going into the Under-9s, you get signed then. We knew he wasn't going to stay because he wasn't one of the stronger ones there and the day came when we got the phone call.

Wayne Rooney shows his true colours with response to Man City being stripped of titles READ MORE :

"I phoned him [Wayne] and I was like, 'You're going to have to tell him,' and then I had a moment before he [Wayne] came in and he [Cass] was on his own in the house.

‌



"I was like, 'Cass, I've had a call and you're not going to be going into the next [year at Everton]' and he threw his head into his hands and he just burst out crying. But an hour later? He forgot about it. He was fine. He still plays for his grassroots team and he was on the phone straight away to my mum and dad saying, 'Everton have released me.'"

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

When asked how the couple coped with their son's heartbreaking rejection from the Blues, Wayne said: "If you think about, anything really, even in school, you have people in higher sets, that's part of life isn't it?

‌



"In football, the amount of players we've played with (gestures to Crouch) who maybe don't make it at Man United, Everton or Liverpool, but then they go and play [Elsewhere], so there's opportunity to have a career.

3 View 3 Images Coleen and Wayne with their children in their home in Cheshire (Image: Instagram/Coleen Rooney) 3 View 3 Images Wayne Rooney and Coleen Rooney attend the UK Premiere of "The Real Rooneys" (Image: Mike Marsland/Getty Images for Disney+)

‌



"And you forget, they're so young. I said to him, 'I didn't join Everton's academy until I was nine, so actually you've got loads of time. Enjoy playing football and if it comes, it comes.'"

Wayne and Coleen have recently thrown open the doors of their family home, giving viewers an intimate glimpse into their day-to-day lives through the brand new Disney+ series, The Real Rooneys.

Widely regarded as one of the greatest players ever to represent both Everton and United, Wayne's remarkable tally of 253 goals for the Red Devils makes him the club's all-time leading scorer, though he has made clear his desire for his sons to forge their own paths in the game.

Article continues below

In the Disney-produced programme, the 40-year-old said: "Kai wants his own legacy, and I'll be there to support him. What I don't want is him to get a scholarship or get a contract because of me.

"I want it to be because of him in his own right. It's something he's wanted for a long time, so [I'll] be proud, really proud of him to get a scholarship."

Sports.title: Celebrity Traitors: 13 famous footballers we'd love to see take on iconic BBC show
Sports.content:
Fans of The Traitors will be elated to see the series return for its second celebrity edition on Thursday night. And despite the excitement buzzing over this year's cast, football fans far and wide might wonder whether we couldn't do just slightly better.

The Beautiful Game is no stranger to its own bit of cloak and dagger. And it's not unreasonable to think there are more than a few footballing figures who might excel sleuthing their way around the turret - as well as those who really wouldn't.

After all, half the fun stems from seeing those unaccustomed to lying flounder under pressure. Mirror Football has compiled a cast of football stars who would make for one stellar season of The Traitors, for one reason or another.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Erling Haaland

Don't let those boyish features fool you; beneath Erling Haaland's facade lies the instincts of a killer. Strictly in a goal-finishing sense, of course, as his three Premier League Golden Boots will attest.

Sir Chris Hoy wants to go on The Traitors as Olympic icon makes BBC admission READ MORE :

In addition to being one of the best strikers of his generation, the Manchester City marvel just seems like an all-round good time. No stranger to keeping a cool head in tense moments, one could see Haaland succeed as either a traitor or a faithful.

Declan Rice

If ever you needed someone to keep morale in the camp high after accidentally banishing a string of faithfuls, Declan Rice is your man. The Arsenal and England talisman is rarely seen without a smile on his face when he's not playing and would be a source of frivolity in the castle.

Fibbing doesn't seem like Rice's forte, meaning it may be a death sentence if he were named among the traitors. Not to mention an inexhaustible engine would undoubtedly come in handy raising funds when it comes to missions.

‌



Jimmy Bullard

View 4 Images Jimmy Bullard's second stint on I'm A Celebrity! ended in controversial circumstances (Image: Jonathan Hordle/ITV/Shutterstock)

You've seen him on I'm A Celeb (twice), Tipping Point and he's even had a stint on Celebrity Big Brother as a panellist. Jimmy Bullard only needs a trip to the Scottish Highlands to complete the UK competition show hat-trick.

Seeing the former Wigan and Fulham joker capitulate while attempting to lie his way out of a trator's corner would make for iconic TV. Then again, if Alan Carr can get away with the grand prize under inquisition, then nothing's impossible.

David Luiz

If David Luiz was even half as entertaining in the castle as he was during his Chelsea career, the BBC would be onto a winner. The ex-Brazil centre-back earned the nickname Sideshow Bob for a reason and there's no better show in Britain to show his split personality at its best.

‌



Currently playing for Cypriot side Pafos, we envision Luiz working best as a late recruit to the traitors' team. His signature grin would be priceless having proved himself as a faithful, only to turn on his former comrades at the last minute and snatch the prize fund for himself (or at least a charity of his choosing).

Thomas Muller

Another international joker of generational standards, Thomas Muller routinely provided the levity in an iconic Bayern Munich side that was otherwise all business. In those tense clashes where emotions can sometimes run high on The Traitors, the German would be on hand to remind his fellow competitors it was all just a game.

And then he'd steal in to reveal he was the grand deceiver all along. Muller would make for a classic misdirect, perceived as too nice to be able to lie his way to victory but cerebral enough to fool the rest of the cast.

Jermain Defoe

One of the Premier League's greatest strikers of all time but also your everyday man, Jermain Defoe would relate to the average viewer excellently. Not to mention one can see the ex-England poacher being a dab hand come task time.

‌



Full of great anecdotes, Defoe would also provide excellent value in those moments where the cast are simply milling around the castle. And there's one potential colleague in particular who'd make for a fabulous foil to the Tottenham legend.

Peter Crouch

View 4 Images Peter Crouch has turned from fan favourite footballer into a wonderful broadcasting personality (Image: Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

There would be no disguising Peter Crouch's chemistry with Defoe given their prolific partnerships over the years. While some members attempt to hide their connections with other participants to try and keep the scent off, everyone would know straight away just what links the former Spurs and Portsmouth duo entering the castle.

Just imagine awaiting the reveal of The Secret Traitor, only to see a cloaked, 6'7" figure lookimg down the hallways of the manor. The BBC might even have to open a skylight in the turret just to ensure Crouchy can take part in discussions.

‌



James Milner

As far as outside impressions go, there doesn't appear to be an insincere bone in James Milner's body. All the more reason to thrust him into an environment where lying is obligatory, depending on which side of the aisle he's allocated.

The Premier League's appearance record-holder is twiddling his fingers his fingers after hanging up his boots this year. And what better way to keep himself busy and disprove the 'Boring Milner' moniker than by showing it to the nation first-hand?

The major issue with any night-time Traitor meet-ups is the ex-Liverpool and Manchester City midfielder would likely be up for his morning jog around the grounds already.

Sol Campbell

The original Premier League traitor. Just imagine Sol Campbell coming into the castle given his history, being assigned as a faithful and then spending the rest of the season attempting to convince his fellow team he really was one of them.

‌



Having infamously swapped sides of the north London derby at his peak, Campbell would arrive with a reputation. But history aside, he's also a wonderfully whimsical character who would no doubt leave the rest of the cast bemused one more than one occasion.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic

Zlatan Ibrahimovic is almost a cheat answer to the question of which footballers would entertain on The Traitors. That being due to the fact there isn't an environment we can think of where the Swede wouldn't add supreme value.

A hearty breakfast of salmon and eggs over discussion about whom he thinks the only traitors are. The only risk would be he'd be so confident in his own abilities that he'd reveal his identity as a traitor, believing he could still win the show regardless.

We wouldn't put it past him, either.

‌



Mark Goldbridge

View 4 Images Watching Mark Goldbridge lose his rag with Zlatan Ibrahimovic for not securing him a shield would be a sight to behold (Image: YouTube/The United Stand)

The token entry of an influencer personality would provide no small amount of comedic value among the assortment of verified stars. And seeing YouTuber Mark Goldbridge interact among some of the biggest names in the sport would be well worth the watch.

Claudia Winkelman might struggle to keep her act together amid Goldbridge's complaints that he doesn't like to get wet, never mind wade in a fountain of faux blood. In the end, he'd probably still find some way to blame his exit on Manchester United's poor recruitment.

Michael Owen

It's Episode 12 of The Football Traitors. The four finalists stand huddled around a bonfire as they determine who among them is lying - and Michael Owen still doesn't know whether he's a faithful or a traitor.

‌



The former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Man United striker might succeed in accidentally bamboozling his rivals at all the right moments. And as a bonus, he could pilot the helicopter that ferries his fellow contenders into the loch in the final.

Ian Holloway

The man who once said he hoped Cristiano Ronaldo was "hung like a hamster" would need no introduction among British fans. Swindon Town manager Ian Holloway could even make for a great guest host in Winkelman's place, rocking up to breakfast with a new iconic quote each morning.

He may be less useful when it comes to the more physically demanding tasks that tend to pop up on the show. However, there'd be no man better suited to sniffing out deception among the ranks as he looked to lead a new crop of merry men to the top prize.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola warning fired as Real Madrid circle World Cup star
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola warning fired as Real Madrid circle World Cup star

The latest Liverpool news sees new signing Bradley Barcola given a verdict on his start to life at Anfield

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola signed for Liverpool this summer (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

The current lengthy international break has given Liverpool a chance to reflect on the season so far. The summer saw the Reds undergo a bout of surgery on their squad, which has led to a solid, if unspectacular, unbeaten start to the new campaign.

One of the areas addressed was the Reds’ attack. Andoni Iraola's star signing in the final third was Bradley Barcola, who joined from Paris Saint-Germain for £123 million.

It's been a slow start for the French winger so far, however, and a former French hero has given his verdict on what Barcola needs to do to win over the Anfield faithful. Elsewhere, Real Madrid are rumoured to be circling a former Liverpool star.

Thierry Henry fires Bradley Barcola warning

Arsenal and France icon Thierry Henry has warned it will take time for Barcola to settle at Anfield following his blockbuster move from Paris.

The Reds signed the France international at the end of the transfer window, but he has enjoyed an understated start to his Liverpool career so far. He has made five appearances, without registering a goal contribution.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“People forget that the tactic, the team and how you play matters,” Arsenal legend Henry told Betway. “It’s not always easy when you’re used to a certain system and a way of playing, where everybody knows what’s happening at any time.

“He just arrived in Liverpool, he doesn’t speak English, and it’s a different style of play with different intensity in the league. I had to deal with it the same way, and then that little switch happened and I was more comfortable.

"You start to speak English, you can joke around in the dressing room, you’re a bit less shy and people start to know what you’re about.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola of Liverpool (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

“It’s not an easy place to start, and he didn’t ask for his price tag, but it’s on his back. We all know that one-v-one, he is deadly, and he has pace. The only thing he needs to work on is his finishing, but that’s normal.

“If you see my finishing when I was 19 or 20 compared to the end of my career, it was so different. I became so much more sure about my game.

“With winning the Champions League back-to-back, playing for France, with the price tag and the quality that he has, people are not going to wait for him to become the finished article, so he’s going to have to deliver. “There is going to be a level of expectation, and sometimes he is a bit raw in his finishing, but he creates a hell of a lot.”

Former Reds star on Real Madrid radar

According to SPORT BILD, Real Madrid have declared an interest in ex-Liverpool defender Jarell Quansah. The England international joined the Bundesliga outfit for £30m in the summer of 2025.

The Warrington-born centre-back was subject to interest from Arsenal this summer, with the Gunners bidding £55m for the defender, who has a deal with Leverkusen until 2030. However, Arsenal eventually pivoted to Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa instead.

View 3 Images Jarell Quansah's future remains up in the air (Image: Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty Images)

According to BILD, Real are on the hunt for at least two new defenders next summer and so are watching the former Liverpool star with a keen eye. Should he move to the Spanish capital, he would follow Ibrahima Konate and Trent Alexander-Arnold as the third ex-Liverpool defender to move to Los Blancos in recent years.

Liverpool have also been linked with a move to bring Quansah back to Merseyside. Upon the initial sale, the Anfield hierarchy protected themselves by inserting a hefty £70m buy-back option into the centre-back's contract.

Article continues below

According to the agreed terms, Liverpool will only have to pay £52m to re-sign the player, but will have to exercise their option before June 15, 2027.

Sports.title: Morgan Gibbs-White speaks out after England call-up clip featuring his fiancee caused a stir
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White speaks out after England call-up clip featuring his fiancee caused a stir

Nottingham Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White was called up by England as a replacement for Cole Palmer after he was forced to pull out and a video of the midfielder then went viral

View 3 Images Morgan Gibbs-White has played for England twice during the international break (Image: Getty Images)

Morgan Gibbs-White has claimed his viral England call-up clip alongside his fiancee was just ‘banter’ after her Thomas Tuchel dig. The Nottingham Forest star was not initially included in the Three Lions’ squad for the first international break of the season.

‌



But he was eventually called-up as a replacement for Cole Palmer, who pulled out late on. A video of Gibbs-White leaving a family holiday, mouthing the words to a High School Musical song, went viral in the aftermath.

‌



And he has now spoken out and claimed it wasn’t too serious and she understood that he needed to consider his career.

‌



“It was just me and my missus having a bit of banter, we do it all the time,” the 26-year-old said. “We were just trying to make a bit of light out of a situation that was difficult for her and the kids, but she completely understood.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“She made light of it. We always do silly, stupid stuff like that, and it's just us being funny together, and in a good relationship.”

He added: “I got to the hotel around eight o'clock Dubai time and then two hours later got a text message. I spent more time on the plane than I did in Dubai. But playing for my country comes first, 100 per cent.

"There was no question in my mind. No debate whether to come. It's an honour to represent your country, whether it's for 10 minutes or sitting on the bench."

‌



The video was not the only drama that Gibbs-White’s fiancee Britney De Villiers was involved in. When he was initially left out, she took to Instagram to post a picture emphasising the fact that Gibbs-White is the only player in the Premier League who has created five plus chances in every game that he has played so far this term.

3 View 3 Images (Image: @britneydevilliers/TikTok) 3 View 3 Images (Image: @britneydevilliers/TikTok)

‌



Explaining Gibbs-White’s initial omission, England boss Tuchel said: “It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

"It's one thing to be nominated, but it's another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination."

Gibbs-White has so far earned eight caps for England since making his debut and has made brief cameos against both Spain and Czechia over the international break. He could make a further appearance at the weekend with the Three Lions set to take on Croatia in Rijeka.

Sports.title: Harry Kane gives verdict on Man City charges hours after explosive Premier League statement
Sports.content:
Harry Kane gives verdict on Man City charges hours after explosive Premier League statement

Three Man City players are part of the England squad for the current international break with the club having been found guilty of breaches of financial rules

View 2 Images Harry Kane has spoken about the Man City charges case (Image: Sky Sports Football/Youtube)

Harry Kane says that full concentration in the England squad is on their next Nations League game after the guilty verdict against Manchester City. The Premier League have confirmed that the club have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges for breaches of financial rules.

‌



City strongly deny the charges and are set to appeal the decision made by an independent panel. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the club could face severe punishment, including a heavy points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.

‌



Three City players, Marc Guehi, Nico O’Reilly and Elliot Anderson are part of the England squad for the current international break. Both Guehi and Anderson started Tuesday’s 2-0 win over Czechia, with O’Reilly missing the game through injury.

‌



Speaking after England’s win over Czechia, Kane, who scored the second goal of the game, revealed that there hadn’t been talk of the verdict in the England dressing room. “To be honest today I didn’t even know the news literally until after the game,” said the Three Lions skipper. “I’ve been off my phone all day.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I can’t comment on it now. I’m sure in the next days it will be spoken about in a casual way. I always say when we’re here we’re with England.

‌



“We have our England head on and those guys [Anderson, O'Reilly and Guehi] will deal with it obviously when they are back. From our point of view it is all about Croatia on Saturday.”

England manager Thomas Tuchel is taking a similar stance. When asked if he had to ‘look after’ the City players in the squad, he said: “I did not actually because I am just focused on everything we have to deal with here and to prepare the team. I did not talk to them about the issue and I will not comment on it.

“I think Marc today was absolutely excellent after a tough match against Spain. The reaction was on the highest level and Elliot Anderson had a good match as well.”

‌



View 2 Images Marc Guehi played for England just hours after Man City's guilty verdict was confirmed by the Premier League (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In the statement, released just a few hours before England’s match, the Premier League said: "The independent Commission found that Manchester City arranged ‘sham’ commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees.

‌



“The remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club. As part of the scheme, further ‘sham’ arrangements, funded by ADUG, were entered into to enable the club to record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred, as well as a ‘sham’ circular arrangement with Fordham, an entity that purchased the club’s players’ image rights, that was funded by ADUG.

"The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900 million during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules. The consequence of this, as the Commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators. “

Sports.title: Man City sponsor threatens Premier League with legal action as row escalates further
Sports.content:
Man City sponsor threatens Premier League with legal action as row escalates further

Manchester City are at the heart of the biggest scandal the Premier League has ever seen and one of their main sponsors has now released a scathing response following their guilty verdict

View 2 Images Man City's principle sponsors have issued a strong statement (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City’s principle sponsors Etihad Airways are set to seek legal advice in the aftermath of the Premier League’s landmark verdict. City were found guilty of 114 of 115 financial rule breaches they were accused of including inflated sponsorship agreements and revenue.

‌



They club continue to maintain their innocence and will also respond with an appeal. And sponsors Etihad have now spoken out on the scandal.

‌



The Middle Eastern airline say that they reject the Premier League’s findings that they have been involved in any dodgy commercial deals and have threatened legal action after ‘damaging implications’.

‌



A statement on Wednesday evening read: “Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements. The Premier League’s public communication of the Commission’s findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“At no time did the Premier League reach out to or engage with Etihad in the process associated with the Commission’s opinion. Etihad was therefore never given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions that may now be interpreted as reflecting adversely on the airline.

“Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly. The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision. The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented.

“We stand with the Club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the Commission’s conclusions through the processes available to it. Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests.”

‌



View 2 Images Etihad Airways have spoken out on Man City's charges (Image: Getty Images)

Etihad have sponsored Man City since 2009, with the club's stadium having been renamed as part of the deal, while they have been their front-of-shirt sponsor in that time. Their owners are of Abu Dhabi heritage - the same as City's owner Sheikh Mansour.

Etihad’s statement comes the same day that former City boss Pep Guardiola spoke out on the guilty verdict.

Article continues below

Taking to social media, he said: "I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran [Soriano] the players, staff, Enzo [Maresca] and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."
