Sports.title: 'Could be in the first round' - AJ plots 'spectacular' win over Fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua said he wants to deliver a "spectacular" victory over Tyson Fury as he predicted the blockbuster heavyweight clash could end with a first-round knockout.

The pair came face to face on Wednesday in London for the first time since the long-awaited all-British clash was confirmed for December 11 in Cardiff.

The fight between the pair of two-time world champions, which has been a decade in the making, appeared to be in danger of falling through amid a dispute over where it would take place, with Joshua and his promoter Eddie Hearn pushing for it to be in the United Kingdom.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best bits from the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference

Asked what the fight means to him, Joshua told Sky Sports News: "It meant a lot to me because of the fans. Bringing it to the UK meant a lot to me for the fans.

"And for me personally, as much as it is just another fight because I don't like to make too much of it - it's just what we do - it would be amazing to get the victory in spectacular fashion."

Joshua revealed that he wasn't necessarily willing to walk away from the fight if his push to have it staged in the UK had failed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury sits down to talk about the much-anticipated fight

He said: "I wanted to do everything I could to make it happen and part of that was it being in the UK and we got that so we're here, but I wasn't completely willing to walk away from it because it still needed to go ahead.

"You just listen to the cries and the conversation of those people who love boxing and love competition.

"People who wanted it to be in the UK would have still been happy that it happened, but I think getting it here is the cherry and icing and everything that needs to be on top of the cake."

AJ reveals knockout gameplan

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua come together in a face-off

Fury has been installed as an early favourite by bookmakers for the fight, with the fact Joshua has been floored in the opening round of two of his last three fights undoubtedly a factor.

Joshua admitted that he has "vulnerabilities" but insisted he is "hard to beat" and not considering retirement regardless of the outcome of the fight.

Asked where he feels like he's at as a boxer, Joshua replied: "Durable, hard to beat, can show vulnerabilities, but makes it exciting for the fans at home.

"There's more to come. The Anthony Joshua journey doesn't end here."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Moore, Barry Jones and Matthew Macklin debate who will win

On his opponent, Joshua added: "He performs to the level he's at as well, if I'm honest.

"He's versatile, and he's a good little mover around in the ring."

And as for what he expects to happen in the ring on December 11, Joshua said: "A knockout, if I'm honest with you. Could be in the first round."

Asked whether that's his gameplan, Joshua added: "Yeah, it is."

Sports.title: Price books Clayton showdown at World Grand Prix as Aspinall races through
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price set up an all-Welsh quarter-final showdown with Jonny Clayton with a straight-sets win over Ross Smith at the World Grand Prix, as Ryan Joyce and Nathan Aspinall also progressed in Leicester.

Price, among the tournament favourites after Luke Littler's shock early exit, followed his opening-round victory over Sebastian Białecki by dropping just four legs to despatch Smith at the Mattioli Arena.

The 2020 champion was outscored by Smith - having posted the highest average of the first round - but dropped just four legs during his 3-0 win, securing him a meeting with World Cup of Darts partner Clayton on Friday evening.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gerwyn Price set up an all-Welsh quarter-final at the World Grand Prix with Jonny Clayton, with the Ice Man boasting about his record against his compatriot

Clayton opened with three consecutive ton-plus checkouts and made four in total during a 3-1 victory over Wessel Nijman, where a 93.08 average and some remarkable finishing pushed him past the 12th seed.

Ryan Joyce breezed into the quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Danny Noppert, as Luke Woodhouse - who stunned Littler in the first round - was knocked out after losing 3-0 to Nathan Aspinall in a one-sided contest.

How Price and Clayton set up all-Welsh showdown

Price averaged 101.61 on Monday night but was over 10 points lower against Smith, where he recovered from being broken early with a 13-darter to match it in the next and then claim the opening set in a final-leg decider.

The world No 4 took out an 86 finish on his way to winning the second set and nailed an 80 checkout early in the third, where Smith took out 116 to break and extend the match before Price closed out victory on D18.

Image: Gerwyn Price and Ross Smith

"I don't think it was a great game and I don't think we played brilliant," Price admitted to Sky Sports. "What we did do in patches was start well and finish well, but the bits in between were a little bit rubbish.

"I know he [Clayton] is chasing a Grand Slam spot, so the pressure is on him. I think he got lucky first round - hopefully he doesn't get lucky in the next round!"

Clayton won the opening set in straight legs after three consecutive ton-plus finishes, immediately breaking with a 112 checkout, taking out 116 to hold throw and then nailing a 125 finish on the bullseye.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jonny Clayton sealed the first set against Wessel Nijman with a stunning 125 checkout, finishing in style on the bullseye

Nijman responded to Clayton pinching a leg with a 90 finish to take the second set in a final-leg decider, before 'The Ferret' regained the lead by starting the third with another bullseye finish to take out 126.

Clayton, who posted eight maximums alongside his impressive finishing, then reeled off four of the next six legs to reach the quarter-finals for a third consecutive year.

"My scoring was good but, to be fair, Wessel [Nijman] missed a few chances on doubles and he gave me a few chances," Clayton told Sky Sports. "The two bullseyes were good, the 126 was good and I have a big smile."

Sports.title: 'I find myself defending you!' - For how long will Fury-AJ stay friendly?
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua finally came face-to-face on Wednesday - but few could have predicted how their first press conference ahead of their blockbuster heavyweight clash would unfold.

Perhaps because of the uncertainty that has continued to surround the fight since it was announced, there was something of a surreal atmosphere in west London until the two biggest names in British boxing finally appeared on stage shortly after 6pm.

The whole thing suddenly felt very real, with the audible excitement of the relatively small number of fans who had been able to buy tickets to watch from the arena's upper tier clearly appreciated by both fighters.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua come together in a face-off ahead of their fight on December 11.

With the two-time world champions sat just a few feet apart, attention quickly turned to how they would interact after years of verbal sparring from a distance.

Joshua's measured persona made his approach easier to predict, but the wildcard was which version of Fury would show up.

Minute of silence sets respectful tone

After a lengthy introduction from master of ceremonies Max Kellerman, the American's questions about the fighters' sparring session - which took place in 2010, when Joshua was still an amateur - produced some light-hearted banter.

However, Joshua soon took control of the proceedings to pay tribute to several people in his life who had passed away, including Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele, who died in a car crash in Nigeria last December that Joshua survived.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Joshua makes his predictions for his fight against Tyson Fury on December 11.

Joshua requested a minute of silence which was impeccably observed by everyone in the arena, before applause at the end of it, which Fury warmly participated in.

Whether it had always been his intention or Joshua's words had influenced him, Fury then offered some extremely kind words about his rival.

"This man is a two-time heavyweight world champion, Olympic gold medallist, and he has been a role model and a poster boy for British boxing for years," Fury said.

"I mostly find myself defending my arch rival to fans I meet in the street. If you could achieve 10 per cent of what this man has achieved, you'd be doing well."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury sits down to talk about the much-anticipated fight with Anthony Joshua on December 11.

While there is little doubt tensions will rise and less friendly exchanges will follow between now and fight night, both fighters made it clear that there is a great deal of underlying respect between them, with no obvious personal malice.

That was further underlined when Fury invited Joshua to join him for a pint of Guinness in the pub after the fight, regardless of the result.

Joshua's humorous suspicion of the invitation, however, perhaps reflected his surprise at Fury's approach to the event. Was the master of mind games at it again?

'Too early for aggro'

Few are better qualified to analyse this event and everything around it than Britain's former undisputed heavyweight world champion Lennox Lewis, who was in attendance.

Lewis is adamant that once Fury and Joshua are deeper into their training camps, their exchanges will become less friendly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Joshua came up with the perfect response to Tyson Fury during their press conference ahead of their fight on December 11.

"It's too early, at this time [for aggro]," Lewis said. "You need to be in training camp and not see people for a couple of weeks.

"To be training hard and thinking about each other. Then when they see each other, it will be different, because everyone will be touchy at that point."

Fury also showed just how quickly he can switch from friendly to confrontational when responding to a video released by Joshua and his promoter, Eddie Hearn, before the fight was finalised. The video positioned Joshua as a 'landlord' coming to collect his money.

Fury suggested that the fact his name appears first on all the promotional material for the event proves he is the A-side of the fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury was quick to shut down any idea that Anthony Joshua is his 'landlord'!

"In the build-up to this fight, Eddie [Hearn] and AJ were talking about landlords, being the boss, being the 'guvnor', the rent man and all that," Fury said.

"When I look behind me, I only see one don and that's Fury vs AJ. Now you've come to get the rent and I ain't f****** paying because I'm No 1.

"I don't make a big thing about all that but we're going to walk out seeing Tyson Fury versus his opponent Anthony Joshua - an old dosser who works for me."

With several details still to be decided - including which fighter will walk to the ring first and be left waiting for his opponent - the battle of egos is only likely to intensify.

The start of a popularity contest?

While the result is ultimately all that will matter, it will be fascinating to see the receptions these two legends receive in the build-up to December 11 and right through to the opening bell.

If the first press conference was anything to go by, Fury and Joshua are set to receive a huge reception wherever they go between now and fight night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury reveals to AJ how he plans to beat him on December 11!

After the huge cheers that greeted both fighters as they arrived on stage, Fury's fans broke into his "get up" catchphrase, with Joshua playfully joining in and repeating it back to them.

It was also notable that there was little of the hostility often directed at one fighter by the other's supporters. Instead, the focus was firmly on backing their respective heroes.

Joshua remained on stage for at least 30 minutes after the press conference had finished, signing autographs and posing for photos with fans.

After protracted negotiations had left the British public tired of waiting, this ultimately felt like a day of celebration for everything the pair have achieved in setting up one of the biggest fights in the sport's history.

The question now is: how long will the feel-good factor last?

Sports.title: Somerset pair Overton and Luff win PCA awards
Sports.content:
Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff have won the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards in partnership with Toyota while emerging England stars Sonny Baker and Tilly Corteen-Coleman also received coveted honours at Exhibition White City.

Overton saw him collect a PCA awards quadruple, winning the PCA Men's Player of the Year trophy, the PCA Men's Domestic Overall MVP, the Rothesay County Championship Player of the Year and selection in the IG PCA Men's Team of the Year.

The 32-year-old, who has scored 951 runs, taken 76 wickets and 45 catches across all three formats this season, becomes the first Somerset player to secure the award since Nick Compton in 2012, beating competition from the notable shortlist of players including Joe Clarke, George Hill and Dan Lawrence.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Overton had to face the last balls of The Hundred match from his brother Jamie!

He also scored a memorable unbeaten 79 in the Vitality Blast quarter-finals to take Somerset to Finals Day.

"It's a phenomenal feeling. To be chosen by your peers to win this award is very special; it means so much to me," said Overton.

"To be able to put in consistent performances has made it a great year. My bowling ticked along and after I scored that hundred at Essex in the second game of the season my form with the bat carried on throughout the summer. The quarter-final against Yorkshire was where I felt like this year is the one where everything's going my way and everything clicked.

"I felt like I got in a groove where my body was in a good spot, not 100 per cent because of the schedule, but mentally I felt like I was in a great spot to be able to go out and perform when games come along near enough every other day."

Image: Sophie Luff emerged victorious from her peers to win the award against nominees Maia Bouchier, Sophia Dunkley and Mady Villiers

Somerset completed the double as their captain Luff also won the player-voted for award and becomes the first winner of the Toyota PCA Women's Player of the Year since Eve Jones won it in 2021 to not have played international cricket.

Impressing for her county all season and in The Hundred, which she won with Trent Rockets, Luff was also selected in the Metro Bank PCA Women's Team of the Year.

"It's super special people have voted for me after the performances and impact they feel I've had this year. It means that I'm doing things in the right way, and people think highly of you," said the 32-year-old, who scored more than 1,000 runs this summer.

"I've always been a leader that wants to lead from the front, but I think people are seeing that play out in games now. I think this year I've just showcased what I'm capable of."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sonny Baker became the first player to take five wickets in the final of the Vitality Blast Men as Hampshire fought back against Northamptonshire

The Toyota PCA Men's Young Player of the Year award went to Hampshire and England's Sonny Baker who was rewarded with a Test match debut, playing against New Zealand at the Kia Oval.

The 21-year-old took 10 international wickets, showing his prowess with six in IT20s and remarkably becomes the first Hampshire player to win this award since it was introduced in 1990.

Left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman enjoyed a year which saw her earn IT20 and ODI debuts for England, whilst impressing for Surrey and Southern Brave in The Hundred as she claimed the Toyota PCA Women's Young Player of the Year award.

Former England captain Heather Knight was announced as the PCA Outstanding Contribution Award winner for her incredible dedication to the game over a prolonged period.

The ECB announced the winner of their Special Merit Award, which was presented to former England batter Tammy Beaumont following her stellar international career.

Sports.title: Gill hits 223 not out as India chase down 406 to beat West Indies in second ODI
Sports.content:
A capacity crowd witnessed a host of batting records on Wednesday, Shubman Gill leading the way with 223 not out off 133 balls as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in their second ODI.

Gill notched his best ODI score and a record-high individual tally in an ODI run-chase. It was his 11th hundred in the format, one of five on the day, as India amassed 406-2 in 43.3 overs to take a winning 2-0 lead in the three-match series.

Opening partner Rohit Sharma made 101 as the duo put on 255 off 158 balls - the second-highest opening stand for India in ODIs.

It was the second successful 400-plus run-chase in ODI history, after South Africa's record 438-9 against Australia in 2006.

Sports.title: Building of the Pep supremacy is an era that will be defined by sham-ball
Sports.content:
“Do you know the question that you are asking me? Today, do you honestly think it is my job to make this kind of question happen …” Cut to the long, painful pause. Chuck in a deep, shaming stare, eyes that have suddenly become death rays of betrayal and disgust and Pep Guardiola himself transformed from a man cheerfully toasting his own FA Cup final victory to a grizzled chief detective addressing a room full of convicted perverts.

Guardiola had the wind entirely at his back at this point, sitting in the Wembley press room an hour after Manchester City’s 6-0 defeat of Watford in May 2019. Success drowns out every other noise in football. To be good is also to be good, noble, virtuous. History is written by the domestic treble winners. Right up until the moment it isn’t.

The question in question was asked by Rob Harris of the Associated Press. It was basically this: information is now in the public domain that suggests Roberto Mancini received a second salary from Abu Dhabi when he was City manager. Mancini was one of Guardiola’s immediate predecessors. So had he, Pep, ever received two salaries?

Even as Harris was asking this he was interrupted by City’s press officer, saying: “We’re not going here, we’re really just not going there.” A simple “no” would have done the job. Instead the exchange ended with another beautifully executed mad-dog stare from Guardiola; not angry, just sad and disappointed. But also, let’s be honest, really angry as well.

Fast forward to this week and a clip has been doing the rounds of the same Rob Harris, now of Sky News, and still the same perky, questing figure. Harris is approaching Ferran Soriano this time, Pep’s key man through that era, and asking the same entirely legitimate things, with a very different outcome. “The Premier League maintains you cheated for nearly a decade … is all this success, as the Premier League says, based on sham contracts?”

There is no glare in return now, no outrage, no flushed moral high ground. “Thank you, thank you,” Soriano mutters, with the look of a man caught shoplifting a Twix at the local primary school fete, followed by a mute, fumbling exit.

Sunlight. Scrutiny. Awkward questions from awkward people. It turns out these are still the best disinfectant. Just as it turns out “the question” was the only one worth asking in that room in 2019. Not that anyone agreed at the time. Predictably enough the comments on social media were about scum, bias, the press as a national embarrassment. Even other journalists held a perfumed kerchief to their noses, suggesting this was all a non-issue because, er, the club had just won a treble.

It turns out the exact opposite was true. It was entirely the right moment to ask this question. That Cup final win came at the end of the main period of shammery. It was in many ways its unholy coronation. There was an industrial-scale embarrassment in that room. But it wasn’t the person asking the questions.

View image in fullscreen The sports correspondent Rob Harris confronts Manchester City’s chief executive, Ferran Soriano, in Copenhagen. Photograph: Sky News

There is an obvious problem with the City story at this stage. It’s just too big. There is too much to say, an entire Dickensian multiverse interlayered with oddities and moments of jaw-drop. This is not, repeat not, a media story. And yet it kind of is a media story. After all, it was media scrutiny and the efforts of the hacker Rui Pinto that first winkled it out. As such, Harris deserves his moment of grace, living proof that it’s culturally vital to keep on asking questions, the same Rob Harris I have seen grilling Vladimir Putin about corruption on the hoof in Zurich, and also walking into a pillar at the World Cup in São Paulo while running off with his laptop to ask someone else something else, a man so deeply locked into the news cycle even reinforced stadium infrastructure doesn’t register.

It is also worth mentioning at moments like this Nick Harris, AKA Sporting Intelligence, who has kept going at this story relentlessly despite an unusual degree of abuse, harassment and threats, and who has every right to feel vindicated, part of a world where we can still hold power to account, where a cat can look at a king. But for now the real object of interest in this exchange is, of course, the person on the other end of it. Welcome to the stage once again Pep Guardiola, the public face of the club for the past decade.

What did Pep know? This is more than just football legacy chat. It relates to pretty much everything here, the true nature of the club, of elite football itself, and more basic things like truth, spectacle and human nature. Is believing the assurances of others any kind of defence, given Guardiola was in the perfect position to ask questions of his own? Is any kind of deniability plausible here?

The other significant statement from Guardiola in that time came after City’s two-year ban from the Champions League for a serious breach of Uefa’s financial fair play rules was overturned by the court of arbitration for sport. “We didn’t break the rules. We played the same rules as all the clubs in the Premier League,” was Guardiola’s conclusion, which seemed pretty silly at the time, given time-barring of offences was key to that decision. How does it look now?

To this day Guardiola’s stance remains slavish adherence to the promises of his paymasters, as evidenced by his first statement on the matter on Wednesday. Guardiola says he will be getting through the current unpleasantness with the club and its fans, sticking together as always. But were you together, really? Because City’s fans have some urgent questions of their own now. The majority believed what they were told, and put their faith in the “irrefutable body of evidence” schtick. That ring binder of truth really is going to have to do a lot of instant high-speed kung fu when it finally comes screeching into the appeal room on its trail bike. Not to mention explaining where it’s been over the past three years of information exchange.

Guardiola will face his own questions too, and on a level that will hurt him. The coach who only stays for three or four years stretched this out to a full decade at a club where 80% of that time was spent under a cloud of sham contracts and casual hubris. Through all this he had a deeply personal relationship with his chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak. The pair of them are seen whispering tenderly in the recent Prime documentary, in which Guardiola is presented as the most genuine and heartfelt of truth-seekers, a lone castaway on Integrity Island, Jedi-like in a tailored hoodie, eyes brimming with tears as he talks feelings and eternal truths, like a dad in the pub on Christmas Eve.

View image in fullscreen Kevin De Bruyne joined Manchester City from Wolfsburg for £51m in 2015. Photograph: Ash Allen/EPA

In his farewell hagiographies, Guardiola was routinely described as the greatest modern manager. He invented the Messi role for Messi. He reimagined the basic texture of the sport in this country. If this guy isn’t good, nobody’s good. On the other hand, the only logical conclusion on the facts as they stand is that all his City trophies were won with the benefit of concerted macro-cheating.

During the period embraced by the charges, City’s net spend on transfers was, according to Transfermarkt, almost £400m more than Manchester United in second place, and five times as much as Liverpool and Arsenal. From 2016 to 2018, the key period in building the Pep supremacy, they massively outspent every other team. After which they won the league on the final day or by a single point three times. There were little things throughout, like digging out an extra £25m for Kevin De Bruyne, stretching those fine details in your direction. How is it possible not to see that success as unrelated to stolen margins? This is an era that will now be defined by sham-ball, trophies hoisted with a hand behind your back and a thumb on the scale.

Pep can only double down now and ride this to the end. His life’s work, his vast and all-consuming reputation is at stake. “We will get through this together,” he says in Wednesday’s statement. Well, you have no choice now, Pep. Wherever that destination might be.

There are others who must now enter the matrix of who knew what. Soriano, subject of the second Harris grilling, is utterly bound up in this. He’s there right at the start, speaking to us in the leaked emails published by Der Spiegel. “We will need to fight this,” Soriano writes in one leaked memo, “and do it in a way that is not visible.” Hmm. How’s that part working out?

Soriano’s own pre-City past has already been sliced and diced by those who wish to see a pattern. For the record, and as a basic statement of fact, he was at Barcelona during the period when the alleged, unproved, time-barred refereeing scandal happened, but not implicated or punished. He was at Air Spain when it collapsed, but cleared of any wrongdoing. And now he’s been at City in the period of inflated income that has, in effect, left the club dangling over the edge of a cliff. It is certainly an unfortunate chain of coincidence.

Others who will be asked what they knew, or not asked because he’s not going to speak to you, include the owner, Sheikh Mansour. This has an added element. It speaks to the ultimate test, some way down the line, of fitness to run a football club. How is it possible to spend so much family money on this thing, to dole out what are in effect government contracts, and not know the actual process here?

But let’s face it, we all knew really. Weren’t the sham dealings obvious? It was there even in the absence of furious statements of support from the independent directors at First Abu Dhabi Bank, Etihad Airways, Experience Abu Dhabi, Emirates Palace Hotel in Abu Dhabi, Aldar Properties of Abu Dhabi, Masdar Energy of Abu Dhabi, e& telecoms of Abu Dhabi. Come on, chaps. Stand up for the investment. No word either from Dude Wipes, the club’s official male-oriented toilet-paper partner. Although who knows, we may now be entering full Dude Wipes territory.

We knew about the sportswashing aspect, knew that City was a soft-power vehicle for the state of Abu Dhabi, which has a record of alleged – and of course denied – human rights abuses and so on. And of course City’s fans must have known this too, or felt it on some level. It was there cooked into the blueprint, the sense of something brutally high-end but strangely cold.

JG Ballard coined the phrase “the death of affect” to describe the institutionalising of public feeling, rage and triumph commodified as a spectator event. Some champion teams have a strut. City’s basic vibe was always closer to an unceasing V-sign. Perhaps there was even a buried unease here. No one really enjoys being treated as a glove puppet, even when it is done gently and with a hand held discreetly under the desk. On which note, Pep? Any other questions now? Is this a good time?

Sports.title: Rival clubs feel relegating Manchester City to Championship would not be enough
Sports.content:
The Premier League will face pressure from Manchester City’s rivals to push for a sanction that will result in a prolonged absence from the top flight after the club were found guilty of more than 100 charges of financial rule-breaking.

Executives at a number of Premier League clubs have told the Guardian that a points deduction that would relegate City to the Championship for a single season would be insufficient given the scale of what an independent commission described as the club’s “disguised funding scheme” and “sham commercial deals”, which enabled them to artificially inflate their income by £900m between 2009 and 2018.

While the clubs have no involvement in the sanctioning process, the extent of their ill-feeling towards City illustrates the difficulties facing the Premier League as it seeks to conclude a case it began investigating almost eight years ago.

The same independent commission that found City guilty of the vast majority of 115 rule breaches will determine their fate at a sanctions hearing pending the outcome of the club’s appeal, which will be heard by a newly convened independent panel.

Under new Premier League rules introduced this season, the appeal hearing must be concluded within 12 weeks of the deadline on Friday for it to be submitted, with the panel given a further 30 days to deliver its judgment, meaning a decision should be reached by the end of January next year.

While not confirmed, the sanctions hearing could take place concurrently during the same time period, although it will not be published pending the outcome of the appeal. City could also subsequently appeal against the sanctions imposed by the commission.

It is also possible that the club could delay the process further by arguing that the Premier League’s new expedited timescales should not apply given they were only introduced this season, whereas the charges against them are historic.

The club has already succeeded in delaying the publication of the commission’s “core decision”, which was finally released on Tuesday following an appeal procedure.

As prosecutor, the Premier League is permitted to petition for its preferred punishment at the sanctions hearing, with City also pleading their case, before a decision is taken by the commission.

The Premier League’s position on sanctioning will be taken independently of the clubs by the board of directors comprising the chair, Alison Brittain, the chief executive, Richard Masters, and three independent non-executive directors: Mai Fyfield, Dharmash Mistry and Matthew Ryder KC.

View image in fullscreen Sheikh Mansour (centre) and Khaldoon al-Mubarak (right) have been Manchester City’s owner and chair respectively for the whole period covered by the rule breaches. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

The commission has a wide range of sanctions at its disposal including points deductions, transfer embargos and expulsion from the Premier League. Given the scale of City’s offences, according to the independent panel, there are no comparable precedents. City say they are “innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case”.

In the first successful profitability and sustainability rules prosecution, of Everton three years ago for a £19.5m overspend, the Premier League pushed for the club to be docked 12 points in the sanctioning hearing, with the independent commission ultimately docking them 10 points, which was reduced to six on appeal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Many of the clubs are calling for a far more severe punishment for City given the commission’s conclusion that without the hugely inflated income they would have breached Premier League and Uefa spending limits in multiple seasons, and will also lobby to ensure that the whole process is concluded before the end of the season.

“Relegation to the Championship for one season would be insufficient,” a club source told the Guardian. “The commission has to arrive at a punishment that is proportionate for years of sustained and deliberate cheating, as well as providing a strong deterrent to it happening again.”

The Premier League is in a difficult position, as it is also eager to prevent further mass litigation against City by rivals seeking financial recompense. Burnley were awarded £35m at an arbitration hearing earlier this year after suing Everton on the back of their PSR breach, which they claimed led to their relegation at the end of the 2021-22 season, a decision that has set a precedent for clubs claiming compensation following regulatory offences.

Manchester United, Arsenal, Tottenham and Liverpool all reserved their rights to sue City in the event of a guilty verdict two years ago, and have already held informal conversations about whether to pursue a claim now the judgment has been published. While those clubs will all arrive at individual decisions, the extent of City’s punishment could prove critical to their thinking.

Many of the top-flight clubs remain unhappy with the Premier League’s decision to reach an agreed sanction this year with Chelsea of a £10m fine after they self-reported the previous owners making unlawful payments to players and agents during the Roman Abramovich era.

Sports.title: Manchester City whistleblower Rui Pinto no longer a protected witness in Portugal
Sports.content:
Rui Pinto, whose leaks of private documents helped to trigger the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City’s financial affairs, will no longer be protected as a witness by the Portuguese authorities, it can be revealed. The removal of the whistleblower’s protection was decided on Wednesday, according to documents seen by the Guardian.

Pinto has also been advised to “exercise caution with family contacts” and avoid social media. The 37-year-old, who is the man behind the website Football Leaks, has been a protected witness since 2020, after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest.

The Portuguese police have deemed the risk to Pinto’s safety to be low, despite an assault on him in Lisbon in April and the ongoing fallout from the City investigation. It is understood that Pinto was left with a bruised eyebrow after the incident and the police were informed, although no complaint was filed.

Pinto was handed a suspended four-year sentence in September 2023 after being found guilty on counts of attempted extortion, illegal access to data and breach of correspondence. But he has been hailed as a hero by some supporters for exposing millions of confidential documents linked to some of the biggest clubs, players and organisations in world football. That included providing information concerning City’s finances, which was passed to the German publication Der Spiegel and its partners in the European Investigative Collaborations network and led to Uefa and the Premier League opening separate investigations.

While City eventually overturned their Champions League ban via the court of arbitration for sport, they were found guilty of 114 charges spanning nine seasons by the Premier League on Tuesday having been accused of disguising over £900m in funding through sham commercial contracts and false accounting. The deadline for City to appeal is on Friday.

Pinto has been heavily active on social media since reports that City had been found guilty emerged last week. He described it as a “historic decision for English football” and took aim at City’s executives in another post, who he said had “acted with complete impunity, challenging everyone and everything”, saying: “From the very beginning, they have demonstrated a complete lack of respect for the rules, for the bodies responsible for overseeing and regulating the game, for the integrity of the competition, for the other clubs and, above all, for the fans. Years and years of cheating, lying and manipulation will finally have consequences.”

Hours before confirmation that he will no longer be a protected witness emerged, Pinto also accused the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, of having done “everything in his power” to ensure that City and Paris Saint-Germain would only be fined for contravening Uefa’s FFP rules when he was general secretary at European football’s governing body.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo walks out on Portugal after being dropped from starting lineup
Sports.content:
The Portugal captain, Cristiano Ronaldo, announced on Wednesday that he had left the team’s training camp in Denmark after head coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the iconic striker would not start their next match.

Ronaldo had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus’s press conference. The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday’s Nations League clash away to Denmark either.

“Following the national team coach’s press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram. “In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

“Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates, without exception.”

Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side’s Nations League win over Norway.

Following the 2-1 victory in Oslo, Ronaldo went straight to the changing rooms without joining his teammates in acknowledging the Portuguese supporters in the stands. “There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus told reporters.

“Any player – and I was a player myself … when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on … no one is happy about that,” Jesus said on Wednesday.

The Portuguese coach added that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he would not be in the starting lineup, but that he might bring him on towards the end of the game.

“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about,” Jesus insisted. The former Benfica manager also explained that Ronaldo had not refused to train on Tuesday, as some Portuguese media outlets had suggested, but that he had had to do individual exercises for physical “mobility” and “strengthening”.

Jesus had said that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would train as normal on Wednesday. However, despite arriving at the stadium in the team bus, Ronaldo did not join his teammates on the pitch. Portuguese media shared a video of him leaving Parken alongside two members of the backroom staff just after Jesus’s press conference. Reports also said that Ronaldo’s private jet was heading to Copenhagen. Just before Ronaldo’s social media post, the Portuguese federation had released a brief statement merely confirming that the former Real Madrid, Manchester United and Juventus player had not trained.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Jesus had said earlier that for the Denmark match he again intended to start the Milan striker Gonçalo Ramos, who scored the winner against Norway.

“If everything goes according to plan, it will be Gonçalo who plays,” he said, before adding regarding Ronaldo: “If I need him, he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t.”

At 41, Ronaldo announced this summer that this season would “probably [be] my last year in football”. He is Portugal’s leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.

Sports.title: Leah Williamson blunder gifts Paris FC a point as Arsenal’s struggles continue
Sports.content:
Renée Slegers did not attend the post‑match press conference, the manager understood to have been too furious after Arsenal threw away a two-goal lead in their draw with Paris FC on Wednesday night.

The assistant coach Aaron D’Antino stepped in to speak to the media instead of Slegers, after a disastrous mix-up between the goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez and the centre-back Leah Williamson gifted Paris FC a penalty that Maeline Mendy converted to deny Arsenal all three points in the Champions League.

“The most frustrating part is how much we are working behind the scenes to try and turn this around, and it is just not going our way at the moment,” D’Antino said.

Alessia Russo and Georgia Stanway had given the Gunners a two-goal lead but Clara Mateo pulled one back before Williamson handled the ball after the referee deemed play to have restarted from a goal-kick when Rodríguez passed it to her.

D’Antino said: “If we’re looking at what we can control, it’s just passing the ball to Leah. From what I remember seeing, the ball was still rolling and she was moving it to Leah for her to take the goal-kicks as we normally do. So maybe the learning in that is how we get the ball to Leah, so we don’t put ourselves in that situation. But as far as we’re concerned, that’s not a penalty … we haven’t taken a goal-kick, there’s no advantage gained by Leah stopping the ball.”

It has been a tough start to the season for Arsenal, who are up against it in the title race with only five points from their opening four games, and the closing stages of the match in Paris delivered another gut punch.

Quick Guide WCL roundup: Barcelona win big again Show Barcelona continued their emphatic start to their title defence by brushing aside Roma 6-0 in the Italian capital. Caroline Graham Hansen got Barça off the mark in Rome inside 20 minutes. A Shukurat Oladipo own goal put them two up before the break and Clàudia Pina (pictured) made the points safe just after, before Graham Hansen and Pina both got their second goals and Ewa Pajor put the cherry on the cake late on. Bayern Munich, who gave up a two-goal lead last week to draw with Manchester City, were in danger of behind held again at Benfica, but won 3-0 thanks to three goals from in the last 16 minutes from Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder and Franziska Kett. Juventus downed Häcken 3-0 in Sweden to make up for last Tuesday’s defeat by Benfica. The Spanish World Cup winner Alba Redondo scored again, making it three goals in as many games and seven in 12 in all competitions since joining from Real Madrid. AFP Photograph: Domenico Cippitelli/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Paris FC had promised another tricky test, with teams that are happy to concede possession frustrating an Arsenal side that just cannot seem to find their way through low blocks. Chelsea had read that script on Sunday: they were organised at the back and punished Arsenal’s profligacy and failure to make their early dominance count.

At the Stade Jean-Bouin, which sits in the shadow of Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, the story was familiar. As a result, it was less a wave of relief that swept through the pocket of travelling Arsenal fans and the players when their first goal went in and more a tsunami. It had looked as if Arsenal’s hesitancy had cost them a possible opening again when Stanway prodded the ball towards Russo but the England forward took several touches to create the space to shoot before firing her low effort in.

With the home team forced to come out more, that it took only five minutes after the restart for Arsenal to double their lead was no surprise. It was a stylish finish from Stanway that gave Arsenal breathing space, the midfielder pushed Emily Fox’s cross forward a little with her chest before lashing a volley in from close range.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway is embraced after scoring Arsenal’s second goal before their evening took a turn for the worse. Photograph: Catherine Steenkeste/Reuters

However, only 22 minutes of comfort followed, before the team that inflicted a shock win on penalties to knock Arsenal out of qualifying in 2023 pulled the goal back that would test the Gunners’ resolve.

It was a mix-up between the centre-backs Lotte Wubben-Moy and Williamson that delivered the goal. The pair both moved to close down Evelyne Viens and the Canadian forward slipped the ball wide to Clara Mateo who raced free, rounded Rodríguez and slotted into the empty net.

It was tense as the clock ticked down. Paris posed a threat throughout, but the leveller followed the most calamitous of mistakes by Arsenal. Rodríguez collected the ball for a goal-kick, rolled it on to the pitch and then passed it to Williamson who bent and stopped the ball with her hand. The referee’s whistle went and she pointed to the spot, with Rodríguez deemed to have taken the goal-kick while Williamson clearly assumed she was being given the ball to take it. VAR did not intervene and Mendy converted from the spot, driving powerfully into the bottom corner.

It was a bruising end to another bruising game for Arsenal, who really need some luck to go their way to lift the increasing pressure. Meanwhile, Slegers’s decision to avoid talking after the game will have only ramped that pressure up further ahead of a must-win game against league leaders Manchester City on Sunday.

Sports.title: Hampton’s heroics preserve WCL point for Chelsea on Bompastor’s OL Lyonnes return
Sports.content:
There were plenty of encouraging signs for Chelsea as they claimed a valuable point in the Champions League on their head coach Sonia Bompastor’s return to face her former team OL Lyonnes.

The goalless draw was a slow-burner but concluded with a flurry of late action where both teams missed chances to steal the points. However a draw felt fair on a night when Chelsea’s double pivot of Keira Walsh and Lexi Potter in midfield continued to flourish, three days after they similarly impressed in Sunday’s victory over Arsenal.

OL Lyonnes had scored eight times in their first fixture in the league phase, away against the Swiss side Servette, but Chelsea looked comfortable for large periods and Bompastor said: “I’m really proud of my team, being able to not concede here. We are happy also with the ball, the way we performed, we were able to exploit different spaces. The only thing that was missing was the goal.”

The French side had scored at least seven times in all four matches they had played in all competitions this season. Given that formidable form and the confidence in the hosts’ front line, Chelsea were grateful to Hannah Hampton for her sharp save from Salma Paralluelo on 20 minutes, and similarly glad to see Melchie Dumornay’s powerful effort fizz just wide of a post a few minutes later.

Chelsea had the majority of the ball, however. Potter, buoyed by the receipt of her first senior England call-up on Tuesday, gave as good as she got in the physical battle in midfield and generally appeared at home on this stage, at the record eight-time European champions, which will have been pleasing for Sarina Wiegman. The 20-year-old, alongside her compatriot Walsh, helped Chelsea maintain an element of control.

Unlike Chelsea, who played a fiery derby against Arsenal in England, the top French sides were able to rest at the weekend, in between the first two European fixtures, as the French league helps its sides stay fresh for the Champions League. Other French top-tier sides played in the League Cup instead. It was therefore reasonable to assume that Lyonnes might look the stronger as this contest went on. That was true to a degree, as Chelsea – missing Katie McCabe through illness – tired slightly late on.

Quick Guide WCL roundup: Barcelona win big again Show Barcelona continued their emphatic start to their title defence by brushing aside Roma 6-0 in the Italian capital. Caroline Graham Hansen got Barça off the mark in Rome inside 20 minutes. A Shukurat Oladipo own goal put them two up before the break and Clàudia Pina (pictured) made the points safe just after, before Graham Hansen and Pina both got their second goals and Ewa Pajor put the cherry on the cake late on. Bayern Munich, who gave up a two-goal lead last week to draw with Manchester City, were in danger of behind held again at Benfica, but won 3-0 thanks to three goals from in the last 16 minutes from Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder and Franziska Kett. Juventus downed Häcken 3-0 in Sweden to make up for last Tuesday’s defeat by Benfica. The Spanish World Cup winner Alba Redondo scored again, making it three goals in as many games and seven in 12 in all competitions since joining from Real Madrid. AFP Photograph: Domenico Cippitelli/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

It was Chelsea, however, who started the second period the brighter. They thought they deserved a penalty when Tarciane took out Sjoeke Nüsken at the far post, just as the Chelsea midfielder looked certain to score, but after a check on the monitor, the referee concluded that Lucy Bronze had been interfering with play from an offside position as the ball was crossed. Tarciane was booked for her challenge, nonetheless.

Bompastor, who won this competition as a player and a manager with Lyonnes, brought on Lauren James to give her side a different forward dynamic with just over half an hour remaining, while Lyonnes introduced a former Ballon d’Or winner in Ada Hegerberg, but neither side looked likely to break the deadlock until much later, as the off-the-ball qualities of both teams appeared to cancel each other out. A cautious approach, from Chelsea in particular, was understandable; this was, by a significant distance, the toughest-looking fixture of their league-phase matches, against last season’s runners-up.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s Lexi Potter impressed on the big stage after her first England call-up. Photograph: Alexandre Dimou/Reuters

Lyonnes, owned by the London City Lionesses and Washington Spirit owner, Michele Kang, have high ambitions to win this title this term. They thought they had scored on 72 minutes, when Paralluelo struck a low shot into the bottom corner, but the offside flag was raised.

Just a few minutes later, a moment of real controversy arose, as Chelsea were awarded a penalty for a foul by Damaris Egurrola on James. After a video review, the decision was overturned with the referee appearing to conclude that James had made contact with Egurrola rather than the other way around. The Lyonnes midfielder, though, looked very fortunate to escape, having mistimed her tackle and also missed the ball completely. Chelsea were exasperated. Bompastor said later that she felt it was a “clear penalty”.

James had Chelsea’s best chance late on but her close-range strike was blocked by Mala Grohs in goal, before Hampton saved superbly from Hegerberg at the other end, as the match finally came to life in the very late stages and Maika Hamano dragged a shot wide deep into stoppage time. But Chelsea will be satisfied with this point.

Sports.title: ‘I like him as a No 9’: Bellingham a striking alternative for England, says Tuchel
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel’s hunt for alternatives to Harry Kane has led to him identifying Jude Bellingham as an option at No 9 for England. Kane continued his remarkable scoring record in the 2-0 win against Czechia in the Nations League on Tuesday, moving to 87 goals in 123 international appearances with a late strike in Prague, but he has little cover up front.

There is no prospect yet of Tuchel having to consider life without Kane. The England head coach backed the 33-year-old striker to last another decade at the highest level, tipped him to reach a century of international goals soon, and said England cannot expect to produce a replica of their greatest forward. However, there is concern over whether England have enough depth in attack.

Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney have been overlooked for this camp. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who came on for Kane during the defeat by Spain on Saturday, is 29 and has four goals in 13 caps. Liam Delap, the 23-year-old Nottingham Forest forward, is yet to earn a senior call-up and it was noted that Bellingham led the line after coming on for Kane in the closing stages against Czechia.

“You will not get another Harry Kane, first of all,” Tuchel said. “We look for different solutions. We finished the game with Jude as a No 9. There will be someone else but it will not be Harry or a copy of Harry. We will find a solution when it comes to it but maybe not me. It might be another 10 years.”

Bellingham wore the captain’s armband after coming off the bench in Prague on Tuesday. “I like him as a [No] 9,” Tuchel said. “Then he can contribute to both sides and overloads the sides and doesn’t affect so much of the balance. We found a bit of a new role for him in the last match, as a central [No] 10, so he can go to both sides and it is more of a 4-2-3-1 than a 4-3-3 to have Harry and Jude closer together and to give them a chance to overload both sides.

“We are working on that. Jude in general should always be able to go through the last line and be able to end up in the box. He is a natural goalscorer and has the hunger to be on the scoreboard. He wants to have the decisive action so it makes not a huge difference if he plays as a [No] 9 or a [No] 10.”

England moved second in Nations League Group A3 after seeing off Czechia, who were reduced to 10 men midway through the first half. Anthony Gordon opened the scoring and Kane finished well late on.

“The ball falls down and you see Harry taking the shot and that is exactly the player you want it to drop down to,” Tuchel said. “He does it in every single match. The highest level of finishing.”

Tuchel was the manager who took Kane to Bayern Munich in 2023. Uli Hoeness, Bayern’s honorary president, has since said the former Tottenham striker is the club’s greatest signing. “That is so beautiful as it tells me everyone can see his true value and his personality,” Tuchel said. “It is not easy to change and to come to Bayern Munich when you win, win, win and it is a big club. You are under the spotlight and he won everyone over.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

England’s next assignment is a trip to Rijeka to face Croatia on Saturday. It remains to be seen if Tuchel sticks with Trent Alexander-Arnold after the right-back marked his first international appearance since June 2025 by creating Gordon’s goal.

“Trent’s outstanding,” Kane said. “The delivery, the passing range, the crossing but also today defensively he was outstanding. He’s a fantastic player. Trent just has to keep his head down, keep working hard. He’s been great in camp so far. He’s showing to the boss that he wants to be here.”

Sports.title: Craig Bellamy urges Wales improvement but wary of Norway’s threat
Sports.content:
Craig Bellamy has said Wales must improve against Norway on Thursday after appearing unrecognisable in their defeat against Denmark, and highlighted their next opponents’ run to the World Cup quarter-finals as proof of their talent.

Wales host Norway in Cardiff hoping to record their first win since last November and their first since promotion to Nations League A. “This team has been on a surge,” he said of Ståle Solbakken’s side. “They are progressing and they will keep going as well – they ain’t going away, especially with the youngsters they’ve got coming through. We’ve all been waiting [for them to flourish]. But it was coming and it’s come with a bang.”

Bellamy said Norway having two teams in the Champions League – Bodø/Glimt and Viking – would have been a “miracle a number of years ago”. Addressing the Norwegian media at his pre-match press conference on Wednesday, Bellamy said: “I think you’re all sneakily hoping we don’t talk about you as much but the World Cup exposes you. But I’m on to yous. I know what you’re up to and I know your younger age groups are getting even stronger.

“Sander [Berge], [Martin] Ødegaard and [Erling] Haaland, they are really close friends and their three sons are all the same age, born within a few months of each other. They’re already preparing the next generation, so we’re all in trouble.”

Addressing Wales’s 2-0 defeat in Copenhagen on Sunday, Bellamy said: “I didn’t recognise anything about us in the game and that was hard. We didn’t look clear in what we were doing, we were ‘in between’ and that comes from myself. I want us to improve as a team and I want to improve.”

Meanwhile, the Brentford defender Kristoffer Ajer insisted Haaland has displayed the same personality as normal amid the noise surrounding Manchester City after the club were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-year period. “Ever since I met him he’s been a guy that brings a lot of energy and joy to the group and that’s the biggest compliment I always give Erling,” Ajer said.

“When people ask about him, he hasn’t changed one bit since the first time I met him, even though he’s the biggest star on the planet right now. He’s been exactly the same the last few days as well, which is not a surprise for me.”

Solbakken, Norway’s head coach for the past six years, said “everything’s fine” with Haaland, who has scored three goals in his past two matches, and played down the idea that the City verdict has been a distraction. “[He’s been] very good, scoring goals,” Solbakken said.

“He missed one chance against Portugal that he usually doesn’t miss and that’s the only thing I can say negative, because he’s on fire.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bellamy said he did not expect Haaland to be bothered by his club’s situation at Cardiff City Stadium. The Wales head coach said: “I don’t think he’ll be distracted, the guy’s a machine. Have you seen his record at international level? He’s brilliant. If you love football, you have to appreciate him … You see certain moments in certain sports. Remember the Jonah Lomu factor [in rugby union]? We’re coming through the Haaland factor at this present moment.”

Ødegaard is a doubt for the game on Thursday after a poor challenge by Bernardo Silva in the 2-1 defeat by Portugal on Sunday. “He will probably test himself a bit today,” Solbakken said of the Arsenal and Norway captain before training in the Welsh capital. “If he had no chance [of playing], he wouldn’t be here.”

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal player Mohamed Elneny joins bottom-of-the-table club on free transfer
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal man Mohamed Elneny has joined Greek Super League club Levadiakos, who are rock bottom of the division.

The Egyptian international was a free agent after leaving UAE club Al Jazira in the summer, and he's now looking to try and save his new side from the drop.



3 Elneny was a very loyal servant at Arsenal, not often getting a lot of game time but filling in whenever needed Credit: Getty

Levadiakos have started the season with one draw and four defeats.

They are yet to score a goal and have conceded nine, but Elneny is confident he can make a difference.

In a message to the fans, he said: “Hello everyone, I have signed with Greek club Levadiakos. I am very happy to start my career here.

“I hope things go well. I will give my best for this team. Levadiakos fans, I’ll see you in the next match. I am very excited to start my career with the club.”



It will be a bit different to playing at the Emirates Stadium in front of 60,000 people as Levadiakos' stadium holds a capacity of jusy 5,900.

The good news for Elneny and his new teammates is that they have already played Greek big hitters PAOK, Olympiakos and Panathinaikos as well.



New career path for Elneny

Elneny has never been afraid to try different leagues and test himself at various levels.

The 34-year-old has been in Switzerland, Egypt, England, Turkey and Abu Dhabi.



And now, he's in Greece but not with one of the major sides and instead a team battling relegation and looking to try and survive.

It is a far cry from winning the FA Cup with Arsenal in 2019 under Mikel Arteta.

3 Elneny spent eight-and-a-half years in north London Credit: Getty

During his eight-year spell at Arsenal, Elneny only made 161 appearances but Arteta always praised the Egyptian for his character and work rate.



The duo even played together near the end of the Spaniard's playing days in north London.

But the feeling was very much mutual as Elneny said when leaving Arsenal in 2024: "Everyone made me feel welcome but there were two people in particular who went out of their way to make me feel at home.

"The first was Arsene Wenger, the day I arrived at the training ground, and the second? Mikel Arteta.

"As soon as I came onto the pitch he was talking to me and, after, we would go for lunch, and in the dressing room he was talking to me, all through my first few days here.



"What Mikel also did was talk to my agent and tell him I was a good player because he knew my agent was going to tell me. And it made me happy. I think things like that, which seem to be part of the Arsenal DNA, are incredible."

3 Arteta and Elneny played two games together before the Spaniard managed him for four-and-a-half years Credit: Getty

And it seems Elneny predicted Arteta's success, as he said: "We're really together and we do everything together.

"I love Mikel's ideas, for sure, because he always wants us to be together, with him as well.



"Mikel for me is a genius because he made this connection between the players, and him, and the club, and the fans, all of us together. I think it's something really magical - because you have to do magic to do this. I swear, the fans feel like they are one of us.

"They're not apart from us. They come to the stadium happy and you can see how much they are behind the team - when we are away you see how many people come. We are lucky to have these fans behind us."

Sports.title: Major Man City sponsor threatens to join club’s fight against the Premier League
Sports.content:
Manchester City sponsor, Etihad Airways, has threatened legal action against the Premier League after the club was found guilty of all financial breaches.

The Premier League announced on Tuesday that City had been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges against them.

3 Manchester City's 61,000-capacity stadium is named after Etihad Airlines Credit: PA

In an explosive verdict, the Premier League stated that the club had disguised funding of more than £900million via a series of commercial deals between 2009 and 2018.

During this period, City won eight trophies, including three Premier League titles.

The ruling by an independent panel found City guilty of inflating their revenue by around £900 million through 'sham' contracts with sponsors, which were funded by the club's owners.

While Etihad weren't named in the judgement, it is the long-standing sponsor of City’s stadium, kit and training centre in a relationship with the club that stretches back to 2009.

talkSPORT understands the club are set to appeal against the ruling, having been given until Friday to respond to the verdict.

Etihad responds in explosive statement

In the wake of the Premier League's verdict, Etihad have now hit out at the English top-flight for suggesting they are implicated in the inflated 'sham' sponsorship deals.

The Abu Dhabi airline said that 'at no time' did the Premier League engage with them during the process, and claimed they were never given a right of reply or a chance to ‘provide relevant information.

It slammed the Premier League for having 'created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings'.

An Etihad spokesperson said: "Etihad categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements.

"The Premier League’s public communication of the Commission’s findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings.

3 Etihad has been Man City's main shirt sponsor since 2009 Credit: Getty

They added: "At no time did the Premier League reach out to or engage with Etihad in the process associated with the Commission’s opinion.

"Etihad was therefore never given the opportunity by the Premier League to be represented, to provide relevant information, or to ensure the accuracy and fairness of information relied upon in reaching conclusions that may now be interpreted as reflecting adversely on the airline."

The statement continued: "Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly.

"The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision.

"The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented."

Etihad went on to reveal they are now considering legal action against the Premier League in light of their statement.

3 The legitimacy of Manchester City's dominant era between 2009 and 2018 has now been called into question Credit: Getty

In the same breath, the spokesperson reaffirmed the airline's support of Man City throughout the ongoing process.

The statement finished: "We stand with the Club, its supporters and our wider Etihad community as Manchester City challenges the Commission’s conclusions through the processes available to it.

"Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests."

It remains to be seen how Man City will be punished for their numerous financial breaches, with possibilities ranging from points deductions, transfer bans and even possible relegation.

City, who won three Premier League titles, three League Cups, one FA Cup and one Community Shield during the period in question, could even be stripped of their titles.

The Premier League's official statement comes just two days after Oasis legend Liam Gallagher leaked what his beloved side's punishment will be.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s sister drops huge hint he has retired from international football after he leaves Portugal camp
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s sister drops huge hint he has retired from international football after he leaves Portugal camp

Cristiano Ronaldo's sister has hinted he has retired from international football after he left the Portugal camp midway through the international break.

He has stated that he 'will tell the truth' about why he has departed amid reported frustration over his lack of minutes.

4 Ronaldo has officially left the Portugal camp after being left as an unused substitute for the first time since 2008 Credit: AFP

Ronaldo was an unused substitute for Portugal in their 2-1 win over Norway on Sunday, with that being the first time in 18 years that he had not played a single minute despite being in the squad.

The footballing icon was said to be unhappy with that, leading to a crisis meeting being planned with manager Jorge Jesus and the Portuguese Football Federation.

Jesus has since spoken out to deny those rumours - but hours later Ronaldo has now dropped the bombshell statement that he has departed.

Ronaldo confirms Portugal camp exit

“After the press conference of the national team, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team camp," he wrote on Instagram.

“In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave the national team, to which I always devoted myself.

“Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my teammates good luck, without exception.”

Portugal still have two games left in their international break schedule, with the first of those coming on Thursday.

They take on Denmark in their third Nations League clash, with another meeting with Norway coming on Sunday.

A Selecao have won both of their outings in the competition so far, with Ronaldo having a goal disallowed against Wales.

He played 67 minutes in the 1-0 win over Craig Bellamy's side before then playing no part against Norway.

4 Ronaldo was not happy to remain on the bench and has left after reportedly holding crisis talks Credit: AFP

Bombshell U-turn

Ronaldo confirmed that he has left the Portugal camp soon after Jesus had denied that any emergency meeting took place.

Jesus said: “Cristiano Ronaldo did not refuse to train.

“There are no issues. Cristiano told me: 'If you want me to play, I’ll play.

"If you want me to sit on the bench, I will. If you want me in the stands, I will'."

And those comments seemed to match what Ronaldo had already said publicly last week about his future with Portugal.

He had admitted that he was happy to sit on the bench and play less regularly under Jesus, who was also his manager at Al Nassr.

4 Ronaldo had said he was okay with playing less regularly under Jesus just a week ago Credit: Getty

4 Ronaldo's bombshell announcement comes hours after Jesus claimed things were fine between the two Credit: AFP

“Whatever the coach needs from me with the national team, whether that means playing, coming off, coming on, coming off again, or even not playing at all...I am available," he said.

"The pride I feel in representing Portugal is greater than that of any other international player”.

Ronaldo's final act for Portugal?

At 41 years old, Ronaldo is in the final days of his football career but his sister Elma Aveiro suggested he will never represent his country again.

In a wild social media post, she said: "CR7 deserved more respect. The national team deserved more structure.

"Portuguese journalism deserved more competence and less speculation.

"As for the Portuguese people, well… they don't deserve to have the best at anything.

"We are envious, disdainful, ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity we always had in football before CR7.

"Thank you for everything, CR7! You deserved more!"

Sports.title: Chris Smalling closes in on move to Champions League club on free transfer
Sports.content:
Chris Smalling closes in on move to Champions League club on free transfer

Chris Smalling is close to a shock free transfer to Porto, according to reports.

Fabrizio Romano reports that the former Manchester United defender has agreed a deal to join the Portuguese giants.



2 Smalling has already played for several massive European clubs Credit: Getty

The 36-year-old is now set to have a medical before penning a contract with Porto, who are in the Champions League this season.

Smalling is a free agent after leaving Saudi Arabian side Al Fayha in July.

He was unable to find a club during the transfer window, but Porto have elected to bring him in as cover and to compete with the club's current centre-backs.



They include former Arsenal man Jakub Kiwior and ex-Southampton star Jan Bednarek.

Smalling will be signing a one-year deal with the option for an extra one as he returns to Europe after two years in Saudi Arabia.



It marks another step in a career that has taken Smalling all over.

Smalling gets his move

The centre-back joined talkSPORT Breakfast in August to discuss his future.

He made it clear that he wasn't going to just accept any offer and wanted a project that excited him, and Porto is clearly that.



He said: "At the minute, there's conversations ongoing.

"I've had some offers, so I feel like I'm in a good position.

"But at my stage in my career, it's now about being patient, making sure it's the right kind of project that fits everything in terms of my role in the team and what I can bring on and off the pitch.

"I'm in a nice position and just kind of seeing where that lies over the next couple of weeks."

2 Smalling has won nine major trophies across his career Credit: Getty - Contributor

Smalling's career

Smalling started his career with Millwall before moving onto non league Maidstone United.



From there, he progressed through the academy and got a move to Fulham, where he exploded.

It took just 13 Premier League appearances across two seasons for Manchester United to agree a pre-contract agreement with the defender.

That saw him join the Red Devils in the summer of 2010, and he remained until 2019.

During his time at Old Trafford, Smalling won two Premier League titles under Sir Alex Ferguson.



And he became an important part of the team from 2013 onwards, helping Man United win the League Cup, FA Cup and Europa League in his time at Old Trafford.

On the international stage, Smalling played every minute of Euro 2016 as England were knocked out by Iceland. He managed 31 caps for the Three Lions.

A transfer to Roma rejuvenated his career and saw him help the club win their first European title.

That was under Jose Mourinho, and it was the Conference League as Smalling played ten games and scored a goal on the way to Roma lifting the title.



Now, he'll be hoping to add another major league title to his name as well with Porto flying at the top of of the Primeira League, with seven wins from seven.

Sports.title: Portugal manager dismisses Cristiano Ronaldo crisis talks and insists superstar is happy despite no game time
Sports.content:
Portugal manager dismisses Cristiano Ronaldo crisis talks and insists superstar is happy despite no game time

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus has denied rumours of crisis talks with Cristiano Ronaldo following his frustration over a lack of minutes.

It had been reported that the 41-year-old forward was set to meet with the head coach and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proenca this week to resolve his unhappiness.

4 Ronaldo was reportedly set to hold crisis talks after being left on the bench against Norway on Sunday Credit: AFP

This came after Ronaldo spent the entirety of Portugal's 2-1 win over Norway on Sunday on the bench.

With this the first time in 18 years he had been an unused substitute, Portuguese outlet Record claimed the football icon was upset by this.

Jesus' decision not to bring the five-time Ballon d'Or winner on was alleged to have broken a pre-match promise made to Ronaldo.

To resolve any tension, the report stated the player was set to hold talks with Jesus and Proenca on Wednesday in Copenhagen, ahead of Portugal's Thursday night Nations League clash with Denmark.

Jesus shuts down Ronaldo rumours

With rumours circulating over an emergency meeting with Ronaldo, Jesus has now quashed any talk of this.

The Portugal boss insisted the Al Nassr star had no issues with his decision not to play him against Norway, insisting he had already agreed to play whatever role the manager asked of him.

Jesus said: “Cristiano Ronaldo did not refuse to train.

“There are no issues. Cristiano told me: 'If you want me to play, I’ll play. If you want me to sit on the bench, I will. If you want me in the stands, I will'."

Jesus' comments echo Ronaldo's own comments ahead of the international break, where he discussed his decision to continue playing for his national team.

He said: “Whatever the coach needs from me with the national team, whether that means playing, coming off, coming on, coming off again, or even not playing at all... I am available.

4 Jesus opted against bringing Ronaldo on despite promising to give him 30 minutes off the bench Credit: Getty

"The pride I feel in representing Portugal is greater than that of any other international player”.

Ronaldo's international break

While Jesus has insisted Ronaldo had no issue with not featuring against Norway, the manager had previously revealed both in private and during his pre-match press conference that he planned to give him a 30-minute cameo in Oslo.

However, despite warming up on the touchline, Ronaldo did not feature in the 2-1 away victory.

Ronaldo is Portugal's all-time leading scorer and appearance maker with 146 goals in 234 caps for his country.

Portugal head into Thursday's clash with Denmark with a 100 per cent record in the competition after wins over Wales and Norway.

Ronaldo started their opener against the former last week, playing 67 minutes as captain.

4 Ronaldo will meet with Jesus and Proenca in Copenhagen on Wednesday Credit: Getty

He was subsequently replaced as skipper against Norway by Ruben Dias.

His side continue their campaign away to Denmark before the final match of the current international break at home to Norway in Porto on Sunday.

Ronaldo under Jesus

Ronaldo's tension with Jesus comes just months after the pair won the Saudi Pro League title together.

The veteran coach was in charge of Al Nassr last season as they finished two points clear of nearest challengers Al Hilal.

During his time as manager, Ronaldo scored 30 goals in 37 appearances.

Having left Al Nassr, Jesus succeeded Roberto Martinez as national team boss in July.

4 Ronaldo and Jesus have won silverware together at club level this year Credit: Getty

It came after Portugal were knocked out of the World Cup in the last 16 by eventual winners Spain.

Jesus has signed a four-year deal through to the end of the 2030 edition of the tournament.

He will also oversee the current Nations League campaign and Portugal's quest to reach Euro 2028.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger urged to stand against Gianni Infantino in FIFA elections
Sports.content:
Arsene Wenger has been told to stand against Gianni Infantino in the upcoming election to become the next FIFA president.
