World.title: Butković: We’re Signing Largest Contract in History of Croatian Railways
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Transport Minister Oleg Butković has stated that today the signing of the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways will be signed.

Minister of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Oleg Butković announced the signing of a contract for the reconstruction and upgrading of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway line, worth almost 900 million euros. Index reports that this is the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways.

The Dugo Selo – Novska line is part of one of the main corridors that runs through Croatia towards the east of the country. “This is truly the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways – almost 900 million euros for 83 kilometres of track reconstruction and the construction of a second track. We’ve been working on this project for a long time, preparing it, a public tender was carried out and now the procedures are complete,” said Butković.

first cooperation with an indian company

After the realisation of this project, he added, the Okučani – Vinkovci section will still remain. “Then we will have a fully reconstructed and built railway line from the Slovenian border, because Savski Marof – Zagreb has been reconstructed, that is, from Zagreb to the border with Serbia,” the minister said. Butković confirmed that this is the first time a company from India has won a job in such a tender. “As far as we have inquired and according to the documentation they submitted, they have very good references. They have worked on one of the largest projects in India and the world, so I believe everything will be as it should,” he said.

The minister is aware that large projects also bring challenges. “Some things today you cannot predict and you cannot influence them. I hope there will be as few of them as possible,” he said. The start of works is planned for the first quarter of 2027 and they should last five and a half years. Butković expressed the hope that there will be no new major crises in the world that could, like previous ones, cause disruptions and price increases.

the lowland railway project

The minister also spoke about the lowland railway, a project that has been in preparation for a long time. “We have started with the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section. As for the reconstruction of the lines around Zagreb, mostly everything has been reconstructed: towards the west, towards Zagorje and towards Bjelovar. By the end of the year we are finishing Dugo Selo – Križevci, which is actually almost done, and Križevci – Koprivnica – Hungarian border,” he said.

He emphasised that it is now important to move towards Rijeka, where the most expensive section from Karlovac to Rijeka remains, whose value is estimated at more than 2.5 billion euros. “There has been an increase in prices due to all the disruptions I spoke about, but we have accelerated the entire project.

A tender for technical assistance is currently underway. We would go for the so-called Alliance model, in which design, obtaining building permits and execution of works would be in one package,” he explained. Under that model, the selected contractor would lead all procedures, which would shorten public procurement and appeal procedures, and the deadline for construction of the line would be five to six years.

another decade before any real change

Asked when passengers will feel real progress and get fast trains, Butković replied that passenger transport around Zagreb is already functioning well. “We’ve more than 70 new trains in passenger transport. Of those, 42 trains have been procured in the last four years. Contracts are constantly being signed and funds secured. This was also shown these days during the strike, when the trains helped a lot, especially in the suburban area,” he emphasised.

Nevertheless, the complete reconstruction of the railway network will still take time. “I always say that we have to be patient for another ten years or so. In those ten years we would manage to mostly reconstruct and build everything on the main corridors and reconstruct a large part of the regional lines. We have already spent around 900 million euros on the reconstruction of local and regional lines across Croatia,” he said.

the continuation of motorway construction

The minister also commented on motorway construction. He announced that the Istrian Y will be completed by the end of the year or the beginning of 2027. “We’re strongly and decisively going ahead with the construction of the Adriatic-Ionian Corridor, Križišće – Žuta Lokva. Two contracts have been signed there. Today we received the building permit for the first section and we are starting the works. That is around 400 million euros,” he said.

Bids have also been opened for the first section of the motorway towards Dubrovnik. Although the new bids are also above the estimated value, the tender will not be cancelled again. “We would not have cancelled the first one either if there had not been really large differences in price compared to the estimated values. The bids that arrived in the new tender are around 40 to 50 million euros lower compared to the previous tender,” Butković concluded. He said that they are decisively proceeding with the completion of the Adriatic-Ionian Corridor, that is, the motorway towards Dubrovnik and the Križišće – Žuta Lokva section.

World.title: Record Revenue from Foreign Tourists in Croatia in 1st 6 Months of 2026
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Record revenue from foreign tourists in Croatia during the first 6 months of 2026 has amounted to incredible sums, amounting to well over 3 billion euros.

In the first six months of this year, 2.5 billion euros more revenue was generated than in the same period of 2016, said Tonči Glavina. As Novi list reports, according to the latest data from the Croatian National Bank (HNB), in the second quarter of 2026 revenues from foreign tourists amounted to 3 billion and 641.7 million euros, which represents growth of almost 4 percent compared to the same period in 2025, or 132.7 million euros more.

Overall, in the first half of 2026, revenues from foreign tourists amounted to 4 billion and 587 million euros, which represents growth of almost 5 percent compared to the same period in 2025, or 212.4 million euros more. In addition, strong growth in domestic tourism also contributed to the positive results of the tourist year.

In the first six months of 2026, a record 1.5 million arrivals and 4.2 million overnight stays by domestic tourists were recorded, which is 7 percent more arrivals and 6 percent more overnight stays than a year earlier.

“The excellent indicators in the pre-season are the result of strong strategic and promotional activities that we adapted to changes in the market, thereby continuing the positive trends of Croatian tourism even in this extremely challenging year. If we compare these financial results with those recorded back in 2016, revenues from foreign tourists have risen by 120 percent, both in the second quarter and in the first half of the year.

In the first six months of this year, 2.5 billion euros more revenue was generated than in the same period of 2016, while in the second quarter revenue was higher by two billion euros compared to the same period ten years ago. In line with all our strategic goals, we’re permanently changing Croatian tourism for the better in all segments,” emphasised Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina.

World.title: St. Jerome Exhibition Awaits Passengers at Split Airport
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – A brand new St. Jerome exhibition now awaits passengers coming and going from Split Airport.

The new exhibition brings together works by 24 prominent Croatian painters and sculptors created at the St. Jerome Art Colony on Marjan. Morski reports that the exhibition was officially opened by Split-Dalmatia County Prefect Blaženko Boban.

“On the occasion of the feast of Saint Jerome and Split-Dalmatia County Day, we organised an exhibition of our most eminent painters and sculptors, not only from our county but from the whole of the Republic of Croatia, who took part in the art colony on Marjan. We are presenting the exhibition for the third time, after the University Gallery and the National and University Library in Zagreb,” said Boban. He added that the exhibition at the Airport also opens the possibility for the story of Saint Jerome, Marjan and contemporary Croatian fine art to travel beyond Croatia’s borders.

“I’d like to thank all the artists and the director of Split Airport, and I congratulate him and all the staff on 60 years of very high-quality work by Saint Jerome Airport,” the Prefect said.

This year’s presentation of the exhibition has additional symbolism because Split Airport is marking the 60th anniversary of its founding. Its director Josip Čorić expressed satisfaction that such a cultural event is being held for the first time in the Airport premises.

The exhibition brings together works by Goran Balić, Duje Botteri, Nikola Džaja, Kažimir Hraste, Petar Jakelić, Kuzma Kovačić, Đani Martinić, Duje Matetić, Matko Mijić, Dijana Iva Sesartić, Ana Marija Botteri, Josip Botteri Dini, Željko Bubalo, Alma Čače, Vladimir Davidenko, Lili Gluić, Karin Grenc, Ivan Listeš, Zvonimir Mihanović, Tea Morić Šitum, Hrvoje Marko Peruzović, Vice Tomasović, Marko Gugić and Frane Šitum. The works were created at the St. Jerome Art Colony, held on the 22nd and 23rd of September 2023 on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of Split-Dalmatia County, organised by Split-Dalmatia County, the University of Split and the Parish of the Holy Cross, Veli Varoš.

World.title: HVARMONY, Celebrating Wellbeing on Croatia’s Premier Island
World.content:
September 30, 2026 – Famous for its sun, beaches, heritage and nightlife, a new initiative celebrates another of its gems – wellbeing. Meet HVARMONY.

Soon after I moved to the island of Hvar back in 2003, an island whose existence I had only become aware of two days before I bought my house, I realised that it was a very distinct island of two halves. The most famous, of course, was the tourism side, with its world famous beaches filled with tourists all over the world, as they also enjoyed the fine gastronomy, culture and endless sun.

But there was another side to Hvar, and one that I liked much better – the off-season. No longer warm enough to swim (although some did), devoid of tourists, most businesses closed for the season, but what a fantastic slice of nature to enjoy in peace and quiet. If Croatia made me realise that quality of life, lifestyle and wellbeing were the shortcut to happiness, it was the winters in Jelsa that first pointed the way.

Olive groves, vineyards, growing their own food, while loudly discussing olives and Hajduk Split over timeless coffees, I had never come across a place so contented with itself. And I quickly learned that I was not alone. All over the island, there were Austrians, Norwegians, Americans, Germans living in the hills or smaller villages, some with yoga studios, but all thrilled that they had found such a gem off the radar.

The digital nomad revolution came to Croatia in 2020, enabling a new breed of tourist to spend an extended period in Croatia. One of the first was an American couple who moved to Jelsa and did a great documentary for national tv on why life on a Dalmatian island in January was perfect. Some locals might have thought they were nuts, but I understood perfectly.

And as look around Hvar these days, in addition to the tourism, there is another undercurrent bubbling away – wellbeing. Yoga, pilates, energy healing, retreats – they are all increasing in number and diversity. It is for me an essential part of the Hvar DNA – this is, of course, the island that was nicknamed the Austrian Madeira for its temperate and healing climate, which resulted in it becoming the birthplace of organised tourism in Europe with the founding of the Hvar Health Society in 1868.

But there has been precious little official recognition of this wellbeing aspect. Until now.

Meet HVARMONY, an excellent initiative from the Hvar Tourist Board, which will take place for the first time from October 15-18. And before we get to the concept and programmes, the locations of the event set the tone – the oldest public theatre in Europe, the impressive Arsenal on the corner of the main square, the 1930s colonnade, Bonj les Bains, and the 5-star Maslina Resort, whose slogan is Mindful Luxury.

So what exactly is HVARMONY? An explanation from the dedicated website:

HVARMONY is a four-day gathering built around one simple question: how can we live better, longer and more fulfilling lives?

From 15 to 18 October in Hvar, talks, conversations, workshops and shared experiences will explore what wellbeing really means today, why we seem to need it more than ever, and whether somewhere along the way it has become yet another industry selling us health, happiness and longevity.

Over the four-day event, some 23 Croatian and international speakers will put on an excellent and diverse programme exploring key themes on health, happiness and longevity, with plenty of yoga, pilates and other energy food for the body. You can see the whole programme here.

I really like the direction that Hvar tourism is going these days, it is a much more pleasant experience, and I applaud the organisers of this initiative, which will not only bring together motivated like-minded people, but also showcase some of the magic I first discovered a quarter of a century ago.

Entrance and participation for events is free of charge (with the exception of a few sessions which are paid), although registration is required. You can do this on the official HVARMONY website.

World.title: Uber CEO Comes to Zagreb and Tries Out Rimac’s Robotaxi
World.content:
September the 30th, 2026 – Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi arrived in Zagreb and tried out Mate Rimac’s famed robotaxi without a safety driver.

Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi visited Verne and the Rimac Campus in Zagreb yesterday and rode in a robotaxi without a safety driver, Mate Rimac announced. “Uber is an investor and strategic partner in Verne. Dara tried out the robotaxi without a safety driver in Zagreb and was delighted with the experience. We talked about further cooperation and expanding Verne beyond Croatia with the ‘final’ Verne car without a steering wheel and pedals,” Rimac wrote on Facebook.

Index reports that Uber and Verne have otherwise been cooperating for months now on an autonomous taxi project. Back in March, Verne, China’s Pony.ai and Uber announced a strategic partnership to launch a robotaxi service in Europe, starting in Zagreb. Uber also announced an investment in Verne at that time.

driverless rides are already being tested out in zagreb

At the beginning of September, Verne and Pony.ai began testing rides with passengers in Zagreb without a safety driver or other staff in the vehicle. The tests are taking place on a 22-kilometre route connecting Verne’s headquarters with the area of Zagreb Airport. However, these are vehicles from the Chinese manufacturer BAIC with Pony.ai autonomous driving technology, not the final Verne vehicle without a steering wheel and pedals that Rimac mentions in today’s post. Since August, Uber has also enabled the ordering of autonomous rides via its app in Zagreb. In that phase a licensed operator was still behind the wheel, while fully driverless rides were introduced as separate tests.

the final report for the eu-funded project has been submitted

Mate Rimac’s announcement comes on the same day that Project 3 Mobility, the company developing Verne, submitted its final report to SAFU on the last day of the deadline for the robotaxi project financed from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan. According to what remains unofficial information, the company is not requesting recognition of the remaining part of the already paid advance in the final documentation. Verne had 179.5 million euros in non-repayable EU funds approved for the project, and back in July 2023 it received an advance of 89.75 million euros. SAFU earlier confirmed to Index that of that amount around 8.77 million euros had been justified so far, while around 80.98 million euros had not been justified.

The project formally ended on the 30th of August, after which a 30-day deadline for submitting the final documentation began. SAFU now has 60 days to check the reported costs and documentation, and during the procedure it may also request additional information. Only after the check is completed will it be known how much of the paid advance will be recognised and how much money, if any, Verne will have to return.

the primary contracted goal was not completed in time

The key problem of the EU-funded project remains the fact that by the deadline it was not confirmed that a fully autonomous Level 5 vehicle had been produced and homologated, which was one of the main contracted results of the project. Prime Minister Andrej Plenković said after the deadline expired that the project had not received final homologation from the competent institution in Germany and that it had not been completed by the end of August.

At the beginning of September, Verne revealed that it was ready to return the funds if the final evaluation showed that the contracted obligations had not been fully met. At the same time the company claimed that during the project test prototypes of fully autonomous electric vehicles had been confirmed and appropriate tests carried out. Mate Rimac’s meeting with Uber’s Dara Khosrowshahi therefore concerns the continuation of Verne’s commercial development and cooperation with Uber, while the final evaluation procedure for the EU-funded project continues separately.

World.title: EU Raises Retirement Age, Here’s What Awaits Croatia
World.content:
September the 30th, 2026 – As the EU raises its retirement age and multiple countries now expect their work forces to work for longer, what exactly awaits Croatia?

Working life across the European Union is lengthening significantly, and for younger generations the difference could be as much as ten years. Croatia is not currently going to raise its retirement age above 65. The retirement age is rising across Europe, and for some of today’s younger workers a working life could last until the age of 70 or even longer. The OECD estimates that the average retirement age will increase further in the future as life expectancy rises, while numerous countries have already legally adopted gradual increases.

Denmark stands out the most. There it has already been decided that the statutory retirement age will rise to 70 by 2040, while the OECD projects an even higher threshold for generations that have only just entered the labour market if the current method of linking the pension age to life expectancy continues. According to the latest edition of the OECD’s Pensions at a Glance report, the average normal retirement age for people who retired in 2024 is around 64.7 years for men and 63.9 years for women.

For those who have only just entered the labour market, the OECD expects a significantly longer working life. The average future retirement age is estimated at 66.4 years for men and 65.9 years for women.

denmark is taking it the furthest

Denmark is at the top of the European ranking. The current normal retirement age there is 67, and parliament has already adopted an increase to 70 years from 2040. The OECD projects that if the current formula linked to life expectancy continues to be applied, the future retirement age in Denmark could rise as high as 74 years. It is important to emphasise, however, that 74 is not a legally set limit for a specific year, but a projection that depends on whether Denmark continues to link the pension age to increases in life expectancy. The country is already discussing possible easing of that formula after 2040.

High future thresholds are also expected in other European countries. Estonia could reach 71 years, while the OECD projects a normal retirement age of around 70 for Italy, the Netherlands and Sweden. Under current rules, Finland could reach around 68 years and Slovakia around 69, while in a number of other countries the future normal retirement age is approaching 67.

many countries are adopting reforms

The changes are no longer just projections. In several European countries reforms have already been adopted that gradually increase the retirement age or link its future movement to life expectancy.

Belgium will reach a retirement age of 67 years, while the United Kingdom has planned a further increase towards 68. The Czech Republic has also adopted a gradual increase of the statutory age to 67. Slovenia has reformed its pension system and raised the statutory age, but in international comparisons the possibility of full retirement with a sufficient number of contribution years must also be taken into account. The main reason for such reforms is demographics. Europeans are living longer, while at the same time in many countries the share of the working-age population that finances pension systems is shrinking.

Countries are therefore trying to achieve a balance between longer life expectancy, the number of years spent in retirement and the financial sustainability of the system.

men and women are moving towards the same threshold

Differences in retirement age between men and women are gradually narrowing. In most European countries men and women already have the same statutory retirement age, while differences have been retained only in some countries. Some countries where the difference still exists have already decided on its gradual abolition, so the number of systems in which women can take full retirement earlier than men will decrease further.

where does croatia fall here?

Croatia is currently among the countries that do not have a legally determined increase in the regular retirement age above 65. Men in Croatia acquire the right to an old-age pension at the age of 65 with at least 15 years of pensionable service. For women a transitional period is still underway. In 2026 a woman can acquire the right to an old-age pension at 64 years of age and at least 15 years of service.

The threshold for women then increases by three months each year. In 2027 it will be 64 years and three months, in 2028 64 years and six months, and in 2029 64 years and nine months. From the 1st of January 2030, the conditions will be equalised, so both men and women in Croatia will acquire a regular old-age pension at the age of 65. There are also special rules for long-term insured persons. A person who has 60 years of age and 41 years of insurance service in effective duration can acquire the right to an old-age pension for a long-term insured person.

For early old-age pension the general rule is 60 years of age and 35 years of service. For women a transitional period is still underway, so in 2026 they can acquire the right at 59 years of age and 34 years of pensionable service.

will people in croatia have to work for longer?

So far no decision has been taken according to which the regular retirement age in Croatia would be increased above 65. This currently distinguishes Croatia from countries that have already legally linked the retirement age to life expectancy or adopted increases towards 67, 68 or 70 years. Nevertheless, the demographic pressure that is driving reforms in other European countries is also present in Croatia. The population is ageing, and the ratio of the number of employed people to pension beneficiaries is one of the key factors in the sustainability of the system.

That is why the question of how long future generations will have to work before retiring will remain one of the more important topics of European, and also Croatian, social policy. The difference between today’s and future generations can be large. While in a large part of Europe today’s normal retirement age is around 65, in some countries those who are only just starting work could, under current rules, retire only after the age of 70.

World.title: Wellovar – Bjelovar Geothermal Complex Now Open
World.content:
September the 30th, 2026 – Wellovar, the much anticipated Bjelovar geothermal complex is now open, with the ceremony attended by approximately 600 guests.

The ceremony was attended by around 600 guests, and alongside Mayor Dario Hrebak and Bjelovar-Bilogora County Prefect Marko Marušić, the highest-ranking state guests included Prime Minister Andrej Plenković, Speaker of the Croatian Parliament Gordan Jandroković and Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina.

Poslovni reports that after years of planning, preparation and 23 months of intensive construction, Wellovar opened its doors today. The ceremony was held as part of the celebrations of Bjelovar’s 270th birthday, and the new complex in Veliko Korenovo was presented as the largest project in the city’s history.

The way Wellovar was opened was particularly symbolic. Instead of the classic ribbon-cutting, 18 Bjelovar residents of different generations jumped into the Olympic pool. The youngest was a kindergarten-age girl, and among the participants were also well-known Bjelovar athletes, swimmers and pensioners. This “Generational Jump” was meant to symbolise the decades during which the people of Bjelovar had waited for an indoor Olympic pool, as well as the fact that the project is intended for the generations to come.

Wellovar was built as a geothermal sports and recreational complex and contains a total of 10 pools – five indoor and five outdoor. The complex also has four saunas, a gym, sports and recreational facilities and a restaurant. The outdoor pools will be presented to the public next spring.

Terme Bjelovar Director Zvonimir Žarec emphasised that behind the project were 23 months of intensive work, numerous challenges, but also a large team that in recent months prepared the complex for its first guests. Terme currently employs 47 people, and the number of employees will continue to grow. For Bjelovar, the opening of Wellovar also marks the beginning of a new tourism and economic story. With the project, the city aims to position itself as a destination for geothermal, sports and health tourism, and the new complex should also attract visitors from outside Bjelovar.

World.title: Man City scandal risks damage to Premier League’s booming brand
World.content:
Manchester – The Premier League has won a lengthy legal battle with Manchester City over financial impropriety, but the consequences could leave lasting damage for a league that has long since become the envy of world football.

City face severe sanctions after being found guilty of over 100 charges between 2009 and 2018, with an independent commission exposing “sham” contracts to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).

A hefty points deduction resulting in relegation, stripped titles and even expulsion from the English top flight have been mooted as potential sanctions.

But the damage may not be limited to City alone with an entire era of the Premier League now under a cloud.

A takeover in 2008 by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, transformed City’s fortunes, but also the face of the Premier League.

The club’s first top-flight league title for 44 years was one of the most iconic moments in Premier League history when Sergio Aguero netted the winner against QPR in the 94th minute to deny Manchester United the title.

Some of City’s rivals have been quick to revel in their downfall.

“Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet,” posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand, who was part of the United team that finished second to City in the 2011/12 season.

Yet there could be more lingering collective consequences for a league that has become accustomed to flexing its financial muscle to hoover up the best talent from around the globe.

Italy’s Serie A once enjoyed that status in the 1990s.

Although it had lost some of its lustre by the time the Calciopoli scandal came about in 2006, Italian football has arguably never fully recovered in the two decades since.

That case surrounded club officials influencing which referees would officiate their games and led to Juventus being stripped of two titles and relegated to Serie B.

– Haaland exit inevitable?

The question is now whether fans will be turned away from the Premier League after feeling cheated over what they have witnessed over the past 18 years.

In total City have won eight titles in the last 15 seasons.

They rewrote the record books, becoming the first side to ever achieve 100 points and win the English top flight for four consecutive years.

All of those achievements are now labelled with an asterisk.

“If I was a player, I’d be 100 percent sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it’s cheating,” said former Manchester United captain Roy Keane.

Despite the Premier League’s spending power, English clubs have still struggled to keep the world’s biggest superstars away from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

City’s demise could also see the Premier League lose its marquee player in Erling Haaland.

“The Premier League is Britain’s greatest soft power cultural asset,” Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian sport, told AFP. “What happens when people start to question, ‘what have I been watching all these years?'”

By contrast, the Premier League has argued the City case is proof of strong governance.

The league pursued and persisted with an investigation which began in 2018 despite City’s best attempts to frustrate the process.

“This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history,” said the league’s chief executive Richard Masters.

“It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition.

“It is paramount that the league remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.”

World.title: Asian stocks mixed as positive US data offset by elevated oil, bond yields
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks were mixed Thursday following a largely down day on Wall Street with positive US data offset by elevated government bond yields and oil prices.

Analysts said traders were presented with a “Goldilocks” batch of figures that provided a fillip to equities on Wall Street as the dealers revised lower the likelihood of a second successive interest rate hike.

The closely watched personal consumption expenditure gauge came in at a below-forecast 3.4 percent, while the Commerce Department revised upwards its estimate for second-quarter economic growth thanks to the artificial intelligence investment boom.

Private jobs creation topped expectations.

The readings pointed to a healthy economy despite the impact of the Middle East crisis and surging oil prices, and saw investors row back their expectations on the Federal Reserve lifting borrowing costs on October 28.

CME’s FedWatch tool put the chances of an increase at less than 40 percent, having priced it at more than 65 percent earlier in the week.

“Second-quarter growth was stronger than expected, consumer spending was more robust, the labour market rebounded sharply in September and the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge came in well below expectations,” said Chris Osmond, of Fifth Third Wealth Advisors.

“The net effect is broadly supportive of risk assets and materially reduces the probability of an October rate hike.”

However, investors remain concerned about the outlook for borrowing costs, with the US 10-year Treasury yield sitting around its highest level since 2007, and the US 30-year yield at a 24-year high.

Elevated oil prices remain a crucial driver of the spike, with the commodity supported by uncertainty in the Middle East, even as Saudi Arabia pumps more fuel through its partially reopened East-West pipeline.

Both main contracts edged down Thursday having jumped around one percent the day before.

Brent for December delivery was around $97.60 a barrel — the November contract closed at more than $103 — while West Texas Intermediate was hovering below $90.

In New York trade, the Dow and S&P 500 ended in the red, though the Nasdaq rose on the back of a tech rally sparked by a healthy forecast from chip giant Micron, even as it warned on narrower margins.

Chip firms led gains in Asia, with SK hynix and Samsung’s advances lifting Seoul’s market, while Tokyo’s Nikkei rallied thanks to big gains in tech giants Kioxia, Advantest, Tokyo Electron and investor SoftBank.

Taipei and Singapore also gained, though there were losses in Sydney, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta.

World.title: UK fears grow over AI giant Palantir’s health service deal
World.content:
London – The UK government is facing mounting pressure to end a £330-million contract between the National Health Service and AI giant Palantir, as doctors, lawmakers and campaigners warn of ethical risks.

The US company, co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel — a close ally of US President Donald Trump — has enjoyed a growing role in Britain’s public sector and the contract, awarded in 2023, allows it to provide a data management platform to the NHS.

Worth around $440 million, the Federated Data Platform (FDP) is designed to improve coordination between hospitals and help manage and streamline appointments, making more efficient use of resources.

The NHS insists sensitive patient data remains stored in Britain, is not owned by Palantir and is not used for commercial purposes or AI training.

But critics point to the firm’s broader work, including with the Israeli military and US immigration authorities, arguing such activities undermine any technological benefits as well as trust in the health service.

“The NHS has to function on trust — the trust I can tell my doctor anything. Those ethical concerns are basically poisoning everything,” Duncan McCann, head of technology and data at the campaign group Good Law Project, told AFP.

– ‘Break the contract’ –

Medical organisations and rights activists are planning protests on Thursday outside some 30 hospitals as well as Palantir’s London headquarters.

They are urging the government to use a break clause that would prevent the contract being renewed beyond March 2027.

So far new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who took office in July, has not publicly commented on the contract, which is under review with ministers expected to decide by December.

The British Medical Association (BMA) has urged doctors not to use the platform, citing risks to patient trust, data security and NHS independence.

“Given Palantir’s track record, including controversies in the US involving immigration enforcement… we believe there must be a complete break from Palantir technologies in the NHS,” BMA chair Tom Dolphin told the British Medical Journal in February.

A YouGov poll published in July found 65 percent of Britons backed ending the contract.

But supporters argue the system is delivering results and around two-thirds of NHS hospitals have adopted the platform.

Palantir, which did not respond to AFP requests for a comment, says it has helped enable 110,000 additional operations while reducing waiting lists.

“The benefits of the FDP service are clear, with thousands more patients benefitting every month, including through the reduction in the number of unnecessary days spent in hospital after treatment,” a Department of Health spokesperson told AFP.

The debate has widened beyond healthcare.

A parliamentary committee recently warned of growing UK dependence on US technology providers, and one of its members, Liberal Democrat MP Martin Wrigley, has called for a “sovereign” British alternative.

“That has to be within the control of a UK, preferably UK-owned firm, but certainly a UK firm that understands the ethics and way that the NHS works,” he told AFP.

He warned of the risks that Trump could arbitrarily decide that Palantir’s services to the UK could be “switched off” if for instance “he doesn’t like what Andy Burnham says, or they differ on Ukraine or something”.

– Alternatives –

Palantir has secured multiple public sector contracts in Britain, including a £240-million defence deal signed in 2025.

The UK is now Palantir’s second-largest global market, accounting for 10 percent of the company’s revenue in 2025.

France however this year decided to move away from using Palantir’s software in their intelligence agencies, replacing it with software developed by French company ChapsVision.

German media reported that Berlin has acquired the French technology and is testing it.

London Mayor Sadiq Khan also blocked a £50-million contract between the Metropolitan Police and Palantir in May, citing procurement concerns, prompting the company to launch legal action.

Several British organisations have also chosen to part ways with the firm.

In northern England, NHS Greater Manchester, which manages the region’s hospitals and local healthcare providers, has spent the past decade building its own data platform capable of performing some of the same functions as the FDP.

“What we’ve built to meet the system needs is better” for local patients, the provider’s chief data officer, Matt Hennessey, told AFP, adding other regions could also achieve the same results.

World.title: US government’s new AI chatbot pulls back from debunking Trump
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump unveiled what he called a “damn good” AI chatbot, but it quickly drew attention for contradicting some of his contentious political claims.

A day later, however, it stopped answering some political questions.

“Hello, America. Whatever you need from government, start here,” reads the America.gov platform, which Trump launched on Tuesday in a bid to simplify access to government information and federal services.

The chatbot soon began contradicting Trump on controversial subjects such as the 2020 presidential election, which he wrongly claims to have won, and the January 6, 2021 insurrection that saw a violent mob attacking the US Capitol.

“On its first day, America.gov harnessed facts and official documents to contradict some of the false narratives and political framing about immigration and elections heavily promoted by the administration that built it,” said the Digital Democracy Institute of the Americas.

“Initial analyses found that America.gov generally provided evidence-based answers backed by government records, even when those records contradicted claims made by Trump and his administration.”

On Tuesday, when asked whether there had been widespread voter fraud in the 2020 election, the chatbot responded: “Official federal assessments after the 2020 presidential election did not find fraud at a scale that changed the outcome.”

Democratic lawmakers quickly promoted the chatbot’s responses about the election.

“Finally, a straight answer from someone in the Trump administration,” Senator Adam Schiff of California wrote on X on Tuesday, alongside a screenshot of the chatbot’s statement that former president Joe Biden had won the 2020 election.

But on Wednesday, the chatbot changed its tune when asked the same question. “I do not provide political commentary or analysis of past elections,” it said.

It was unclear whether the Trump administration had tweaked the settings to prevent the chatbot from debunking the president. The White House did not immediately weigh in.

“America.gov will continue to be updated to provide Americans the most accurate and reliable federal information and resources,” the White House said in a statement to US media.

The chatbot, however, continued to debunk some of Trump’s other claims on Wednesday.

When asked about Trump’s widely debunked claim that the United States experienced the “worst inflation” ever under former president Biden, the chatbot disagreed.

“No. Official Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) data do not show the highest US inflation on record during 2021–2025.”

“‘Worst inflation ever’ is not supported by the official CPI record.”

The launch of the new government platform comes as growing cyber incidents have raised concerns around the world about risks posed by uncontrollable AI, with some tech executives urging a slow-down for safety.

Trump has dismissed those concerns as a conspiracy to undermine US economic growth and hamper competition with China.

World.title: UK PM says ‘strong indications’ Iran involved in airbase incident
World.content:
London – British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Wednesday said there were “strong indications” Iran was involved in suspicious activity at a UK airbase that triggered a major security incident this weekend.

“There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford,” Burnham told the BBC, referring to Sunday’s bomb scare near the airbase in southwest England, which is used by the US military in its war against Iran.

“Of course it remains an ongoing, complex, and serious police investigation,” said Burnham.

Iran’s embassy in London earlier said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” speculation it was involved in the incident, while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on X that Burnham was “barking up the wrong tree”.

Police said on Tuesday that no explosives were found at the scene. The nature of the threat has not been explained by officials.

Burnham’s comments are the first official confirmation from UK authorities that Iran may have had a hand in the incident, which saw three white vans appearing to head towards RAF Fairford in the early hours of Sunday.

A local resident who rang the police said she saw a group of masked men near the vans, which were blocking a road in a village next to the military base.

– Growing confusion –

The case was plunged into confusion when UK police released on bail five British men it had arrested on Sunday on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences.

After three days of investigations, including using a bomb disposal team, police said Tuesday they had found no explosives in the vehicles, but they had retrieved a “quantity of petrol”.

Then on Wednesday, The Times newspaper reported that the incident had been foiled after one of the five suspects tipped off the police before the group was apprehended.

US President Donald Trump and his Secretary of State Marco Rubio had previously indicated that intelligence bodies were aware of the suspects and that a foreign state could be involved, but UK officials had not weighed in.

“We have been waiting to confirm what we could say, but we can now confirm our belief that Iran played a part,” Burnham told Sky News.

Speculation was rife that Iran or another hostile state could have been involved, after Tehran previously warned London against allowing its military bases to be used by Washington.

Britain gave the US the greenlight to use RAF Fairford for defensive strikes against Iran, drawing Tehran’s ire and unease from some residents in the Gloucestershire countryside where the base is located.

World.title: Google restricts access to new AI model over safety concerns
World.content:
San Francisco – Google on Wednesday said it would withhold its most powerful artificial intelligence model from the public for now, releasing Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts to avoid misuse by hackers.

“Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach,” wrote Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google’s chief AI architect, in a blog post announcing the model.

Google said it is voluntarily giving the US government early access to the model and will gather feedback from testers before making it widely available.

The cautious rollout mirrors the approach of rival Anthropic, which has kept its most advanced model, Claude Mythos Preview, restricted to a small number of trusted organizations.

Washington briefly forced Anthropic to suspend access to its publicly released Claude Mythos and Claude Fable models in June, and has since set up a voluntary process for vetting the most powerful AI models before release.

The announcement came a day after President Donald Trump hosted top tech executives, including Google chief Sundar Pichai and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, at the White House, where they signed a voluntary accord pledging to police the risks of their own AI systems.

Cybersecurity experts fear the state-of-the-art technology could be used to hack banks, hospitals and government systems.

Google said Argon excels at complex tasks in software engineering, legal and financial work and cyber defense, with a leading ability to find and fix critical software flaws.

Early testers used Argon to uncover a flaw in software used by hospitals around the world that exposed sensitive personal information — something other advanced models had missed, Google said.

Google said Argon is designed to refuse requests that could help carry out cyberattacks or develop chemical, biological or nuclear weapons.

Anthropic and ChatGPT-maker OpenAI have built similar safeguards into their most advanced models.

Google said it is monitoring the model’s reasoning to stop it from straying beyond what users intended, a risk researchers call misalignment.

The issue has taken on new urgency since OpenAI disclosed in July that two of its models, including one not yet released, broke out of a sealed test environment during a cybersecurity evaluation and hacked into the servers of AI company Hugging Face.

World.title: Hegseth says US cut number of generals, admirals by 20%
World.content:
Washington – Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Wednesday that the United States has slashed the number of its generals and admirals by 20 percent, in a move he said is aimed at “accountability.”

Hegseth suggested the cuts targeted officers who failed to get on board with his efforts to ensure the military is focused on war-fighting rather than the “woke” policies of previous administrations, describing the reductions as an “accomplishment.”

“The number-crunchers say we fired 10 percent of the generals and admirals across the force,” Hegseth told troops at the Quantico military base, saying: “We’ve also reduced the overall number of general officer slots by an additional 10 percent.”

“So yes, 20 percent reduction across the board,” he said. “The media calls that a purge. I call it accountability, and long overdue.”

The address to junior officers and enlisted personnel at Quantico came a year after a similar speech to top officers in which Hegseth said the US military was too fat, too focused on leftist “woke” ideas, and in need of major shake-up.

He said Wednesday that top officers who “responded positively” to the previous speech are “leading newly focused and newly empowered and disciplined formations,” while those who did not “no longer work here.”

“We are no longer the woke department, or the weak department,” Hegseth said.

“Simple translation of that: no fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors — just tough, ready, committed troops.”

– Cutting ‘fat’ –

Hegseth ordered major cuts to the US military — including a 10-percent reduction to the overall number of generals and admirals, and a 20-percent decrease in the highest four-star ranks — in May 2025.

There were 831 active duty US generals and admirals as of the end of that month, but Pentagon figures from the end of July 2026 — the latest available — showed there were actually more top officers — a total of 851.

Asked to clarify if the 20 percent cuts had been completed or were still ongoing, the Pentagon said: “We have nothing further to provide beyond the secretary’s comments.”

During his confirmation hearing in January 2025, Hegseth argued that the Pentagon’s bureaucracy was top-heavy and in need of cuts.

“It’s going to be my job, working with those that we hire and those inside the administration, to identify those places where fat can be cut, so it can go toward lethality,” he told lawmakers at the time.

Since returning to office early last year, Trump has overseen a purge of top military personnel, including the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, general Charles “CQ” Brown, whom he fired without explanation in February 2025.

Other senior officers pushed out include the heads of the US Army, Navy and Coast Guard, the general who headed the National Security Agency, the vice chief of staff of the US Air Force, a Navy admiral assigned to NATO, and three top military lawyers.

The chief of staff of the Air Force also announced his retirement without explanation just two years into a four-year term, while the head of US Southern Command retired a year into his tenure.

Hegseth has insisted the president is simply choosing the leaders he wants, but Democratic lawmakers have raised concerns about the potential politicization of the traditionally neutral US military.

World.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal training camp after coach says he is dropped
World.content:
Copenhagen – Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Wednesday that he had left the team’s training camp in Denmark after coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the striker would be dropped for their next match.

Ronaldo had been due to train with his team-mates at the Parken stadium in Copenhagen on Wednesday but left abruptly after Jesus’s press conference.

The veteran coach had said that Ronaldo, who spent the entire match on the bench against Norway on Sunday, would not start Thursday’s Nations League clash away to Denmark either.

“Following the national team coach’s press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.

“In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

“Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception.”

Jesus had insisted earlier that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old did acknowledge that his captain had been disappointed to remain on the bench in the side’s Nations League win over Norway.

– ‘No incident’ –

Following the 2-1 victory in Oslo, Ronaldo went straight to the changing rooms without joining his team-mates in acknowledging the Portuguese supporters in the stands.

“There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus told reporters.

“Any player –- and I was a player myself… when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don’t get on… no one is happy about that,” Jesus said on Wednesday.

The Portuguese coach added that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he would not be in the starting line-up, but that he might bring him on towards the end of the game.

“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It’s nothing to make a fuss about,” Jesus insisted.

The former Benfica boss also explained that Ronaldo had not refused to train on Tuesday, as some Portuguese media outlets had suggested, but that he had had to do individual exercises for physical “mobility” and “strengthening”.

Jesus had said that the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would train as normal on Wednesday, however, despite arriving at the stadium in the team bus, Ronaldo did not join his team-mates on the pitch in Copenhagen.

Portuguese media shared a video of him leaving the Parken stadium alongside two members of the backroom staff just after Jesus’s press conference.

They also said that Ronaldo’s private jet was heading to Copenhagen.

Just before Ronaldo’s social media post, the Portuguese federation had released a brief statement merely confirming that the former Real Madrid, Manchester United and Juventus player had not trained.

Jesus had said earlier that for the Denmark match he again intended to start AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos, who scored the winner against the Norwegians.

“If everything goes according to plan, it will be Goncalo who plays,” he said, before adding regarding Ronaldo: “If I need him, he’ll come on. If I don’t need him, he won’t.”

At 41, Ronaldo announced this summer that this season would “probably (be) my last year in football”.

He is Portugal’s leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.

World.title: Will Amrinder Singh Warring resign as Punjab Congress president? His response: 'No comments'

World.title: SC refuses to unfreeze TMC bank accounts, asks Calcutta HC to expedite hearing
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a plea by the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction seeking permission to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts, declining to interfere with a Calcutta High Court order that had rejected the request.

A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale noted that the Election Commission has frozen the party symbol and that the larger question of who is entitled to the funds in the accounts remains pending adjudication.

"We refrain from going into the merits. We are not inclined to exercise our jurisdiction under Article 136. We request high court to expedite the hearing," the bench said.

The TMC had sought permission to operate four accounts with public sector banks that were debit-frozen by the West Bengal Police, arguing that the FIRs related to the freeze contained procedural lapses.

Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has frozen Rs 440 crore in three accounts held by the party with HDFC Bank as part of its investigation into the alleged laundering of Rs 160 crore in party funds through Kolkata-based Carewell Aviation.

The agency alleges that the funds were used to purchase an Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft and an Agusta helicopter for Rs 112 crore through what it described as dubious transactions.





The ED said the aircraft and helicopter were later rented to the TMC, with substantial amounts transferred on the pretext of their use.

âThe Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft and Agusta helicopter were rented to TMC itself, even though they were purchased from the corpus of the party, and substantial amounts were transferred on the pretext of aircraft usage. The above stated dubious arrangement is under probe to ascertain the actual beneficial purpose of the transactions,â the ED said.

World.title: 'Incredibly proud': SpiceJet lauds Captain Smit Machchhar, who flew with airline for 11 years
World.content:
NEW DELHI: SpiceJet, the Gurugram-based budget carrier and former employer of Captain Smit Machchhar, on Thursday praised the pilot after he was stabbed by his co-pilot aboard an Israel-bound flight but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and overpower the attacker.

Chairman and Managing Director Ajay Singh said that "all of India and SpiceJet" is "incredibly proud of him."

"I was incredibly proud to know of this, but this is the job of a pilot. His job is to protect the lives that have been entrusted to him. And in this case, 180 lives were entrusted to Captain Smit Machchhar, and he did a tremendous job saving and preserving those lives. So really incredibly proud of him. All of SpiceJet is proud of him, and of course, all of India is proud of him," Singh told ANI.

"The first thing that will go through a pilot's mind is preserving lives, saving lives. And remember that in this case, what really saved lives was the fact that he was able to open the door of that cockpit, and let me tell you that the handle which allows that door to be opened is actually on the co-pilot's side. So, it would have needed real courage, after being stabbed, to reach out to the co-pilot side and somehow find a way to unlatch that door.





So the fact that he was able to do it essentially saved those lives because then passengers and other pilots were able to come into the cockpit and help him overpower the co-pilot and fly the plane back," he added.

The captain was also able to activate the cockpit door emergency release mechanism, communicate with the crew on board and send an emergency communication signal.

"The mechanics are that the cabin crew or anybody on the outside can punch a code in that door.

But the door still doesn't open. It needs the captain to physically unlock the door. And that unlocking mechanism is actually on the side of the co-pilot. In this case, the co-pilot was actually attacking the captain, and he still managed to reach out and find a way to unlock that door. And that is possibly what saved lives," the SpiceJet chairman and managing director said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Machchhar, who spent 11 years with SpiceJet, has more than 13 years of commercial aviation experience and has logged 9,750 flying hours, primarily operating Boeing 737 aircraft.

He later joined UAE-based airline flydubai, where he currently serves.

On Wednesday, the flight was en route from Dubai to Israel's Tel Aviv when Machchhar was stabbed by the co-pilot, reportedly an Omani national. The flight was later diverted to Saudi Arabia's Tabluk, where it made an emergency landing. Around 180 passengers, mostly Israelis, were on board.

Machchhar is currently recovering at a hospital in the kingdom and is in stable condition, according to the Indian Embassy in Riyadh.

World.title: ‘Voices against electoral 'capture' getting louder': Congress targets EC over SIR
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Thursday said the âchorus of voicesâ against what it called the âcapture of the electoral systemâ was growing louder, and asserted that citizens would no longer tolerate âvote choriâ in any form.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh made the remarks while citing former chief election commissioner O P Rawatâs criticism of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Ramesh alleged that nearly 14 crore voters had already been disenfranchised through the exercise.

âIn an interview to a leading national daily, Former CEC O.P. Rawat has questioned the SIR and the violations committed by the ECI.

It is âthe first time since Independence that so many eligible voters have lost their voteâ,â Ramesh said in a post on X.

He further cited Rawat as saying that the Election Commission, once considered the âgold standardâ, had lost credibility and that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi should have done more to oppose decisions they disagreed with.

INDIA bloc announces protests

The Congress's latest attack came a day after the INDIA bloc announced a joint campaign against what opposition parties have described as irregularities in the electoral process.





At a meeting attended by leaders of 19 opposition parties, the bloc announced joint âSave Democracyâ marches across districts and five major rallies. Opposition MPs are also scheduled to march to the Election Commission on October 6, while opposition leaders plan to meet the President over alleged irregularities in voter-list revision.

World.title: 'Prevented another 9/11': PM Modi heaps praise on flydubai pilot Captain Machchhar
World.content:

also praised the wounded pilot, saying he had "prevented another 9/11" â a reference to the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks in New York City, when Al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked passenger planes and crashed them into the World Trade Center, killing thousands.

His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy. India is proud of Captain Machchhar. Praying for his speedy recovery, renewed strength and good health," he wrote.

World.title: ‘Might as well disband you’: SC slams UP police for cover-up job
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Wednesday slammed Uttar Pradesh police for not naming the accused in a road accident case despite the complainant catching him on the spot and handing him over to police.

It said it would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI if the state police worked with an agenda and did cover-up jobs.

A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva asked why the state police should not be disbanded in view of its functioning.

âIn everything you have an agenda. How will people trust you if this is how you proceed with matters? It is better if we ask the CBI to step in all UP police investigations.

We might as well disband UP police. This nonsense has to stop at some point,â the court said.

How will people trust police: SC

Supreme Court added that the affidavit filed by Shobhit Kumar, circle officer of Khurja in Bulandshahr, who was directed to give an explanation, was âutterly uninspiringâ.

âToeing the line is one thing but bending over is another. And this kind of cover up job... less said the better,â SC said and summoned the officer to be present in court to give an explanation on his conduct.





âThe said officer shall be present before court on next date to account for the same. It would be open to him to file a better affidavit explaining as to why FIR No. 195/2026 was filed on Aug 19 against an unknown motorcycle rider when it is the admitted fact that the said rider was apprehended at the spot. In paragraph 6 of aforestated affidavit, the name of the motorcycle rider is disclosed as Tushar s/o Prempal. The reason as to why the name was left blank in the FIR initially and was, thereafter, supplemented, requires to be explained,â the bench said in its order.

World.title: Hashim Musa, key Pahalgam plotter, killed
World.content:
SRINAGAR/ NEW DELHI: In a joint operation by Army, police and security forces, a top Pakistani

terrorist, identified as Mohammad Asif, alias Hashim Musa, was killed in an overnight encounter in the upper reaches of Yousmarg, around 60km from Srinagar.

With his elimination, the entire group of four LeT commanders who had been operating in J&K since 2022 and were also behind the Pahalgam massacre has been wiped out. Home ministry called it a massive victory. Intelligence agencies had been tracking for two years the whereabouts of this former Pak Special Service Group (SSG) commando who had infiltrated into the Valley.

Musaâs neutralisation blow to LeT network

Neutralisation of Musa is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in J&K,â the ministry said in a statement.

This group was responsible for a string of sensational and deadly attacks across the region. The Musa-led squadâs terror trail included the Kandi attack in Rajouri (May 2023) where five Army personnel were killed, the Halan attack (Aug 2023), and the Dera Ki Gali ambush (Dec 2023) where terrorists targeted two Army vehicles, killing several soldiers.

The group also orchestrated the June 9, 2024 attack on a bus carrying Hindu pilgrims in Reasi, killing nine and wounding 40. They were linked to the Oct 2024 Gagangir attack in Ganderbal, which claimed the lives of seven, and the Bootapathri attack near Gulmarg that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The violent spree culminated in the devastating April 2025 Baisaran Valley attack in Pahalgam, where the terrorists massacred 26 tourists and a local horseman.

World.title: Gen-2 joined green crackers | Explained
World.content:
Story so far: On September 30, the Supreme Court ruled out a nationwide firecracker ban and accepted CSIR-NEERI’s recommendation for a “limited and conditional relaxation”. This allows the manufacture of next-generation joined green crackers that meet noise, emission and safety norms ahead of Diwali. The Bench said it would not permit 24-hour bursting and would consider fixed time windows.

What are ‘green’ crackers?

They are crackers whose chemistry has been reworked to release less particulate matter than conventional ones, without losing brightness, sound or shelf life. NEERI’s (CSIR-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute) changes include additives such as zeolite, water-releasing compounds that act as dust suppressants, and metallic composites that improve combustion. Conventional crackers rely on barium nitrate, antimony and other metals linked to respiratory disease.

The label is a misnomer, as there is nothing environmentally friendly about these crackers. NEERI’s own scientists have called them “reduced emission fireworks”. NEERI claims that the earlier generation of ‘green crackers’ saw a 30% cut in particulate matter. Its newer analysis says that the newer variants, called ‘Gen-2’, reduce pollution 45%-60% for PM10 and PM2.5, using formulations with less barium. However, these are laboratory figures, not verified in real-world conditions. Only manufacturers with a licence from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), the central explosives regulator, can register with NEERI.

Why are we discussing green crackers now?

The Court has put a time-limited, conditional endorsement on a specific product, the “joined” cracker, a string of crackers burst in sequence. NEERI says the new version bursts five braids a second instead of 25, stretching the burn fivefold. Smaller shells have cut solid waste by 4% to 32%. Noise must stay within 125 dB(AI)/145 dB(C) peak, and barium-based ingredients are restricted.

The science is still unfinished. NEERI is modelling how barium from Gen-2 crackers disperses in Bhopal, Delhi, Kolkata and Chennai, with results due by October 15. The Court has also given the Central Pollution Control Board and the Centre more time for barium and decibel tests.

What prompted their development?

Delhi-NCR’s winter smog and the cracker ban. Petitions were filed in the Supreme Court in 2015 over Delhi-NCR’s winter smog. In November 2016, the Court suspended licences for firecracker sales in the region, and in October 2017 it banned sales. The next year, it laid down the framework that, until now, allowed only reduced-emission ‘green’ crackers and barred barium salts and ‘joined’ crackers.

From 2025: Have ‘green’ crackers brought down pollution?

The September 30 order relaxes that framework for a redesigned version of the joined cracker, subject to NEERI’s conditions. NEERI began developing the formulations that year. In January 2025, the Court extended the firecracker ban to the NCR areas of Uttar Pradesh and Haryana. However, the ban hit a largely small-scale informal industry. Green crackers, the Centre has argued in the past, are meant to balance public sentiment during festivals, pollution and livelihoods.

Does Delhi’s winter-pollution plan say anything on crackers?

The Delhi Government announced its Winter Action Plan 2026-27 on September 29. Reported measures include 50% work from home from November 1, doubled parking charges and a full construction and demolition ban from December 10 to January 20. Non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside Delhi will be barred from November 1. There are no strictures on firecracker dos and don’ts.

From 2025: Fire in the sky: on Deepavali and the battle for clean air

What is IMD’s latest outlook?

In 2024, IMD warned that firecrackers and stubble fires could push Delhi’s air into the “severe” category when dispersion conditions are unfavourable. The monsoon’s withdrawal is expected to be complete from India by mid-October, which will see the onset of atmospheric conditions such as a cessation of high-altitude winds (that flush pollutants), lower temperatures and an inversion layer that traps pollutants. With Diwali expected in the first week of November, it remains to be seen how all of this will play out with ‘green crackers’ in the mix.

World.title: Madras High Court takes up suo motu PIL for removal of caste appellations from names of streets, roads, and localities in Tamil Nadu
World.content:
The Madras High Court on Thursday (October 1, 2026) took up a suo motu public interest litigation (PIL) petition to enforce a series of directions it had passed over the years to ensure the removal of caste appellations from the names of streets, roads, and localities across Tamil Nadu.

The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan directed the State government to submit a status report within four weeks, listing out the references that had been removed so far and those that were yet to be removed.

The suo motu PIL petition was taken up on the basis of the latest order passed by Justice N. Ramesh on August 11, 2026 – his maiden order after being elevated as a judge of the High Court. In his order, the single judge had lamented the existence of such appellations.

After coming across a First Information Report (FIR), in which Sendhamangalam police in Namakkal district had referred to a place as ‘Pallar Street,’ the judge had wondered how such appellations continued to exist despite a series of judicial directions and government orders passed since 1978.

The judge had told State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan that a Government Order issued in 1978 had insisted upon all local bodies to identify caste appellations in the names of streets and roads and remove them. Thereafter, the High Court, too, had issued a series of directions since 2018.

Justice Ramesh had said that the naming of a street or a road after a caste had serious consequences, as the residents of those places get identified by their caste, and those names get reflected in every other official document, such as their ration cards, Aadhaar cards, driving licences, and so on.

Highlighting the constitutional imperative to create a casteless society, the judge had also said that it was in that direction that Justice D. Bharatha Chakravarthy of the High Court had recently ordered the removal of caste appellations from the names of all schools and colleges located across Tamil Nadu.

Justice Ramesh had also referred to the Tamil Nadu government recently renaming the Adi Dravidar Welfare Department as Social Justice Department in order to avoid reference to a caste and said, the exercise would remain incomplete unless all caste appellations were removed completely from the names of streets and roads.

Since he had come across the FIR during the hearing of a bail petition, the judge had directed the High Court Registry to register a suo motu case with respect to the deletion of caste appellations from the names of streets and roads and place it before the Chief Justice for appropriate orders.

World.title: ‘Very perturbed’, draft electoral roll cannot be basis for deleting names without hearing: Bombay HC at Goa
World.content:
The draft roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) cannot be the basis for deletion of names from the voter list, the Bombay High Court has said, holding that administrative software systems cannot supersede statutory laws.

The Goa Bench of the HC also questioned the Election Commission of India (ECI) on the provisions empowering it to delete names without a hearing, saying it was “very perturbed by this”.

The Division Bench of Justice Amit S. Jamsandekar and Justice Valmiki Menezes was hearing a petition on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) filed by six members of a family over deletion of their names from the voter list.

Petitioners Paresh Salgaonkar and his family members told the Court that they had moved to a new house in the same Santa Cruz Assembly constituency and were instructed by the BLO (Booth Level Officer) to submit Form 8 for change of address.

At the time of processing these forms, they said, errors showed up since no record of their Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPIC) was found, and as such, the only option available in the ERONET software was “reject”.

ERONET (Electoral Registration Officers’ Network) is a web-based form-processing and electoral roll management system developed by the ECI.

Mr. Salgaonkar said that the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer informed them that their EPICs had been deleted from the rolls and consequently, their Form 8 applications could not be processed.

“The only recourse available was to submit Form 6 since there was no option in ERONET for reviewing or restoring the deleted EPICS,” the petitioners said, adding that Form 6 was applicable only to first-time electors seeking fresh inclusion of their names in the voter list.

Since they were existing electors, they were required to apply under Form 8 to seek a change of address within the same Assembly constituency, the petitioners said.

The Court ruled that the draft roll cannot be the basis for deletion of voters’ names.

“Otherwise, Form 6, 7 or 8 have no meaning. Form 6, 7 and 8 are specifically for either a person who is a new voter, a person who has lost the right to vote, or a person who is shifting,” the court said.

The Court told the ECI that the “software system did not allow” it to accept Form 8. “He was never a new voter. He was an existing voter. He became new for your system,” the Court said.

The Bench questioned the ECI on the provisions empowering it to delete names without a hearing.

The judges said, “Show us from the Act…what empowers you to delete without hearing?… Your officers were helpless, and they just decided to throw it on the system. So, they recorded it in the order, saying that the system has rejected. We are very perturbed by this…we are just wondering how many more who have not come to court.”

The Bench said that once a Form 8 is received, the authority must “apply its mind and see whether this person has really moved (to a new address)”.

The judges said such actions will take lakhs of citizens off the rolls. “Here there is only one family. Take a situation where there are so many people who have shifted residence,” the Bench said.

World.title: India's manufacturing sector growth hits seven-month high in Sept. 2026 on strong demand: PMI
World.content:
India's manufacturing sector activity growth touched a seven-month high in September, boosted by accelerating new orders and output that fuelled solid expansion in factory hiring, a monthly survey reported on Thursday (October 1, 2026).

Indian manufacturing activity regained its upward momentum in September, driven by strong domestic and export demand. Moreover, business optimism reached a four-month peak.

The seasonally-adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose by more than two index points in September, to 55.1 from 52.8 in August, signalling the strongest improvement in the health of the sector for seven months.

In the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), a print above 50 means expansion, while a score below 50 denotes contraction.

"India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, Chief India Economist at HSBC, said.

On the price front, there were quicker increases in both input costs and selling prices, but rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.

Firms also procured more materials for use in production processes and to add to inventories. Overall buying levels expanded at a quicker pace than in August.

"Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Mr. Bhandari said.

Strong demand across electronics, food, pharma, and textiles pushed total sales growth to its highest level since February. Moreover, export orders also expanded at a quicker pace from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the U.S.

According to panellists, job growth resumed in September, following a blip in the previous month and the pace of expansion in employment was solid and the most pronounced since May.

Indian manufacturers upgraded their output forecasts in September, with the overall level of positive sentiment rising to a four-month high. This positive outlook was driven by a healthy pipeline of new inquiries and expectations of sustained strong demand.

Expecting stronger demand ahead, manufacturers actively built up inventory. "Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.

The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global from responses to questionnaires sent to purchasing managers in a panel of around 400 manufacturers.

World.title: Pilot attacked in flydubai altercation Indian
World.content:
The captain who was attacked during an altercation inside the cockpit of a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday (September 30, 2026) is an Indian national, Captain Smit Machchhar.

Mr. Machchaar was previously employed with SpiceJet

In a press statement, flydubai has called the incident aboard FZ 1073 “an altercation”.

“At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation,” according to the press statement.

The airline said that the aircraft was successfully secured by on-duty flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport (TUU) in Saudi Arabia, and that all passengers and crew were safe and accounted for.

flydubai, in a statement, said that flights to and from Israel will be suspended while the investigation regarding the incident continues.

Praise from PM Modi, Netanyahu

Prime Ministers Narendra Modi and Benjamin Netanyahu said that Mr. Machchhar was a ‘hero’ for his intervention.

“In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy. India is proud of Captain Machchhar,” Mr. Modi said.

“My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery. Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster. He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals,” Mr. Netanyahu said in a statement.

Pilot Machchaar receiving necessary medical attention: Indian Embassy

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said that it has been following the health condition of Mr. Machchhar along with the Consulate in Jeddah. “He is admitted in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia and receiving necessary medical attention. A full update on his health is awaited but he is reported to be in stable condition,” the embassy posted on X.

“We hope that he recovers from his injuries at the earliest. We are in touch with his family and assure them that we will continue to follow up on his health with Saudi authorities and extend all possible assistance for his wellbeing.”

World.title: Kerala HC denies plea by Pakistani national married to Indian man seeking visa to enter country
World.content:
The Kerala High Court recently ruled that a Pakistani national could not demand that the government consider her visa application even if she was married to an Indian citizen.
