World.title: 17,000 Shipwrecked Relics Given to Chinese Research Centers
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019075/17,000 Shipwrecked Relics Given to Chinese Research Centers
World.content:
Over 17,000 artifacts recovered from a more than 700-year-old shipwreck off the coast of eastern China have officially been transferred to several Chinese archaeological institutions.

At a Monday ceremony in Zhangzhou City, in the eastern Fujian province, the artifacts were distributed among the Archaeological Research Center of the National Cultural Heritage Administration, the Fujian Provincial Institute of Archaeology, and the Zhangzhou Museum, among others.

The handover marks the first implementation of nationwide trial guidelines issued in July by the National Cultural Heritage Administration. The directive aims to standardize archaeological relic preservation, research, and display, citing an increasing number of archaeological excavations and findings in the country.

Under the new rules, archaeological teams must transfer recovered artifacts to state-owned museums, libraries, or cultural institutions within six months of submitting excavation reports to the National Cultural Heritage Administration and provincial cultural heritage authorities.

The recently transferred artifacts come from a shipwreck dating back to the late Yuan dynasty (1279–1368). Measuring 17 meters long and 4.5 meters wide, the wreck was discovered in 2014 in the waters between Zhangzhou and the nearby Shengbeiyu islet, where the Maritime Silk Road’s southern and eastern routes intersect. The site lies about 30 meters below the surface and is surrounded by reefs and complex waters, making the area prone to shipwrecks.

More than 20,000 artifacts were recovered from the wreck between 2022 and 2023, including over 17,000 celadon — or green-glazed porcelain — bowls, plates, cups, and incense burners. Other finds include pottery jars, lead weights, and seals.

The relics come from the Longquan kiln in the eastern Zhejiang province, one of the largest ceramic production centers in Chinese history and a major source of porcelain for overseas markets. Spanning 1,700 years and renowned for its distinctive jade-green and light-blue glazes, the kiln’s wares became an important commodity in maritime trade networks, reaching markets around Asia and Europe.

Some of the pieces from the shipwreck, including their inscriptions, are unusually large, offering clues about how Chinese kilns adapted their products for overseas markets, according to historical experts.

The ship’s cargo, along with similar finds in east China, suggests it may have set sail from Zhejiang’s coastal Wenzhou City for southeast Asia as a privately operated trading vessel.

“The excavation of the shipwreck marks an important milestone in China’s underwater archaeology,” Liang Guoqing, who led the excavation team, told local media. “It has also allowed the public to see firsthand the thriving trade in Longquan celadon and the prosperity of the Maritime Silk Road during the late Yuan dynasty.”

Archaeologists at the Archaeological Research Center of the National Cultural Heritage Administration said the wreck is also the first Yuan dynasty ship discovered in China with a fully preserved bilge keel — a structure attached to the bottom of a vessel to reduce roll. The discovery provides rare physical evidence for the study of ancient Chinese shipbuilding and navigation.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: Ceramics inside the Yuan Dynasty shipwreck near Zhangzhou, Fujian province. Xinhua)

World.title: [DECODED] No, this ‘handsome’ Duterte grandson is not real
World.content:
Sharp features, styled hair, and easy confidence in front of a camera. At first glance, Lance is your stereotypical content creator. Adding to the charm is his surname: Duterte.

Lance Duterte is supposedly the son of Vice President Sara Duterte and grandson of former president Rodrigo Duterte. This has helped him rack up thousands of swooning comments and online supporters.

And in true Duterte fashion, he is often seen posing with a fist bump for photos at different locations — like Luneta Park and Davao City Hall. If that’s not enough proof of his lineage, he has also been posting photos with his supposed family, like his “aunt” Kitty and mother Sara.

There’s one problem with this almost-too-perfect image: he is not real.

Unmasking the synthetic persona

Lance established his identity through his Facebook profile, “Lance Duterte (Official Account),” with over 382,000 followers on Facebook.

DIGITAL IDENTITY. The Facebook profile of Lance Duterte. Rappler screenshot

He recently caught the public’s eye when he shared his photos posing in Luneta Park.

HARD LAUNCH. A Facebook post by Lance Duterte showing photos of him in Luneta Park. Rappler screenshot

But a closer look at the images exhibits visual signs that they are AI-generated, such as jumbled letters at the Rizal Monument, the absence of the Torre Manila condo behind the monument, and an inaccurate shadow of Lance.

VISUAL INCONSISTENCIES. A photo of Lance Duterte in front of the Rizal Monument shows telltale signs that it was AI-generated. Photo from the “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” Facebook page, graphics added by Rappler

​AI image detection tools Hive Detect and Sightengine rated the image as 99.9% likely to be AI-generated, while ZeroGPT and DeepAI gave it a 91% AI-likelihood score.

​Lance also posted photos of him posing warmly with the Vice President and her husband, Manases “Mans” Carpio, and another set of pictures with Veronica “Kitty” Duterte and Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte. The same AI image detection tools said the pictures were AI-generated, but they were not labelled as AI content on Facebook.

FAMILY PHOTOS. Screenshots of Facebook posts by Lance Duterte with pictures of him with members of the Duterte family. Rappler screenshots

Supporters of the Duterte family also reposted photos of Lance, echoing the narrative that he is related to the Duterte family.

ONLINE DEBUT. Screenshots of Facebook posts from other pages about Lance Duterte. Rappler screenshots

But in reality, it is publicly known that Vice President Duterte and Carpio only have three children: Mikhaila Maria (Sharky), Mateo Lucas (Stingray), and Marko Digong (Stonefish).

No official public record acknowledges his existence. His persona relies entirely on artificial intelligence to fabricate a person that does not exist.

Lance Duterte is the latest addition to the AI-generated media surrounding the Dutertes. Rappler has previously debunked AI-generated images and videos designed to draw sympathy and political support for the Duterte family.

These synthetic contents are circulating amid critical political events for the Dutertes: the impeachment trial of Vice President Duterte and the continued detention of former president Duterte at The Hague, Netherlands, as he awaits his trial in the ICC.

DUTERTE-CARPIO FAMILY. A screenshot of Vice President Sara Duterte posing for a family photo with her three children: Sharky, Stingray, and Stonefish, during her inauguration in Davao City on June 19, 2022. Rappler screenshot from the Inday Sara Duterte YouTube channel

Years of beautiful deception

Lance Duterte’s Facebook profile was created on September 26, 2021, serving as an alternative profile for another account named “Lance Kurt Duterte.”

PROFILE HISTORY. A screenshot of the transparency information of the “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” profile from Facebook. Rappler screenshot

Facebook disabled the latter account on January 27, 2025, after a series of suspensions from 2022 until 2024.

MULTIPLE STRIKES. Screenshots of posts by Lance Duterte stating that his “Lance Kurt Duterte” account was suspended and eventually disabled by Facebook. Rappler screenshots

The “Lance Kurt Duterte” account featured a different face in its profile picture compared to the Lance Duterte persona circulating today.

DIFFERENT FEATURES. A visual comparison of the profile photo of “Lance Kurt Duterte” in 2024 and an image of “Lance Duterte” today shows no resemblance. Photos from the “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” Facebook page

Rappler earlier fact-checked a claim in 2020 made by an account named “Lance Kurt Dong Duterte” that accused Tricia Robredo, daughter of then-vice president Leni Robredo, of allegedly sending hate messages to him. The account similarly claimed that he is the grandson of former president Duterte. Both of the Robredos have denied that the exchanges happened, and the account later became unavailable on Facebook.

Manufacturing charm for political capital

The “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” Facebook profile became active during the national campaign of Vice President Duterte and President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. in 2022. It became inactive in 2023, then posted about the Duterte family and the arrest of their ally, Pastor Apollo Quiboloy, in 2024.

TIDES TURNED. Screenshots of posts by Lance Duterte from 2022 to 2024, indicating a tone shift in commentaries about President Marcos Jr. Rappler screenshots

It became active again in 2025 to support Vice President Duterte and direct online attacks toward the Marcos Jr. administration, specifically after the arrest of former president Duterte over his crimes against humanity case in the International Criminal Court (ICC).

DEFENDING THE DUTERTES. Screenshots of posts published by Lance Duterte after the arrest of former president Duterte in 2025. Rappler screenshots

In 2026, the account consistently promoted pro-Duterte propaganda. It recently responded to veteran news anchor Korina Sanchez’s remarks that Davao City “looks left behind,” and posted Davao City infrastructure updates paired with pro-Duterte hashtags.

PRO-DAVAO PROPAGANDA. Screenshots of Facebook posts by “Lance Duterte (Official Account)” criticizing veteran anchor Korina Sanchez. Screenshots by Rappler

It also intensified its activity by humanizing the Lance Duterte persona with AI-generated content, attracting thousands of engagements from social media users. Posts about Lance have garnered comments from supporters, saying that he is ”handsome” and “soon to be an artist or politician.”

LANCE’S FANS. Screenshots of comments from various Facebook posts about Lance Duterte. Rappler screenshots

Lance’s online fame has even extended beyond his own Facebook accounts. ​A fan-run Facebook page created on September 26, 2026 now has more than 3,800 followers as of writing. The page actively posts AI-generated videos of Lance, which have amassed thousands of reactions each.

FAN PAGE. Screenshots of AI-generated videos of Lance Duterte posted by a Facebook page dedicated to him. Rappler screenshots

The Global Risks Report 2026 by the World Economic Forum identified misinformation and disinformation as one of the most crucial global concerns, emphasizing that it is now facilitated by AI. The United Nations’ Independent International Scientific Panel on AI has also said in its preliminary report that AI-driven disinformation weakens the information ecosystem and disrupts democracy. – Rappler.com

The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

World.title: Amaya Cojuangco shoots way to PH’s breakthrough archery silver in Asian Games
World.content:
ON TARGET. The Philippines' Amaya Amparo Cojuangco in action in the women's individual semifinal match against South Korea's Jungyoon Park in the 2026 Asian Games.

National team veteran Amaya Amparo Cojuangco ends the Philippines' 12-year drought for an archery medal in the Asian Games

MANILA, Philippines – Amaya Amparo Cojuangco struck a rare archery medal for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games in Japan as she claimed the silver in the women’s individual compound on Thursday, October 1.

A longtime national athlete, the 40-year-old fell just shy of the gold after a neck-and-neck 139-137 loss to Indonesia’s Nurisa Dian Ashrifah in the final at the Okazaki Central Park.

The finale went down to the wire, with Cojuangco and Ashrifah tied at 110-all heading into the fifth and final round, where the Indonesian edged the Filipina with back-to-back 10s on her final two arrows to close with a near-perfect 29.

Cojuangco managed just a trio of 9s for 27 as she settled for silver.

Still, the silver is the Philippines’ highest finish in Asian Games archery and the only other medal the country won in the sport in the continental showpiece after Paul dela Cruz bagged the bronze in the men’s individual compound in the 2014 edition.

“I wanted the gold. I super wanted the gold. I’m sad that I lost. But also grateful that I have the silver medal. I felt good, the shots were good, but they just did not land,” Amparo told POC Media in a mix of Filipino and English. “I can only do my best.”

Cojuangco became the first Filipino archer to advance to an Asian Games final by stunning an opponent from powerhouse South Korea, the most dominant country in the sport, as she took down Park Jung-yoon in a nail-biting 142-141 win.

Park trailed by just a single point going into the fifth end, 114-115, but Cojuangco did just enough, submitting a similar 27 score as the Korean to pull off the victory.

Cojuangco also beat Iran’s Bita Asheghzadeh Oskouei in the semifinals and China’s Wei Fangyao and Vietnam’s Le Pham Ngoc Anh in the first two rounds. – Rappler.com

World.title: Prosecution, defense clash over whether Duterte declared spouse’s 2 properties in SALN
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines – Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband Mans Carpio purchased two properties that cannot be found in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), the prosecution argued on Thursday, October 1.

Prosecutor Keith Flores handled the direct examination of two witnesses from the Land Registration Authority (LRA) to confirm the multi-million-peso properties in Davao Region sold to Carpio.

Davao City Register of Deeds IV Kathy Florence Baldonado said a lot in Matina, Davao City was sold to Carpio for P6 million in July 2024.

City of Samal Deputy Register of Deeds III Marco Pineda said Carpio also bought a property on the island for P3 million in 2018.

Both properties do not correspond to any entries in the Vice President’s SALN.

The prosecution wants Duterte removed from office for betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution in connection with her alleged unexplained wealth.

“We clearly mentioned in Article 2… that one of the allegations is that the Vice President failed to disclose in her SALNs all of her properties. And that’s impossible for us to have known of this property simply because it’s not disclosed in the SALN,” Flores said.

Defense lawyer Lindon Bacquel, however, claimed that the Matina property was declared in the SALN, listed as a residential lot in Barangay 74-A with an acquisition cost of P10 million and assessed value of P82,046.

“Don’t they usually put a lower amount to avoid paying taxes? Right?” Flores asked Baldonado, which the defense objected to for being speculative.

Bacquel also said that the Samal property referred to by the prosecution is listed in the 2019 SALN as a residential lot in Barangay Matanos, Kaputian District, IGACOS. The property was supposedly sold in 2013, had an acquisition cost of P4.04 million, and assessed value of P52,500.

Flores, however, said that the acquisition cost and date for that entry in Duterte’s SALN do not match the transfer certificate of title for the Samal property.

“They declared that the property was bought in 2013 yet the actual deed of sale was made in 2018, five years after. What is the penalty for perjury?” Flores said, but was cut off when Bacquel objected to the line of questioning. – Rappler.com

World.title: Prosecution drops Trillanes as witness in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
World.content:
SONNY TRILLANES. File photo shows civil society group The Silent Majority along with former senator Antonio Trillanes file plunder and graft charges against Vice President Sara Duterte before the Office of the Ombudsman on January 21, 2026.

(1st UPDATE) Former senator Trillanes says he asked the prosecution to remove him from the witness list

MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution withdrew its bid to present former senator Antonio Trillanes IV as its witness in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

“The prosecution has finally decided not to present former senator Sonny Trillanes. We seek the kind indulgence of the honorable impeachment court for the belated final position on this particular concern,” lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro told the court on Thursday, October 1.

In a separate statement, Trillanes said he requested the prosecution to remove him from the witness list.

“This way, the prosecution panel would be relieved from the pressure it is going through,” Trillanes claimed, adding he will hold a press conference on Friday, October 2, to disclose the content of his testimony.

The prosecution had intended to call Trillanes to the witness stand to testify on Duterte’s bank records.

Trillanes, back in 2016, leaked documents detailing years’ worth of bank transactions involving then-presidential aspirant Rodrigo Duterte and his family members.

During the impeachment proceedings at the House back in April, it was confirmed that the Dutertes’ transactions from Trillanes’ records matched with the AMLC records.

In total, the AMLC said there was a total of P6.7 billion in large and suspicious transactions that flowed through the bank accounts of Duterte and her husband Mans Carpio from 2006 to 2025. The amount is a huge disparity from the Vice President’s net worth, which peaked at over P90 million in 2025 based on her SALN. – Rappler.com

World.title: Why did SC junk petitions vs adjusted impeachment voting threshold?
World.content:
In its decision, the SC cites lack of legal standing and prematurity as reasons for dismissing the legal challenges

MANILA, Philippines – The Supreme Court (SC) dismissed the petitions against the adjusted voting threshold in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.

The Senate impeachment court’s September 23 decision stated that the court will count only the votes of senator-judges who are “legally and factually capable” of participating in the proceedings at the time of the vote. Originally, the two-thirds voting threshold was fixed at 16 out of 24 senators.

After this decision, at least three petitions were filed before the SC last month.

But in its decision, the High Court dismissed the petitions due to lack of legal standing and prematurity.

What do these grounds mean?

Watch Jairo Bolledo’s explanation. – Rappler.com

World.title: ShinyHunters website goes offline after FBI deadline expires
World.content:
The ShinyHunters group says on September 22 it had stolen data ;on almost ALL FBI Agents, and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job'

The website used by ShinyHunters, the group that claimed responsibility for a recent hack of thousands of FBI agents’ personal and sensitive data, went offline on Wednesday, September 30, a day after the group’s deadline for the FBI to retract or modify a statement about the group’s tactics and track record expired.

ShinyHunters, a prolific cyber extortion group with a long record of targeting major corporations around the world, told Reuters and other news organizations on September 22 that it had stolen data “on almost ALL FBI Agents, and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.”

A Reuters analysis of a sample of the data shared by the hackers subsequently revealed that the data contained extensive personally identifiable information, sensitive job role information, and psychiatric and medical information.

Reuters could not determine why the site was offline. ShinyHunters could not be reached for comment.

The hackers said they targeted the FBI in response to a May 2026 FBI advisory about the group that the hackers felt misrepresented their prior actions. They gave the FBI a week to either “correct or simply REMOVE” the advisory.

The advisory remains online. ShinyHunters later said it had no intention of publishing the data it stole and that it accomplished its goals.

The FBI said on September 23 that it was “actively and aggressively investigating” the breach. The agency declined to comment on Wednesday on whether it had taken any actions to force the hackers’ site offline. Brett Leatherman, assistant director of the FBI’s Cyber Division, urged the hackers in a video published on the agency’s website on September 29 to get in touch with the FBI “while the choice is still yours.”

Dutch police announced this week that on September 15 they had arrested a Dutch man in connection with an investigation into ShinyHunters. The hacking group told Reuters the man had “no association” with them and mocked the Dutch police as “incompetent.” – Rappler.com

World.title: Dennis Uy loses Donatela resort after foreclosure, another blow to shrinking empire
World.content:
The luxury Bohol resort has been turned over to Landbank as Dennis Uy’s company struggles to overcome its overwhelming debt burden

MANILA, Philippines – Dennis Uy’s luxury Donatela Resort and Sanctuary in Panglao, Bohol, has permanently closed after the property was foreclosed, marking another retreat for the businessman whose debt-fueled empire expanded rapidly during the Duterte administration.

PH Resorts Group Holdings (PHR) disclosed that its wholly owned subsidiary, Donatela Hotel Panglao Corporation, permanently ceased operating the resort at the end of September 30.

Donatela Resort and Sanctuary was an exclusive luxury retreat in Panglao, Bohol, set on a sprawling tropical estate with private villas, landscaped gardens, a spa, and a cliffside restaurant overlooking the sea. The boutique resort catered to high-end travelers seeking privacy and seclusion.

The problem was all that luxury was built on debt that Uy’s company was never able to meet.

The land and improvements comprising the hotel had been mortgaged to United Coconut Planters Bank, which has since been absorbed by Land Bank of the Philippines, and were subjected to extrajudicial foreclosure proceedings. Donatela was to turn over possession of the property to Landbank by the end of September.

Donatela was considerably smaller than Uy’s failed flagship Emerald Bay casino project, but it still represented a sizable chunk of what remained of PHR’s asset base. The land, buildings, and other improvements pledged to Landbank for the Donatela loan had a carrying value of about P1.44 billion as of June 2026, about half of PHR’s P2.79 billion in total consolidated assets.

Its closure comes as PHR attempts a much broader restructuring of a business hollowed out by years of losses and liabilities. Just a week earlier, in a September 23 disclosure, PHR laid out plans to transfer its stake in PH Travel and Leisure Holdings – through which it owns Donatela and its other operating subsidiaries – back to parent Udenna Corporation.

“The Board determined that a comprehensive restructuring, involving the transfer of PH Travel to Udenna together with the rationalization of intercompany balances, offered the most direct and expeditious path to restoring PHR to a sustainable financial position, while providing a platform for future growth,” PHR said in its September 23 disclosure.

There is a lot of restoring to do. PHR’s consolidated stockholders’ equity was negative P5.953 billion as of June 30, while current liabilities exceeded current assets by around P4.01 billion. PHR is targeting a return to positive stockholders’ equity within two years after the restructuring. Restructuring, Uy’s company hoped, would remove most of the liabilities weighing on PHR and leave it operating largely as a listed holding company with no active business operations.

PHR’s 2025 financial statements show that strain clearly, with auditor SGV flagging a “material uncertainty” that could cast significant doubt on the parent company’s ability to continue as a going concern after it posted a P6.2-billion net loss, accumulated a P9.15-billion deficit, and recorded negative operating cash flow.

The Donatela foreclosure adds to the unraveling of the ambitions Uy built during the Duterte years. Uy, a major campaign donor of former president Rodrigo Duterte, snapped up everything from fuel, shipping, telecommunications, food, property, and gaming between 2016 to 2019. His meteoric rise drew scrutiny over his political ties to the administration, and the expansion itself leaned on borrowed capital.

Since then, PHR already lost control of the land and unfinished development behind its much larger Emerald Bay casino project in Cebu after its repurchase option expired in 2025, contributing to billions of pesos in losses. Its provisional gaming license was later revoked. – Rappler.com

World.title: AI Could Make Kazakhstan Regional Orchestrator, Says AI Strategist Olaf Groth
World.content:
ASTANA — The question of AI is especially relevant for Kazakhstan, which is betting big on the technology and preparing for the transformation ahead. AI is already reshaping economic models, changing the nature of work and creating new forms of competition between countries. It is also forcing governments to ask a bigger question: what kind of country do they want to become in an AI-driven world?

“AI is not just another tool set. AI is statecraft,” Professor Olaf Groth, AI strategist and member of Kazakhstan’s AI Development Council, said in a video interview with The Astana Times.

For Groth, the question is no longer whether governments should prepare for the AI transformation, but how they should build the foundations of an economy and a state that will remain competitive as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in public services, business and everyday life.

AI is statecraft, not just technology

Groth opened the interview with a high-stakes argument that AI should no longer be treated as another technology governments can adopt when it matures, because decisions about computing power, data, governance and AI infrastructure are increasingly decisions about a country’s long-term economic and strategic position.

“AI is not just another toolset. AI is statecraft. A government needs to set the right decisions early on, this means putting the right governance structures in place so that we can both check and control and manage tool performance, meaning returns on investment, but also ethical conduct and responsibility of the models that we’re deploying, the quality of the data, and the decisions that come out of it all,” he said.

For Groth, one of the clearest ways for governments to show they are serious about the technology is through their own use of AI, including procuring AI services and developing AI-led public services.

“Kazakhstan has been doing quite well on that front already, it having been recognized by the United Nations for digital government, and it needs to continue on that path because that’s where credibility comes from,” he said.

Kazakhstan’s window of opportunity

The conversation then turned to Kazakhstan’s position in the emerging geopolitical landscape of technology, where Groth sees an opportunity for the country to move beyond simply adopting technologies developed elsewhere. According to him, Kazakhstan’s progress in digital development and AI, combined with its geography, natural resources, agriculture and transit routes, puts it in a strong position to become “the orchestrator and the unifier of the region.”

“If it does that, then, you know, you are now accumulating a lot more economic and political weight in the world, right? And I think Kazakhstan is uniquely positioned to do that. And I think we’re seeing some deals already with countries that are neighboring countries,” he said.

Groth said he sees particular potential in creating a Central Asian data accord that could lay the foundation for an integrated regional data economy, allowing countries to exchange data while maintaining privacy, national agency and national security safeguards.

“That’s a pretty bold vision right there. You can trade data between countries in privacy and agency and national security assured ways, of course, because every country needs to make sure its citizens are well respected, right? But that would then enable Kazakhstan to put its AI into this data market as the engine that drives the data market,” he said.

As other countries develop their own AI hubs, Groth sees another challenge in connecting those hubs through the right protocols, creating the basis for what he described as a “bold vision for the cognitive economy in Central Asia,” one that is AI-driven and led by Kazakhstan, or at least orchestrated by it.

This role, however, would require more than technological capacity, as it would also depend on leadership capable of thinking beyond the next political cycle and building foundations for the decades ahead.

Building for the next decades

As with many of the conversations with AI experts about the future, the interview also moved from technology to leadership, with Groth drawing a distinction between leaders who are “trend chasers” and those who prepare their countries for structural transformation. He said that a forward-looking leader who wants to build solid foundations for the next 20, 30 or 40 years needs what he calls “a theory of the country.”

For Groth, that means understanding a country’s asset base and how those assets can be converted into competitive positioning in the global economy, while also asking why other countries would want to partner with it and what would allow it to enter those partnerships from a position of strength.

“In other words, asking yourself the question, why would anybody else be interested in Kazakhstan or in any country? And why would that country then come at the partnerships from a position of strength? So understanding the competitive assets, the competitive positioning, the state of the governance systems,” he said.

That also means understanding a country’s strengths and weaknesses, determining how AI can reinforce its governance model, and making sure technological transformation ultimately benefits the people expected to live with its consequences.

“Addressing all of that means that you have to lay foundations,” Groth said, adding that Kazakhstan is already making progress in laying educational foundations.

In his view, the distinction between long-term leadership and trend chasing is not difficult to identify. A trend chaser may be visible at ribbon-cutting ceremonies and on social media, while a serious leader is also willing to spend years building systems, infrastructure and partnerships whose results may not be immediately glamorous.

“Sometimes the building act is unglamorous,” Groth said.

The future of work: designing human-AI partnerships

The conversation also turned to one of the most immediate questions surrounding AI: what will happen to humans in a highly technological economy? Groth does not subscribe to the idea that the future necessarily means mass unemployment, arguing instead that work is deeply connected to human well-being because it provides people with purpose, identity and a sense that they are contributing to society.

At the same time, he believes that the relationship between work, earning and learning may change as AI takes over an increasing share of routine and analytical tasks, meaning that societies will have to deliberately design new ways for people to find purpose and meaning in the economy.

“There are many, many things that humans can do that AI cannot yet do. And so instead of just taking an axe and chopping people, which is the easy thing to do, we need to – comparatively easy – we need to embrace the comparatively more difficult thing, and that is design symbiotic jobs between humans and AI,” he said.

Groth believes that such a transition could ultimately create more satisfying and potentially better-paid jobs, but only if organizations deliberately redesign work rather than simply using AI as a justification for reducing headcount.

In the emerging agent economy, he sees a future in which people increasingly work alongside dozens, hundreds or even thousands of AI agents, with the human role shifting toward overseeing, governing and directing increasingly complex chains of tasks. But, again, Groth stressed that this will not happen automatically. The challenge is to design the interface between human capabilities and AI in ways that make people more productive without removing the sense of purpose that makes work meaningful.

From digital sovereignty to strategic sovereignty

The question of digital sovereignty brought the conversation back to Kazakhstan’s wider strategic position. Groth cautioned against interpreting sovereignty as complete digital self-sufficiency or isolation, arguing that the idea that countries can become entirely independent of global technological ecosystems is largely unrealistic.

“If by digital sovereignty, you mean digital autarky, or the ability to island yourself and be completely independent of everybody else, then no, I think that’s, as we say, in America, that’s a pipe dream,” he said.

For Kazakhstan, he said, the more realistic goal should be strategic sovereignty — understanding the country’s long-term path, deciding what it wants to become and identifying which capabilities it needs to build itself and which it can develop through partnerships.

“So what does that mean for Kazakhstan? I think it should be strategic sovereignty and strategic sovereignty means you figure out what your pathway is. What’s your vision? What kind of country does Kazakhstan want to become?” Groth said.

He pointed to Kazakhstan’s agriculture, critical mineral deposits, uranium, transportation infrastructure and growing digital layer as strategic assets that can form the basis of partnerships with other countries. He also highlighted the country’s space legacy and the continuing importance of Baikonur, as well as efforts to build an innovation ecosystem around the space sector.

For Groth, the value of these assets lies not simply in possessing them, but in using them to build partnerships and strengthen Kazakhstan’s position in the global economy.

“I think leveraging those key strategic assets, right, to attract partnerships and to become indispensable to those partners, that is sovereignty. Because then you can negotiate the terms for the future evolution of the country,” he said.

For full conversation, watch the entire interview here.

World.title: Kazakhstan and Denmark Entering More Dynamic Stage of Partnership, Ambassador Says
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan and Denmark are entering a more dynamic stage of their partnership, with the upcoming visit of Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen expected to strengthen political dialogue and expand economic cooperation, Kazakhstan’s Ambassador to Denmark and Sweden Olzhas Suleimenov told The Astana Times.

Rasmussen’s visit on Oct. 1-2 will combine high-level political engagement with a substantial business agenda. He is expected to meet with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and hold talks with Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi, while a Danish business delegation will participate in the Kazakhstan-Denmark Business Forum in Konayev on Oct. 1.

The visit comes ahead of the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Kazakhstan and Denmark in 2027.

“We see it as an opportunity to give fresh momentum to both political dialogue and practical cooperation,” Suleimenov said.

Suleimenov noted that the two countries already have a “solid foundation” for expanding their economic partnership. Denmark has invested nearly $400 million in Kazakhstan since 2005, while Danish companies including Carlsberg, FLSmidth, Novo Nordisk, Danfoss and Maersk are active in the Kazakh market.

One of the most tangible examples of this cooperation is Carlsberg’s new non-alcoholic beverages plant in the Almaty Region. The facility, representing a $344 million investment, is scheduled to officially open on Oct. 1 during the visit and is expected to create more than 230 jobs.

Strengthening economic cooperation

According to Suleimenov, one priority is to establish a stronger institutional framework for economic cooperation.

One expected outcome of the visit is a memorandum to establish a bilateral mechanism for trade, economic and investment cooperation. Suleimenov said such a mechanism could help move the partnership from individual initiatives towards regular engagement between the two governments and business communities.

“The Kazakhstan-Denmark Business Forum on Oct. 1 will be central to this, with concrete work expected in agriculture, industrial technologies, renewable energy, water solutions, transport and logistics, digitalization and pharmacy,” he said.

These sectors, according to Suleimenov, are areas where Danish expertise can complement Kazakhstan’s market potential and strategic location between Europe and Asia.

Focus on Middle Corridor

Another priority is deeper cooperation with Maersk on the Middle Corridor, also known as the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route.

A dedicated roundtable with Maersk, Kazakhstan Temir Zholy and prospective Kazakh partners was held in Almaty on Sept. 30. Suleimenov said the discussions are expected to translate into growing container traffic and the development of multimodal transport solutions.

The Middle Corridor connects China and Central Asia with Europe through Kazakhstan, the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan and Georgia, making it an important area for expanding transport and logistics cooperation between Kazakhstan and European partners.

Moving beyond livestock supplies

Agriculture is another area where Kazakhstan and Denmark see potential for expanding cooperation.

Suleimenov highlighted existing contacts with Danish companies including Viking Genetics, DanBred, FOSS, Vilomix and Thornico. Between 2011 and 2025, Kazakhstan imported more than 10,000 head of pedigree cattle from Denmark.

Suleimenov said Kazakhstan now seeks to move beyond supplying livestock and equipment toward localization, technology transfer and integrated dairy and livestock projects.

“I would like to see us move beyond the supply of livestock and equipment towards localisation, technology transfer, and integrated dairy and livestock projects here in Kazakhstan,” he said.

Suleimenov said the broader objective is to translate the existing political goodwill between the two countries into concrete projects, sustainable investment and lasting institutional ties.

“Our priority now is turning political goodwill into concrete projects, sustainable investment, and lasting institutional ties. Kazakhstan is ready to take this partnership forward, and we see Denmark as an important partner in Northern Europe,” he said.

World.title: Industrial Modernization, Investment in Focus of Tokayev’s Business Meetings in Munich
World.content:
ASTANA – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev began the second day of his official visit to Germany in Munich on Sept. 30 with a series of meetings with senior executives of Siemens AG, Linde and Aurubis AG, focusing on industrial modernization, technological cooperation and new investment projects.

During a meeting with Bernd Ulbricht, vice president for commercial and financial affairs at Siemens AG, Tokayev described Siemens as an important partner for Kazakhstan, noting that its expertise in industrial digitalization, electrification, mobility and smart infrastructure aligns with the country’s economic modernization priorities.

Tokayev welcomed a joint project between Siemens and Kazakhstan’s Silk Road Electronics to modernize equipment at the Qarmet metallurgical plant. He emphasized Kazakhstan’s interest not only in acquiring advanced equipment but also in establishing local manufacturing, engineering and service capabilities, reported Akorda.

The officials also discussed opportunities to apply Siemens technologies in modernizing Kazakhstan’s energy and utilities sectors, environmental monitoring, medical technologies and data center infrastructure.

In a separate meeting with Oliver Pfann, senior vice president at Linde, Tokayev welcomed the company’s plans for new projects in Kazakhstan with potential investments of up to $500 million. The officials noted an agreement between Linde and Qarmet to build a new air separation unit in Temirtau and discussed prospects for cooperation in the petrochemical industry.

Tokayev also highlighted Linde’s carbon capture and storage and hydrogen infrastructure technologies, inviting the company to participate in projects in the petrochemical and chemical clusters in the Atyrau and Mangystau Regions.

During talks with Fritz Vahrenholt, chairman of the Supervisory Board of Aurubis AG, the officials discussed potential investment projects in Kazakhstan’s mining and metallurgical sector. Tokayev emphasized the country’s priority of moving from a raw-material model toward deeper metals processing, advanced technologies and higher value-added production.

The discussions covered processing complex copper-bearing raw materials, recovering associated metals and recycling and localizing downstream production. Particular attention was given to cooperation between Tau-Ken Samruk and Aurubis on processing copper scrap and technogenic mineral formations in Kazakhstan, with the sides considering a joint action plan for prospective projects.

Kazakhstan-Germany cooperation in education and science

During a meeting with German university rectors and research institute heads on Sept. 30, Tokayev called for stronger cooperation between Kazakhstan and Germany in education, research, technology transfer and artificial intelligence.

Tokayev highlighted growing academic ties, noting that 45 Kazakh universities cooperate with around 100 German partners, while nearly 2,000 Kazakh students study in Germany.

He proposed expanding joint education and dual-degree programs, scientific research and technology transfer. He also invited German businesses to establish engineering laboratories and technology transfer centers at joint institutions in Kazakhstan.

Tokayev said cooperation should increasingly connect universities, research and industry and focus on developing technologies and products with higher added value.

World.title: Global Logistics Company Rhenus Advances Plans for Multimodal Terminal in Aktau
World.content:
ASTANA – Rhenus Group, a global logistics and supply chain company, and Aktau International Sea Trade Port are advancing plans to develop a trimodal container terminal in Aktau, designed to connect maritime, rail and road transport and strengthen Kazakhstan’s role as a key logistics hub along the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), or the Middle Corridor.

The agreement outlining the project’s next steps was signed on Sept. 30 during Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s official visit to Germany.

The project is part of Rhenus’ long-term strategy to strengthen transport links between China, Central Asia, the Caspian region and Europe, and supports the development of the Middle Corridor as part of the EU’s Global Gateway initiative, Rhenus press service reported.

“The strategic importance of the TITR is now hardly in question. The key challenge is to bring individual infrastructure projects together step by step into an efficient network in which capacity, operational services and strong partnerships work seamlessly along the entire route,” said Tobias Bartz, CEO and chairman of the Management Board of Rhenus Group.

Aktau to strengthen its multimodal role

The planned trimodal container terminal at Aktau International Sea Trade Port will connect maritime, rail and road transport. It will be developed on a site of at least 30 hectares and is expected to provide additional handling capacity of at least 150,000 TEU annually.

The project would increase capacity on the Caspian section of the TITR and strengthen Aktau’s role as a key logistics hub.

Rhenus is also working closely with Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ), the country’s state railway operator, to expand corridor capacity and build the infrastructure needed to accommodate growing cargo flows.

“Cooperation with Rhenus opens up new opportunities to develop Kazakhstan’s transit potential. The joint terminal project at the Aktau Port will become an important element of our logistics infrastructure and provide a foundation for deepening our partnership,” said Yelzhas Otynshiyev, KTZ chair.

The next stages will include an analysis of expected cargo flows and assessment of the project’s technical and economic feasibility.

Building an integrated logistics network

Rhenus has operated in Kazakhstan for 30 years and has expanded its presence through targeted investments. At the beginning of this year, the company acquired a rail-connected terminal in the Almaty Region, adding terminal, depot and multimodal capacity and strengthening the region’s links to international transport routes.

Beyond Kazakhstan, Rhenus is present in key markets along the Middle Corridor, including Azerbaijan, Georgia, Türkiye and Uzbekistan.

The company’s long-term objective is to integrate terminals, depots, rail and maritime services and freight forwarding activities along the route and connect them with its European logistics and terminal network.

The approach is intended to gradually develop individual infrastructure projects into a more reliable and predictable logistics network between Asia and Europe.

About Rhenus

Rhenus Group is a global logistics company with annual turnover of 8.2 billion euros (US$9.3 billion). It employs 39,000 people at 1,300 sites in more than 70 countries, providing transport, warehousing, customs clearance and other supply chain services.

World.title: Kazakhstan’s Energy Hinges on Diversification and New Investment, KIOGE 2026 Experts Say
World.content:
ALMATY – Kazakhstan’s position in emerging global energy value chains will increasingly depend on the resilience of its infrastructure, diversification of export routes and investment in new production and technology, speakers said at the strategic plenary session opening Kazakhstan’s International Oil and Gas Exhibition (KIOGE 2026) in Almaty on Sept. 30.

The session, dedicated to Kazakhstan’s role in new energy value chains, brought together senior officials and industry experts to discuss how geopolitical disruptions, changing trade flows and growing energy demand are reshaping the global oil and gas market.

Karen Oldhoven, moderator of the session, said Kazakhstan has positioned itself as an important link between major markets at a time of significant changes in the global energy system.

“This is a year of tectonic and geopolitical shifts and at the same time the world is getting more hungry for energy and despite all this Kazakhstan positions itself as a reliable partner and also a bridge for dialogue, cooperation and investment,” she said, highlighting that the next stage would require cooperation between industry participants, governments and experts to build Kazakhstan’s future energy ecosystem.

Resilient infrastructure becomes a priority

Suhail Mohamed Faraj Al Mazrouei, the United Arab Emirates’ Minister of Energy and Infrastructure, highlighted the impact of geopolitical disruptions on energy and commodity flows. According to him, countries are increasingly looking at projects that would allow hydrocarbons to be exported through multiple routes rather than relying on a single corridor.

“Something that is very important as well, other than the optionality and building other options, is to ensure the resilience and the security of the critical infrastructure. Because those infrastructures were attacked, unfortunately,” he said.

He also stressed the importance of international cooperation, noting that disruptions to major trade routes can affect markets well beyond the countries directly involved.

“If those veins of trade are restricted, threatened, all of us are going to pay the price. It’s not just one country,” Al Mazrouei said.

The emphasis on alternative routes and infrastructure resilience is particularly relevant for Kazakhstan, whose energy exports depend on several international transportation corridors and whose role as a link between East and West is expanding.

Energy markets face a new era of uncertainty

Philip Mshelbila, Secretary General of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, said the latest energy crisis demonstrated that geopolitical disruptions are likely to remain a recurring feature of global markets. The Gas Exporting Countries Forum brings together 20 countries holding about 70% of the world’s proven natural gas reserves, he noted.

“This conflict and the crisis that’s emanated from it has first of all taught us that geopolitical events are going to continue to happen. They will continue to happen more frequently. And we need to accept them as the new norm,” Mshelbila said.

He pointed to the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2022 conflict in Ukraine and the latest crisis as examples of major disruptions that have affected the energy sector within a relatively short period.

“What we just don’t know is what’s going to happen, when it’s going to happen, and where,” he said.

At the same time, Mshelbila said the global natural gas system had demonstrated a degree of resilience during recent disruptions. He cited accelerated projects, additional production from North America, deferred maintenance at energy facilities and increased upstream gas production as measures that helped compensate for supply losses.

“Between March and August, we estimated that about 39 million tons per annum of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) was taken off the market. Mainly between Qatar and the UAE. But, close to 34 million tons of that came into the market,” he said.

According to Mshelbila, this demonstrated that more than 80% of the potential LNG supply gap was compensated through various measures.

“There is already some degree of resilience in the natural gas system globally. It’s clearly not enough. And a lot more needs to be done,” he said, stressing that energy producers ultimately remain dependent on markets, even when they have sufficient resources and production capacity.

“Even if you have all the forms of energy that you need, in the quantity you need, you might actually have a surplus you want to sell to somebody. Which means you’re going to depend on the market,” he added.

Kazakhstan seen as investment and transit hub

Against this backdrop, Mshelbila pointed to Kazakhstan’s geographic position and resource base as factors that could support further investment.

“I think that Kazakhstan gives an example of an investment destination. That could welcome that sort of an investment. Because it is so strategically located between East and West. And it has its own resources in abundance. And it could actually serve as transit even more than it is already doing,” he said.

His comments come as Kazakhstan seeks to strengthen its role in regional energy and transport chains while attracting investment into both traditional and emerging parts of the sector.

KMG targets higher recovery from mature fields

For Kazakhstan’s national oil and gas company, maintaining production from mature fields remains a key part of the long-term strategy. KazMunayGas First Deputy CEO Kurmangazy Iskaziyev said the company has been working to increase output of refined petroleum products while diversifying transportation routes. However, he said expanding the company’s resource base is a central strategic priority.

“KazMunayGas has 65 producing fields, excluding major projects such as Kashagan and other large developments. About 90% of production from the company’s mature fields comes from 12 fields,” he said.

Iskaziyev said many mature fields have already depleted around 70% of their reserves, increasing the importance of identifying new resources, particularly in Paleozoic formations.

“The company has identified 23 projects and is working with the Ministry of Energy on improving the terms of the relevant contracts. The program includes 3D seismic surveys and the drilling of deep wells,” he said.

A second component involves large-scale exploration using 2D seismic surveys covering areas in the south and east of the Caspian region and the northern Caspian area.

Logistics increasingly shape oil prices

The discussion also moved beyond production to the ability to move energy products to consumers. Global Director for Refined Products, Platts and S&P Global Energy Francesco Di Salvo said current oil market dynamics cannot be explained by supply and demand alone, with logistics increasingly affecting prices and trade flows.

Speaking from the perspective of a company that provides benchmark price assessments, including Brent and CPC Blend, Di Salvo said the ability to transport crude from production sites to end users has become increasingly important.

“It is actually the ability to evacuate these molecules, to bring them from the production point to the delivery and consumption point and that is being made incredibly more difficult,” he said.

For Kazakhstan, this has direct implications for the value of its crude exports, including CPC Blend. He noted that shipping has increasingly become a key component of oil trade economics.

Refined products and changing trade flows

Di Salvo also highlighted the growing importance of refined products, particularly diesel, jet fuel and gasoline, whose values can increasingly diverge from crude oil prices. He linked this trend to the broader issue of diversification, particularly in Europe, where dependence on limited sources and routes has created additional energy security challenges.

Another major development, he said, is the reshaping of global trade flows driven by geopolitical developments and sanctions.

“We are really seeing a paradigmatic shift in the market, and I think it’s quite exciting to see, but also very challenging to have to play in this market,” he said.

The discussions at KIOGE 2026 highlighted a common idea across the different perspectives: Kazakhstan’s future role in global energy markets will depend not only on the availability of hydrocarbons, but also on the country’s ability to develop resilient infrastructure, diversify transportation routes, expand its resource base and adapt to changing global trade patterns.

The 30th KIOGE 2026 is taking place in Almaty on Sept. 30-Oct. 2, bringing together more than 500 companies from 62 countries to discuss the future of Kazakhstan’s energy sector, international cooperation and emerging technologies.

World.title: Hong Kong to Host Major Electronics Fairs in October
World.content:
ASTANA – The Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) will host the Hong Kong Electronics Fair (Autumn Edition) and electronicAsia from Oct. 13-16, bringing together more than 3,200 exhibitors to showcase the latest consumer electronics, smart products, electronic components and technology solutions.

The fairs will take place at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Center, providing a global platform for electronics companies, buyers, startups and technology innovators to explore new products and business opportunities.

Last year, the two fairs attracted nearly 60,000 industry buyers from 142 countries and regions, while bringing together more than 3,200 exhibitors.

Focus on AI, robotics and smart wellness

Now in its 46th edition, the Hong Kong Electronics Fair will highlight three key themes: AI and Robotics, Smart Wellness and NEXT Entertainment.

The AI and Robotics theme will feature more than 120 robots, showcasing advances in artificial intelligence, intelligent automation and robotics across industrial, commercial and everyday applications. The dedicated RoboPark zone will offer live demonstrations of robotic technologies.

The Smart Wellness theme will showcase digital health devices, smart wearables, personal care technologies, elderly-care solutions and other technology-enabled wellness products.

NEXT Entertainment will focus on XR technologies, smart gaming devices, digital content creation tools and other immersive and interactive entertainment solutions.

New zones for emerging technologies

The fair will also feature several dedicated zones, including the Hall of Fame, Startup Zone and the new Future Industries Zone, which will showcase innovations in Future Computing, Future Manufacturing, Future Marine & Quantum Technologies, Future Microelectronics and Future Wellness.

A new GoGlobal Connect Zone will provide businesses with one-stop professional support for international expansion and access to overseas markets.

Held concurrently, electronicAsia, organized by HKTDC and MMI Asia Pte Ltd, will focus on electronic components, parts and related solutions.

The four-day program will also include forums, conferences and seminars, where industry experts will discuss market trends and technological developments, while startups will have opportunities to connect with investors and industry professionals.

The registration is available here.

World.title: Kazakhstan Expects Above-Average Grain Harvest as 83% of Crops Collected
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan expects this year’s grain harvest to exceed the long-term average, with farmers having already harvested around 20 million tons of grain from 83% of planted areas, Deputy Agriculture Minister Nazgul Khatepova said at a Sept. 29 government press conference on the harvest campaign.

Kazakhstan’s grain harvest has typically stood at around 18-19 million tons in recent years, reported the Prime Minister’s press service.

The country has sufficient storage capacity to accommodate the new harvest, including carry-over stocks from previous years. Total grain storage capacity stands at 30.5 million tons, including 13.1 million tons at licensed elevators and 17.4 million tons at farms and agricultural enterprises.

Nearly 4.9 million tons of this year’s grain has already been placed in storage.

Potato exports seen at 400,000 tons

Kazakhstan expects a potato harvest of around 2.8 million tons, broadly matching last year’s level. The country exported 388,000 tons of potatoes last year, while this year’s export potential is estimated at 400,000 tons

Nearly 2.5 million tons have already been harvested. In the Karagandy and Pavlodar Regions, potatoes are currently selling for 90-100 tenge (US$0,23) per kilogram.

The Agriculture Ministry, together with local authorities and major retail chains, is working on advance contracting to help farmers export surplus potatoes.

Vegetable storage capacity sufficient

Existing vegetable storage facilities are also sufficient to preserve key produce through the off-season, according to the ministry.

Kazakhstan produces around 2.8-3 million tons of potatoes and 2.5-3 million tons of vegetables annually. The main types of produce require around 2.5-2.6 million tons of storage capacity. More than 700,000 tons of new capacity has been commissioned over the past three years.

Natural losses during harvesting, storage and transportation average 5-10%.

Beef prices remain stable

The domestic market remains fully supplied with locally produced beef, with no grounds for a sharp price increase, Khatepova said.

The average retail price is around 3,800 tenge (US$8,66) per kilogram nationwide, while prices in Astana start from nearly 3,800 tenge.

“Grounds for a sharp increase in prices are not observed. The domestic market is fully supplied through domestic production,” she said.

Kazakhstan produced 434,000 tons of beef last year, with production continuing to grow this year. The ministry said regional price fluctuations occur periodically, but no sustained upward trend has been recorded.

World.title: Tokayev, Merz Take Kazakhstan-Germany Partnership Forward as 30+ Deals Reach $2 Billion
World.content:
ASTANA – More than 30 commercial agreements worth around $2 billion are expected to give new impetus to Kazakhstan-Germany relations, as President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Chancellor Friedrich Merz discussed expanding cooperation in industry, critical minerals, technology, transport and other strategic sectors on Sept. 29 in Berlin.

Expanding trade and investment

Germany is one of Kazakhstan’s key trading partners and a leading foreign investor. Bilateral trade reached $4.5 billion last year, up 13.4%, while cumulative German investment in Kazakhstan has reached $8 billion over the past 21 years, Akorda reported.

Tokayev and Merz identified significant potential for cooperation in industry, critical minerals, transport and logistics, digital technologies, machinery and chemical production, notably in areas involving high-value-added products.

The joint investment portfolio currently includes 40 industrial projects worth around $54 billion.

Tokayev said Kazakhstan attaches particular importance to creating favorable conditions for German investors.

“Ensuring the security of German investments is under our special control,” he said.

New commercial agreements

On the first day of President Tokayev’s visit, more than 30 commercial documents worth around $2 billion were signed.

Tokayev highlighted the role of the Intergovernmental Working Group and the Kazakhstan-German Business Council in advancing bilateral economic ties and supporting joint projects.

He said effective implementation of the newly reached agreements would strengthen economic cooperation between the two countries.

Cooperation in technology and industry

The talks placed particular emphasis on expanding cooperation beyond traditional trade into technology, industrial production and innovation.

Tokayev is also scheduled to visit Bavaria and attend the Kazakhstan-Bavarian Technology Forum, where they are expected to discuss further opportunities for technological and business cooperation.

President Tokayev said Germany’s industrial strength, scientific expertise and technological capabilities provide a strong basis for expanding bilateral cooperation.

Central Asia-Germany cooperation

Both leaders also discussed regional and international cooperation and agreed to intensify engagement through international organizations, including the Central Asia-Germany format.

Tokayev described Germany as a reliable strategic partner for Kazakhstan in Europe and noted that the two countries would mark the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year.

He said bilateral ties have expanded across political, economic, investment and cultural-humanitarian spheres since diplomatic relations were established.

Tokayev and Merz also discussed expanding cooperation in education, science and culture, including joint initiatives in these fields.

Kazakhstan’s position on international issues

The talks also covered regional and global developments.

Tokayev reiterated Kazakhstan’s position that conflicts should be resolved through peaceful and diplomatic means, with respect for the principles of the UN Charter and the territorial integrity of states.

During the press briefing, an ARD correspondent asked Tokayev about his earlier remarks on the war in Ukraine. Tokayev clarified that his proposal to freeze hostilities aimed to create conditions for a transition to diplomatic negotiations.

Merz invited to Kazakhstan

Following the talks, Tokayev invited Chancellor Merz to visit Kazakhstan on a state visit next year.

The invitation comes as Kazakhstan and Germany prepare to mark 35 years of diplomatic relations, with both officials expressing an intention to further expand their strategic partnership across economic, technological, scientific and humanitarian fields.

The same day, Tokayev held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier to discuss the development of bilateral relations and prospects for further cooperation.

World.title: ‘Copper is to us what oil is to other countries’ – expert on Armenia’s mineral wealth
World.content:
Assessment of Armenia’s mineral resources

“Armenia does not have major oil or gas deposits with significant reserves. Instead, it can rely on substantial reserves of copper, molybdenum and gold, as well as rare elements and critical minerals. Gold, silver, copper, molybdenum and polymetals such as lead and zinc are currently in greatest demand. However, so-called critical minerals are gradually becoming increasingly important,” geologist Arshavir Hovhannisyan says.

The head of the Mineral Resources Department at the Institute of Geological Sciences of Armenia’s National Academy of Sciences says the terms “critical minerals” and “rare-earth elements” are sometimes confused in Armenia. He explains that critical minerals are elements, mainly metals, that are particularly important for a country’s industrial development, especially in high-tech sectors.

“Rare elements and rare-earth elements are among critical minerals. Copper, for example, is a critical mineral because neither batteries nor electric motors can function without it, but it is not a rare element,” he told Armenpress agency.

Copper, gold and silver reserves, but copper is key

“Copper is the queen of metals, the most important metal.

“We also talk about the importance of lithium, but it is likely to be replaced in the foreseeable future. Lithium is a rather unsuitable chemical element for use in batteries. It is highly flammable, performs poorly at high and low temperatures and has a limited number of charging cycles, after which it becomes unusable.

“Scientists are now looking for alternatives to lithium. Sodium and potassium are the most likely candidates. China is already producing sodium batteries using extremely cheap raw materials.

“Sodium, along with chlorine, is one of the main components of table salt, and Armenia has vast reserves of it. Yerevan is largely situated on salt deposits. The Ararat Valley, from Armavir to Arzni, lies entirely on salt deposits. If necessary, Armenia would have no difficulty obtaining extremely cheap raw materials.

Gold and silver can also be used in electrical equipment. The only element for which there is currently no substitute is copper.

“Copper is to us what, say, oil is to some other countries.”

Armenia’s copper reserves could last decades

“Reserves will be depleted in around 50-100 years unless we discover new deposits in the meantime. I think new deposits could be found because we have done virtually nothing in this area for about 35 years.

“Deposits that were not considered particularly promising during the Soviet period may now attract interest. First, technologies for extracting metals from ore have advanced. Second, the price of copper on the global market is rising rapidly.

According to Bloomberg estimates, by 2030-2040 global demand for copper will reach a level requiring 10-15 new mines to be brought into operation every year.

“I mean mines comparable in size to the large Kajaran deposit.

“According to various estimates, producing a conventional passenger car requires 10-15kg of copper, while an electric vehicle requires more than 50kg. Tens of millions of electric vehicles are produced each year. Simple arithmetic therefore gives an idea of how much pure copper will be needed for the automotive industry alone, with production volumes expected to continue growing.

“There are also other sectors where copper is essential, including electrification, modern technologies and the infrastructure supporting them.”

Oil and gas not worth considering

“The geodynamic processes that took place over tens of millions of years in the territory where Armenia is now located have left virtually no prospect of large hydrocarbon reserves.

“A large number of deep wells were drilled in Voghjaberd for research purposes, and similar exploration was carried out in Armavir. Some traces were found, including small amounts of gas. These are remnants of deposits that once existed, as well as accumulations formed more recently, over the past 30 million years. Given the geology and location, these cannot be large volumes.

“There is little reason to expect oil and gas deposits to be discovered in Armenia in the future.

Small deposits could potentially be found at great depths. But even finding them would be extremely costly, as numerous wells would have to be drilled.

“Even then, it would not be clear whether the gas discovered would last a month, an hour or a year. In any case, the volumes would be so small that they are hardly worth considering.”

Areas where rare elements could be found

“Demand for rare-earth elements and other minerals has risen sharply worldwide, along with their prices. They are in high demand in modern high-tech manufacturing.

“They attracted little interest in the past, but technologies have changed. We need to understand what resources we have.

We cannot say there is no chance of Armenia having rare-element reserves. There are geological areas in the country that could contain them.

“Further research is needed to establish this. Our institute has a dedicated group studying rare-earth elements, funded by a grant from the Science Committee. The research does not have an industrial or applied research component and is purely scientific, but the fact that it is being conducted is itself a positive development.

“The research covers potential mineralisation of lithium, selenium, tellurium and rhenium. Meanwhile, more than 20 other rare-earth elements have not previously been studied.

“Some have been identified incidentally during other research. As demand for them grows, we will have to explore them, whether we want to or not. If the state does not do so, the private sector will.”

Investment needed to explore new deposits

“Armenia is indeed very rich in mineral resources, both metallic and non-metallic. Kajaran, Sotk, Agarak and Teghut are all located within a relatively small area covering around 30-35% of the country. Moreover, Kajaran is among the world’s 10 largest mines by scale.

“The difficulties are related not to geology but to the terrain. In many cases, mines are located at altitudes of around 3,000 metres, in hard-to-reach areas, and deposits are often relatively small.

The chances of discovering new large deposits comparable in scale to Kajaran or Zod [Sotk] are very low. The chances of finding medium-sized and small deposits are higher.

“Exploration of new deposits will become possible if the state creates the necessary conditions for investment and also invests itself. At the very least, this would give us a clearer picture of the rare elements and critical minerals in Armenia’s subsoil. This would then be followed by detailed exploration and reserve estimates, an even more labour-intensive and costly process.”

World.title: From self-defence to political statements: how former Georgian PM Garibashvili’s ‘prison’ letters have evolved
World.content:
Analysis of former Georgian PM’s “prison” letters

Former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili has published his eighth letter from prison, which differs significantly from his previous seven. In the letter, Garibashvili looks back on his political career and presents himself to the public as a successful prime minister. The text effectively serves both as a political report and a statement of leadership ambitions.

In the letter, the former prime minister seeks to show that in 2021 he led the government out of a deep political and economic crisis and improved the country’s situation through his work.

At the end of the letter, he asks the public whether the situation has improved or deteriorated since he resigned. Although he does not directly name current Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, the question clearly challenges his administration.

“Almost three years have passed since then [my resignation], and I want to ask the people: has the situation in the country improved or deteriorated, both in domestic and foreign policy?”

About former PM Giorgi Gakharia

Garibashvili begins his account with February 2021, when he returned as prime minister for a second time after Giorgi Gakharia resigned. He says Georgia faced several serious challenges at once: a political crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic, a shortage of vaccines, an economic downturn, a large budget deficit, rising public debt and a weakening lari.

In his view, Gakharia abandoned the country and the ruling team under these circumstances. Garibashvili’s position on Gakharia echoes the Georgian Dream party’s narrative:

“Gakharia left the country and the team in the middle of an acute crisis, committing an act of unexpected betrayal by resigning. The government stood on the brink of collapse, the ruling party had lost morale, the team was divided, and the party’s approval rating had fallen to 35–37%.”

Garibashvili portrays his return as, essentially, a rescue operation for the government. He says that after taking office as prime minister, he strengthened the team, stabilised the situation, reopened the country and the economy, secured vaccine supplies and lifted restrictions introduced during the pandemic.

The former prime minister stresses that the government abandoned what he calls a “Covid dictatorship” and gave people complete freedom to choose whether to get vaccinated.

“In the shortest possible time, we restored balance, strengthened the team and stabilised the situation. Together with the team, we took bold, decisive, effective and — at the time — risky steps.”

In his view, these measures secured Georgian Dream’s victory in the 2021 local elections. Garibashvili credits himself not only with helping the party clear the 43 per cent threshold and win 47 per cent of the vote, but also with preventing a potential revolutionary scenario after Mikheil Saakashvili returned to Georgia.

“We prevented destabilisation and an attempted revolution involving Saakashvili, put all destructive forces in their place and brought the political crisis to an end.”

Showcasing economic results

A significant part of the letter focuses on economic indicators. Garibashvili claims that Georgia’s economy grew by 30 billion lari (about $11,516,310,000) during his three years as prime minister. He says the economy recorded double-digit growth in 2021 and 2022, putting Georgia first among EU member and candidate countries in terms of growth.

Garibashvili lists the following among his government’s achievements:

cutting the budget deficit from 9 per cent to 2.8 per cent;

reducing public debt from 60 per cent to 38 per cent of GDP;

stabilising the lari exchange rate at between 2.6 and 2.7;

bringing inflation below the target level;

reducing unemployment and poverty to historic lows;

creating tens of thousands of new jobs;

raising pensions and salaries for public-sector workers.

The former prime minister attributes lower medicine prices to the opening of the Turkish pharmaceutical market and the introduction of a reference pricing system for medicines.

EU candidate status and the issue of being “dragged into war” with Russia

Garibashvili also devotes considerable attention to foreign policy. Here again, he echoes Georgian Dream’s rhetoric. He says Georgia faced intense pressure after the war between Russia and Ukraine began, but his government managed to protect the country from the threat of war and destabilisation.

“From the very first days of the war between Russia and Ukraine, despite enormous pressure, we firmly and uncompromisingly defended our country’s national interests, preventing destabilisation and the real threat of war.”

Garibashvili thus repeats one of Georgian Dream’s key political arguments: after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Georgia faced the risk of being dragged into the conflict.

The former prime minister lists his foreign visits and diplomatic initiatives in the letter. These include applying for EU membership, developing strategic relations with China, signing free trade agreements with several countries, mediating between Azerbaijan and Armenia, and hosting a meeting of the three countries’ prime ministers in Tbilisi.

Garibashvili considers Georgia’s achievement of EU candidate status in December 2023 his main foreign policy accomplishment.

“Without bowing to anyone — either inside the country or abroad — and solely through our uncompromising defence of our country’s national interests and the joint efforts of our team, we secured EU candidate status in December 2023.”

The letter says these results came without political subordination to external forces.

Approval ratings and resignation

Garibashvili claims he left office with high levels of public support. According to him, in January 2024, approval of the government’s performance and support for Georgian Dream both reached 60 per cent.

“Thanks to the results we achieved — and, most importantly, thanks to democratic methods — we politically neutralised the entire radical opposition, leaving no one with any grounds for criticism or complaint.”

Garibashvili presents not only his government’s record but also the neutralisation of the opposition as a political achievement. He effectively equates this “democratic success” with the ruling party’s dominance and the opposition’s removal from the political arena.

The letter does not explain why Garibashvili resigned as prime minister at a time when, according to his own account, the government enjoyed high approval, the economy was growing and the opposition had suffered political defeat.

From self-defence to political statements: analysis of former Georgian PM’s “prison” letters

Garibashvili’s eight letters form a coherent political narrative. At first, he sought to protect himself and his family. He later accused the authorities of orchestrating political persecution. He subsequently began raising questions about the government’s actions and several other issues. In his eighth letter, he defends his political legacy and criticises the current government. Political analysts say the latest letter points to political ambitions on Garibashvili’s part.

The first stage — Ivanishvili loyalty and self-preservation

In his first letters, Garibashvili described the pressure against him as the main source of the conflict. He said he did not plan to return to politics, but the authorities demanded that he admit guilt to new corruption charges, fearing a “one per cent risk” that he might return to politics.

He firmly reaffirmed his loyalty to Bidzina Ivanishvili, while holding him personally responsible if anything threatened his family.

“I am not fighting or battling anyone — I am only defending myself and my family!”

Garibashvili took a defensive position, seeking to show that he had not chosen this confrontation and that the authorities had forced him to defend himself.

The second stage — accusing specific individuals

In his subsequent letters, it became clearer who exactly Garibashvili was targeting with his criticism. His focus shifted from Ivanishvili to Prime Minister Kobakhidze and former regional development minister and former State Security Service chief Mamuka Mdinaradze. Garibashvili accused both of them of organising the pressure against him.

By presenting the situation this way, the former prime minister clearly left the door open to reconciliation with Ivanishvili.
